papers.title: BOTH2Hands: Inferring 3D Hands from Both Text Prompts and Body Dynamics
papers.problem_statement: Text-to-motion methods generate body motion only, without rich two-hand motion or hybrid body-plus-text conditions; existing datasets lack finger-level hand annotations, so two-hand motion generation suffers a fundamental data bottleneck.

stated_limitations.text: Text control gives spatial detail but has no temporal alignment with the motion.
stated_limitations.quote: the fine-grained spatial control provided by text descriptions is sufficient but lacks temporal alignment methods

stated_limitations.text: The body is treated as a whole; the separate influence of individual body parts on the hands is not modelled.
stated_limitations.quote: did not take into account how different parts of the body might separately affect the hands

stated_limitations.text: Metrics that capture alignment between hand, body, text and other conditions are missing.
stated_limitations.quote: more suitable metrics that can precisely reflect the alignment between hand, body, text, and other complex conditions should be presented

stated_limitations.text: The method cannot reliably decide whether a two-hand interaction gesture is produced when the wrists come close.
stated_limitations.quote: it remains challenging to determine whether a two-handed interaction gesture is generated when the wrists are close enough

stated_limitations.text: Standard single-condition metrics such as R-precision are insensitive to multi-condition hand generation; improvements look marginal.
stated_limitations.quote: multi-conditioned generation performance may not be adequately reflected by widely used metrics such as R-precision

stated_limitations.text: Dataset ground truth comes from off-the-shelf markerless multi-view capture with measurable error against triangulated manual labels.
stated_limitations.quote: Our annotations show 31.4 mm MPJPE and 25.2 mm PA-MPJPE overall, with hand metrics at 6.51 mm MPJPE and 3.97 mm PA-MPJPE

stated_limitations.text: Data scarcity for two-hand motion generation persists and multimodal annotation is a barrier.
stated_limitations.quote: the fundamental data scarcity for two-hand motion generation remains, while such a novel multi-modal further constitutes barriers to data annotations

failure_modes: Text-conditioned hands lack alignment with body motion, while body-conditioned hands fail to meet prompt requirements (Fig. 6).
Non-latent baselines do poorly on text conditions and latent baselines struggle with body conditions (Sec. 5.1).
Ambiguity between interacting and non-interacting two-hand poses when the wrists are close.
future_work: Temporally align text control with generated motion.
Model how individual body parts relate to hand movements, especially hand-to-hand interaction.
Develop metrics that reflect hand and multi-condition alignment.
Community to improve tracking quality from the released raw images.
restrictive_assumptions: 32-camera RGB dome (some zoomed on hands) at 3840x2160, 59.97 FPS, with three 5500 W fill lights to capture hands.
Ground truth from off-the-shelf multi-view markerless mocap, not markers.
Gestures from a gesture dictionary without manipulated objects; no hand-object interaction.
Generation requires the full body motion sequence as input; offline diffusion.

benchmark_gaps.observation: All methods cluster near the real-data value (0.104-0.115 vs Real 0.109), so the metric cannot separate methods; authors call the improvements marginal.
Ground-truth annotation error 31.4 mm overall and 6.51 mm for hands against triangulated manual 2D labels.

open_problems_listed: Temporal alignment of text control with hand motion.
Per-body-part influence on hands.
Hand-to-hand interaction detection and generation when wrists are close.
Metrics for multi-condition (hand, body, text) alignment.
Data scarcity and annotation cost for two-hand motion with multimodal labels.
Improving tracking quality of the released raw captures.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet generate or evaluate temporally controlled, contact-aware two-hand interaction motion with metrics that reflect hand-specific alignment.

papers.title: DiVa-360: The Dynamic Visual Dataset for Immersive Neural Fields
papers.problem_statement: Dynamic neural fields lag behind 2D video because of long training times and the lack of large-scale, long-duration, 360-degree multi-view real-world datasets; existing datasets are room-scale, human-only, forward-facing or under 15 seconds.

stated_limitations.text: Evaluation covers images only; audio and text are not evaluated.
stated_limitations.quote: our current metrics and evaluation are limited to images

stated_limitations.text: The capture system is limited to table-scale scenes.
stated_limitations.quote: BRICS cannot capture scenes larger than table-scale

stated_limitations.text: Slow training of state-of-the-art methods prevents more baselines or longer-video metrics.
stated_limitations.quote: Due to the training speed of the existing state-of-the-art methods, we cannot include more baselines or metrics for longer videos.

stated_limitations.text: Radiance fields cannot handle reflections from the glass panel, so 12 views are dropped.
stated_limitations.quote: current neural radiance fields cannot handle reflections from the glass panel on which we place the objects for 12 views in our data

stated_limitations.text: Dynamic methods appear unable to exploit high-resolution images.
stated_limitations.quote: we suspect that current dynamic methods cannot efficiently utilize spatial information in high-resolution images as they are biased toward motion

stated_limitations.text: Foreground segmentation misses small, transparent, highly reflective or white objects.
stated_limitations.quote: the method misses sections where the object is very small

stated_limitations.text: Text descriptions come from one annotator; bias acknowledged.
stated_limitations.quote: To prevent the bias of labeling, we plan to have more people label text descriptions in the future.

failure_modes: MixVoxels struggles with complex dynamic parts such as hands, giving blurry, noisy reconstructions and floaters.
K-Planes fails on static or slow-moving parts and produces background floaters.
Per-frame I-NGP is temporally inconsistent on static parts.
All methods score lower on hand-object interaction sequences than object-only ones because of hand occlusion and complex hand motion (PSNR gap up to 2.73 dB).
All baselines fail on transparent, finely moving objects (hourglass); one codebase cannot handle the plasma ball scene.
future_work: Metrics for audio and text modalities.
Expand capture to volumes larger than table-scale.
More long sequences and baselines.
Attach depth and infrared cameras to the panels.
More annotators for text descriptions; extend to multimodal NeRFs.
restrictive_assumptions: 53 synchronized RGB cameras in a 360-degree enclosure.
Table-scale scenes only, objects centred in the capture volume.
Per-scene optimization over 5-second chunks; over 500 GPU-days for the benchmark.
Segmentation relies on objects being near the centre of the rig.

benchmark_gaps.observation: PF I-NGP 28.31 dB, MixVoxels 27.68 dB, K-Planes 26.39 dB; training 48-58 s per frame.
Interaction sequences lower than object sequences by 2.73 dB (PF I-NGP), 1.98 dB (MixVoxels), 0.44 dB (K-Planes).
Training at higher resolution does not improve MixVoxels or K-Planes (K-Planes 25.38 dB at 1160x550 vs 26.03 dB at 464x220).

open_problems_listed: Training and rendering speed of dynamic neural fields.
Hardware requirements.
Imbalanced capacity between static and dynamic components.
Use of temporal information.
Use of spatial (high-resolution) information.
Long-duration (minutes to hours) dynamic scene capture.
Reflections and transparent or thin objects.
Modelling complex hand dynamics and hand occlusion in hand-object interaction.
Capture beyond table scale.
Evaluation beyond images (audio, text).
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet reconstruct long-duration hand-object interaction scenes with dynamic neural fields that are fast, temporally consistent, and accurate on hands and fine detail.

papers.title: EgoExoLearn: A Dataset for Bridging Asynchronous Ego- and Exo-centric View of Procedural Activities in Real World
papers.problem_statement: AI agents need demonstrations from a congruent viewpoint and environment; existing ego-exo datasets are time-synchronized in the same environment, and no dataset supports bridging asynchronous procedural activities across ego and exo views.

stated_limitations.text: Current models are limited at associating activities across views.
stated_limitations.quote: Findings from this benchmark underline the limitation of current models in associating activities across ego and exo views

stated_limitations.text: Adding exocentric reference gives only marginal gains in skill assessment.
stated_limitations.quote: the marginal improvement observed with the inclusion of the exocentric reference suggests that current models may still struggle to fully bridge asynchronous activities

stated_limitations.text: No paired training data is provided for association; unpaired modelling left open.
stated_limitations.quote: we do not provide such pairs for the training set and leave the modeling of cross-view association on unpaired samples to be further explored

stated_limitations.text: Zero-shot recognition is worse on egocentric than exocentric video.
stated_limitations.quote: This result indicates the limitation in cross-view action understanding of the current method.

stated_limitations.text: Egocentric gaze glasses recorded variable frame rates due to overheating, requiring resampling to 25 fps.
stated_limitations.quote: Pupil Invisible devices that sometimes capture footage at variable frame rates due to issues like overheating

failure_modes: Models trained on a single view struggle with cross-view association and show a large gap when tested on the other view.
Zero-shot cross-view evaluation gives the lowest anticipation and planning performance.
Planning with more steps remains weak (edit distances around 0.75-0.85).
future_work: Better leverage gaze and hand-associated annotations.
Model cross-view association from unpaired samples.
Improve bridging of asynchronous ego-exo activities across all benchmarks.
restrictive_assumptions: Gaze cue requires eye-tracking glasses worn by the participant.
Videos only; no 3D pose or object annotations used in the benchmarks.
Demonstration videos are edited and shorter than the egocentric executions.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best co-trained model with gaze reaches 55.3 (Ego2Exo) and 51.1 (Exo2Ego); zero-shot models 21.7-33.3 vs random 13-14.
Cross-view results mostly 25-56; zero-shot transfer across views is the lowest.
Adding exo reference yields only marginal gains (about 79-84%).

open_problems_listed: Cross-view association of asynchronous ego and exo activities.
Cross-view association from unpaired training samples.
Cross-view action anticipation and planning across different environments.
Cross-view referenced skill assessment.
Cross-view referenced video captioning.
Cross-view action segmentation.
Zero-shot cross-view action recognition (ego worse than exo).
How to leverage gaze and hand-associated annotations.
Length mismatch between edited demonstrations and full egocentric executions.
Sim-to-real generalization; combined multiview datasets of inferior quality or scale (intro).
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet transfer procedural knowledge from an exocentric demonstration to an egocentric execution recorded elsewhere and at another time.

papers.title: FreeMan: Towards Benchmarking 3D Human Pose Estimation under Real-World Conditions
papers.problem_statement: 3D pose datasets are mostly captured in labs with fixed cameras, static lighting and uniform backgrounds, so models degrade in real scenes; datasets also have limited actions and body scales and rely on costly manual annotation.

stated_limitations.text: Error-pose detection depends on image generation models and prompt tuning.
stated_limitations.quote: Prompts to generation model require careful tuning for high quality and accuracy of error pose detection can be limited by human image generation models.

stated_limitations.text: Annotations are 17 COCO body keypoints, not whole body.
stated_limitations.quote: Currently, our pose annotations are in the form of 17 keypoints following the COCO format.

stated_limitations.text: The dataset size is limited and many real-world conditions remain unexplored.
stated_limitations.quote: the real world encompasses a multitude of variables, and there are additional conditions that can be further explored. Despite the limited size of FreeMan

stated_limitations.text: Aligning and annotating data from movable cameras is unsolved.
stated_limitations.quote: how to effectively align data from different cameras and perform efficient annotation remains an open issue

stated_limitations.text: Chessboard calibration alone is not accurate enough and needs dense-matching refinement.
stated_limitations.quote: calibration with coarse matching points on chessboard is not accurate enough

failure_modes: A VoxelPose model trained on Human3.6M fails to locate humans on FreeMan (zero AP below 100 mm).
2D pose detectors are inaccurate under heavy occlusion, requiring a filter and manual correction.
Hands and feet blur at high speed; HumanNeRF reconstruction is poor in some scenes.
future_work: Extend annotations to whole-body keypoints.
Apply dynamic 3D Gaussian splatting to FreeMan.
Explore further real-world conditions.
restrictive_assumptions: 8 synchronized smartphone views with chessboard calibration per session.
Ground truth from triangulated 2D detector keypoints (HRNet) plus smoothing, not marker mocap.
Body keypoints only (17 COCO joints), no hands or objects.
Synchronization error under one frame (33 ms at 30 FPS).

benchmark_gaps.observation: 79.22 mm on FreeMan vs 53.4 mm on Human3.6M.
Zero AP below 100 mm; 103.02 mm even with ground-truth root.
Ranges from 30.11 dB down to 23.86 dB across 10 scenes.

open_problems_listed: Insufficient scene diversity in existing datasets (lighting, background).
Limited actions and body scales from fixed cameras.
Restricted scalability of manual annotation.
Aligning and annotating data from movable cameras.
Whole-body keypoint annotation.
Human rendering under natural lighting; dynamic 3D Gaussian splatting.
Further real-world variables beyond those captured.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet produce 3D human pose estimators and annotation pipelines that generalize from lab capture to varied real-world scenes and moving cameras.

papers.title: HOI-M^3: Capture Multiple Humans and Objects Interaction within Contextual Environment
papers.problem_statement: Capturing multiple humans and objects is hard due to severe occlusion: it needs dense cameras and object IMUs, and even then accurate capture needs tedious stages and manual correction, so multi-human multi-object data is scarce.

stated_limitations.text: Indoor only due to hardware cost; outdoor and in-the-wild extension is non-trivial.
stated_limitations.quote: due to hardware cost constraints, HOI-M3 is currently limited to indoor settings

stated_limitations.text: Only five scenes because of human effort.
stated_limitations.quote: building such a dataset involves significant human resources; thus, HOI-M3 only covers 5 common scenes

stated_limitations.text: Fixed illumination and few backgrounds limit generalization.
stated_limitations.quote: our dataset was collected under fixed illumination conditions with few background variations, limiting its generalization ability to other environments

stated_limitations.text: No tracking-specific ground truth; tracking evaluation is qualitative.
stated_limitations.quote: we lack ground truth specific to tracking, so our evaluations are qualitative in nature

stated_limitations.text: IMU drift and calibration errors degrade object tracking over time.
stated_limitations.quote: the drift error of IMUs tends to reduce confidence as the duration of use extends

stated_limitations.text: No strong object keypoint detectors; masks are the main object evidence.
stated_limitations.quote: Due to the lack of powerful object keypoint detection tools, human and object masks are the strongest evidence for object tracking

stated_limitations.text: Accurate capture is still out of reach even with dense multimodal input.
stated_limitations.quote: even based on such dense and multi-modal input, an accurate capture method remains far-reaching

failure_modes: Without IMU initialization, object rotation cannot be recovered from masks.
Extremely occluded cases need manual correction.
Single-HOI methods with weak-perspective cameras give inaccurate root depth and need a preset object count.
Monocular multi-HOI capture remains qualitatively poor despite better numbers.
future_work: Extend capture to outdoor and in-the-wild settings.
Benchmarks for multi-person pose and shape under object occlusion.
Monocular and multi-view multiple HOI capture.
Multiple human motion generation and multiple interaction generation.
restrictive_assumptions: 42 cinema cameras in a 7.8 m dome plus IMUs embedded in each pre-scanned object.
Known object templates (rigid, pre-scanned).
Manual sync by a controlled jump and manual IMU-camera offset calibration.
Indoor, fixed illumination, white backdrops; offline optimization.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Proposed baseline reaches only 5.9% PCKabs (3.3% matched) vs 68.5% PCKrel; object V2V 297.8 and Chamfer 235.0.
All tested methods (HMR, SPIN, HybrIK, PARE, CLIFF) have MPJPE of 309-332 mm.
Joint generation has 9.265% penetration vs 1.452% for people alone.

open_problems_listed: Multi-person pose and shape estimation under object occlusion.
Monocular multiple HOI capture (limited progress to date).
Multi-view multiple HOI capture.
Multiple human motion generation.
Multiple interaction generation.
Outdoor and in-the-wild capture.
Scene and illumination diversity.
Accurate capture without dense cameras, IMUs and manual correction.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet capture several humans manipulating several objects accurately in 3D without dense camera domes, object-mounted IMUs and manual correction.

papers.title: MMVP: A Multimodal MoCap Dataset with Vision and Pressure Sensors
papers.problem_statement: Foot-contact annotations from visual distance thresholding are inaccurate, and pressure datasets cover only slow, small-range motion; no vision-pressure dataset exists with large-range fast motion and dense accurate contact.

stated_limitations.text: Designed for static viewpoints; moving cameras remain hard.
stated_limitations.quote: Our method is mainly designed for static viewpoints, so it remains challenging to handle moving camera configurations.

stated_limitations.text: Scenes are homogeneous, preventing scene generalization.
stated_limitations.quote: The existing MMVP has relatively homogeneous scenes, making it difficult for current visual networks to achieve scene generalization on this dataset.

stated_limitations.text: Insole and camera cannot be synchronized automatically.
stated_limitations.quote: Due to the hardware limitation, we cannot synchronize the two streams of signals automatically, so we do manual synchronization before usage.

stated_limitations.text: Single-frame contact perception is hard.
stated_limitations.quote: It is challenging to perceive the foot contact solely based on a single-frame image.

stated_limitations.text: Visual threshold contact labels inherit pose, shape and scene-scan errors.
stated_limitations.quote: the accuracy is inevitably affected by the pose estimation error, shape estimation error, and even scene scanning error

failure_modes: Monocular RGB methods (CLIFF, TRACE) drift in depth during side-stepping, jumping and throwing.
Contact estimators trained on threshold labels (BSTRO, DECO) predict contact almost always, giving high recall but low precision.
Prior monocular mesh recovery suffers translation drift, foot sliding and foot-plane penetration in fast large-range motion.
future_work: Collect outdoor scenes to expand the dataset.
Learn human body dynamics solely from pressure sequences.
restrictive_assumptions: Single static Azure Kinect RGB-D camera at 30 Hz.
Subjects wear pressure insoles (242 sensors each).
Manual synchronization of pressure and video.
Single person on a ground plane; ground estimated by ZoeDepth at test time.
Mostly teenage subjects in homogeneous indoor scenes.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best method reaches only 0.532 F1 and 0.522 IoU.
Best MPJPE 83.0 mm; trajectory error 129.3 mm vs 211.4-679.7 mm for CLIFF, TRACE and SMPLer-X.

open_problems_listed: Accurate dense contact annotation without visual thresholding errors.
Vision-pressure data for large-range fast motion.
Handling moving cameras.
Scene generalization beyond homogeneous scenes.
Learning dynamics from pressure alone.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet estimate accurate dense contact and drift-free global motion from monocular video under fast motion and moving cameras.

papers.title: OAKINK2: A Dataset of Bimanual Hands-Object Manipulation in Complex Task Completion
papers.problem_statement: Methods lack human-level understanding of object manipulation for complex tasks; prior OakInk lacks demonstrations fulfilling affordances and complex multi-affordance tasks.

stated_limitations.text: Marker mocap fails under extreme occlusion and needs manual cleaning.
stated_limitations.quote: in extreme cases of occlusion, the system may fail to detect and record some markers; ghost markers may be included due to unwanted environmental reflections

stated_limitations.text: Close markers get mislabelled or merged.
stated_limitations.quote: when two or more markers come into close proximity, the system may incorrectly assign their labels or falsely identify them as a single marker

stated_limitations.text: No framework for end-to-end text-to-motion complex task completion; task decomposed into stages.
stated_limitations.quote: there is currently no adequate framework to address this problem

stated_limitations.text: LLM planner fails on complex tasks with many primitives.
stated_limitations.quote: the LLM struggles to accurately comprehend the relationships and dependencies between objects' affordances and the corresponding Primitives

failure_modes: LLM primitive planning success is 36% overall, 44% for up to 3 primitives, 20% for 3-5, and 0% beyond 5.
Failed plans add superfluous primitives that block execution.
Marker loss under occlusion, ghost markers and label swaps when markers are close.
future_work: Large-scale language-manipulation pretraining for vision-language-action models.
End-to-end text-to-manipulation generation.
Retarget primitive demonstrations to heterogeneous hands and robot platforms.
Integrate scenarios into simulation environments for embodied learning.
restrictive_assumptions: 12 OptiTrack cameras with reflective markers on upper body, both hands and objects.
Known object geometry; TaMF assumes object trajectories given or retrieved from demonstrations by an oracle.
4 RGB views (1 egocentric, 3 allocentric); 9 subjects, 75 objects.
Manual cleaning of mocap data by three annotators.

benchmark_gaps.observation: 13.08-17.56 mm; no world-space result reported for monocular methods.
POEM 9.17 mm, keypoint-based fit 19.30 mm.
36% overall; 0% for tasks with more than 5 primitives.

open_problems_listed: End-to-end text-to-manipulation generation for complex tasks.
Planning long-horizon tasks with many dependent primitives.
Vision-language-action pretraining on manipulation data.
Retargeting demonstrations to other embodiments.
Transfer to simulation for embodied learning.
Robust capture under marker occlusion without manual cleaning.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet plan and generate long-horizon bimanual manipulation from language, nor capture it without markers and manual cleaning.

papers.title: RELI11D: A Comprehensive Multimodal Human Motion Dataset and Method
papers.problem_statement: RGB, LiDAR or IMU alone, or in combination, may be inadequate for complex fast motion; no dataset combines RGB, LiDAR, event and IMU modalities.

stated_limitations.text: Existing methods cannot handle rapid complex motion that needs precise location.
stated_limitations.quote: Most of these methods cannot deal with rapid, coherent, and complex movements that require precise location.

stated_limitations.text: All tested methods perform poorly, even multi-dataset ones.
stated_limitations.quote: We find that all the methods perform poorly on the RELI11D dataset, even for methods trained on multiple datasets.

stated_limitations.text: Monocular methods fail on 3D global motion.
stated_limitations.quote: despite the monocular camera methods can match local motions in 2D RGB well, they do not excel at 3D global motions

stated_limitations.text: RGB-D has limited range; IMUs must be worn and drift.
stated_limitations.quote: RGBD sensors compensate for the absence of depth information, but their sensing range is limited.

stated_limitations.text: IMU drift over long captures forces optimization for labels.
stated_limitations.quote: As IMUs suffer severe drifting for long-period capturing

failure_modes: RGB methods do not model limbs well in rapid taekwondo motion.
RGB methods show artifacts and penetration in table tennis where global position matters.
Event-only input gives the worst results (MPJPE 107.78 mm in LEIR).
restrictive_assumptions: Ground truth requires a 17-IMU Xsens suit, LiDAR, and a laser scan of each scene.
Body shape from handheld scanning.
Sync via a jump at sequence start.
LEIR needs LiDAR, event and RGB sensors.

benchmark_gaps.observation: RGB methods 171.97-249.34 mm; FusionPose (RGB+LiDAR) 136.15 mm.
GLAMR and TRACE: G-MPJPE 489-495 mm, T-Error 582-590 mm; LEIR 115.36 / 146.13 mm.

open_problems_listed: Capturing rapid, complex motions with precise global localization.
Global 3D motion from monocular RGB.
Fusing heterogeneous sensors (RGB, LiDAR, event, IMU).
Sensor limits: RGB light-sensitive and no depth; RGB-D short range; LiDAR sparse and low frame rate; IMU worn and drifting; event no appearance.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet estimate fast, complex human motion with accurate global position from a single affordable sensor.

papers.title: Scaling Up Dynamic Human-Scene Interaction Modeling
papers.problem_statement: HSI modeling is hindered by scarce high-quality data: mocap datasets lack diverse immersive HSI, RGB-D datasets have lower pose and object tracking quality, and synthetic datasets miss dynamic 3D contacts and object tracking.

stated_limitations.text: The motion generator cannot produce human-object interactions outside the training distribution; unfamiliar actions yield unrealistic interactions or object intersections.
stated_limitations.quote: A notable limitation of our method is its inability to generate human-object interaction behaviors beyond those in the training set.

stated_limitations.text: Example given: climbing off a table is not generated realistically.
stated_limitations.quote: it struggles to create realistic motions for unfamiliar actions like climbing off a table, leading to potentially unrealistic interactions or object intersections.

stated_limitations.text: In the introduction the authors say RGB-D recorded datasets scale better but give lower-quality human pose and object tracking than mocap.
stated_limitations.quote: Scalable datasets recorded via RGBD videos offer broader utility but are impeded by lower quality in human pose and object tracking.

failure_modes: Generation of actions not present in TRUMANS (e.g. climbing off a table) produces unrealistic motion and object intersections
Removing the progress indicator condition makes the object-interaction generator fail (ablation discriminator success rate 1.000, FID 2.104)
Without data augmentation, penetration increases in the static setting
future_work: None stated explicitly beyond positioning TRUMANS as a resource for pose and contact estimation research
restrictive_assumptions: Optical VICON mocap with markers on all movable objects in a dedicated capture area
Physical placeholders manually aligned to virtual 3D-FRONT/BlenderKit scenes; RGB-D video, masks and egocentric views are synthetic renderings, not real camera footage
Only 7 actors; actors trained on placeholders and prompted with actions from a predefined pool
Generator needs scene occupancy and frame-wise action labels as input
Objects represented by known watertight meshes and URDF for articulated objects

benchmark_gaps.observation: On PROX the method's discriminator success rate is 0.903, the same as Wang et al.; contact 0.723 vs 0.992 on TRUMANS, showing much weaker results on real scanned scenes
GRAB-trained models show high penetration (e.g. 34.41 for the method, 44.09 GOAL), which the paper attributes to GRAB's limitation for scene-adherent HOI
Adding TRUMANS at 1:1 lowers DECO recall from 0.5232 to 0.4806 and F1 from 0.5115 to 0.4972, despite lower geodesic error

open_problems_listed: High-quality HSI datasets are scarce; prior datasets constrained in scalability and data quality
Mocap datasets lack diverse and immersive HSI
RGB-D recorded datasets have lower-quality human pose and object tracking
Synthetic datasets fail to capture dynamic 3D contacts and object tracking
Generating HOI behaviours beyond the training set remains unsolved
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet capture scalable, real-sensor human-object interaction data with mocap-level pose, object tracking and contact quality, nor generate interactions beyond the training distribution.

papers.title: TACO: Benchmarking Generalizable Bimanual Tool-ACtion-Object Understanding
papers.problem_statement: Existing hand-object methods and datasets mostly handle a single hand and object; the closest bimanual tool-object dataset covers only 12 objects and under 20 triplets, so generalizable bimanual tool-action-object understanding lacks data support.

stated_limitations.text: TACO does not include articulated objects.
stated_limitations.quote: Firstly, TACO currently does not cover articulated objects.

stated_limitations.text: Lacks scene diversity, which the authors note is crucial for understanding manipulation.
stated_limitations.quote: it lacks scene diversities that are also crucial for understanding human manipulations.

stated_limitations.text: Marker removal uses generative inpainting, so true object appearance cannot be perfectly recovered.
stated_limitations.quote: our solution to marker removal is an application of generative models, hence the original object appearances cannot be recovered perfectly.

stated_limitations.text: Existing dual-hand 2D keypoint approaches can fail under severe occlusion or when the hands are far apart, requiring a custom per-hand detection pipeline.
stated_limitations.quote: directly applying existing dual-hand approaches [19, 37, 27] could fail when severe occlusion occurs or two hands are far apart.

stated_limitations.text: Markers on objects widen the appearance gap to in-the-wild objects; a tracker could learn to track markers instead of the object.
stated_limitations.quote: One direct defect is that an object pose tracking network could simply track markers rather than learn to track the target object.

failure_modes: Action recognition accuracy drops sharply on novel tool-action-object triplets and novel tool categories (S3, S4)
Motion forecasting errors rise for the right hand and the tool under novel geometries or triplets; generative forecasters (InterVAE, MDM) have far larger errors than predictive ones
Grasp synthesis yields higher collision ratios and FID, and worse contact and penetration on unseen tool geometries; failures on complex and slender geometries
Hand pose estimators trained on one of TACO or DexYCB degrade strongly when tested on the other
future_work: Improving the accuracy of generative methods for hand-object motion forecasting
Universal generalization strategies for understanding and creating hand-object interactions
Improving physical feasibility and naturalness of grasp synthesis on complex and slender geometries
restrictive_assumptions: 12 synchronized industrial cameras plus a NOKOV optical mocap system with 6 IR cameras; four markers on each object
Rigid objects only, each pre-scanned with an industrial 3D scanner (up to 100K faces)
Egocentric camera is a helmet-mounted RealSense L515 tracked by mocap
Lab capture with limited scene diversity
Forecasting benchmark assumes known object point clouds and past poses; grasp synthesis assumes known meshes of both objects and the left hand

benchmark_gaps.observation: AIM 39.33% and CACNF 44.00% on S4 versus 83.08% and 86.15% on S1

benchmark_gaps.metric: Forecasting MPJPE (right hand) and tool rotation error
benchmark_gaps.observation: Generative baselines reach 54.9-70.5 mm right-hand MPJPE and 52.8-88.2 deg tool rotation error; best predictive models still 28.8-36.6 mm
ContactGen collision ratio rises from 10.40 to 17.56 and HALO-VAE from 2.39 to 11.11 on unseen geometries
CMR trained on DexYCB gives 39.54 mm MPJPE on TACO; trained on TACO gives 76.20 mm on DexYCB

open_problems_listed: Generalizing bimanual HOI understanding to novel object geometries, categories and unseen tool-action-object triplets
Compositional action recognition under novel interaction contexts
Forecasting fast, complex hand-object motion, especially for the dominant hand and tool
Synthesizing physically plausible, cooperative grasps in multi-object scenarios for unseen geometries
Articulated objects not covered
Scene diversity lacking
Realistic marker-free object appearance in mocap-annotated data
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet generalize bimanual tool-object perception, forecasting and grasp synthesis to unseen tool geometries and novel action compositions, nor capture marker-free ground truth for diverse scenes and articulated objects.

papers.title: EgoPressure: A Dataset for Hand Pressure and Pose Estimation in Egocentric Vision
papers.problem_statement: Estimating touch contact and pressure from egocentric views is hard because no dataset provides both accurate hand poses on contacting surfaces and detailed pressure annotations; gloves and tactile sensors obstruct natural touch.

stated_limitations.text: Pressure sensing is confined to flat surfaces; arbitrary object surfaces would need hand instrumentation that hinders natural interaction and adds visible artifacts.
stated_limitations.quote: Our current data capture is confined to sensing pressure on flat surfaces.

stated_limitations.text: Data captured only indoors; green screen overlays are used for background replacement to improve generalization.
stated_limitations.quote: Second, the current dataset was only captured in an indoor setting.

stated_limitations.text: Only single-hand interactions are captured; bimanual use is left as an extension.
stated_limitations.quote: Finally, the current setup only considers single-hand interactions. Incorporating scenarios involving the use of both hands would be a natural extension of our work.

stated_limitations.text: Instrumenting objects for pressure remains open, with recent progress mostly limited to basic contact detection.
stated_limitations.quote: Instrumenting objects for pressure sensing remains an ongoing research area, with recent advancements primarily in basic contact detection [4].

stated_limitations.text: HaMeR single-image predictions look plausible from the top but reveal inaccuracies and scale ambiguity from side views.
stated_limitations.quote: although hand poses from HaMeR [67] appear plausible from a top view, side views expose inaccuracies and scale ambiguities.

failure_modes: Pressure estimation degrades strongly on exocentric camera views unseen during training
Single-image hand pose estimates (HaMeR) carry depth/scale ambiguity, limiting pressure estimation compared with ground-truth poses
Image-plane pressure prediction is ambiguous about where pressure acts in 3D
future_work: Extend the dataset to include objects so pressure can be estimated on more complex geometries
Bimanual pressure scenarios
Advancing hand pose and pressure map estimation jointly
restrictive_assumptions: Seven static calibrated Azure Kinect RGB-D cameras plus one head-mounted camera for annotation
Pressure ground truth only from a flat Sensel Morph touchpad (240 x 169.5 mm)
Head-camera pose from active IR markers around the pad
Per-participant MANO shape calibration sequence
Single hand at a time, lab setting with green screen, black hand stockings up to wrist
Scripted gestures (touch, press, drag, pinch) rather than object manipulation

benchmark_gaps.observation: PressureVisionNet drops to 36.82% contact IoU and 25.05% volumetric IoU, versus 62.11% / 44.73% on seen views; GT pose only raises it to 43.04%
Egocentric contact IoU is 55.73% (RGB only), 58.80% even with ground-truth pose
Best contact IoU 43.04%; volumetric IoU 31.57%, below the HaMeR-pose baseline's 35.40%

open_problems_listed: Measuring pressure while interacting with general (non-flat) objects without instrumenting hands
Instrumenting objects for pressure sensing
Generalizing beyond indoor capture settings to real-world environments
Bimanual pressure interactions
Joint high-accuracy hand pose and pressure estimation from egocentric RGB
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet obtain or estimate hand contact pressure during natural manipulation of arbitrary 3D objects, especially with both hands, from egocentric cameras.

papers.title: GigaHands: A Massive Annotated Dataset of Bimanual Hand Activities
papers.problem_statement: Large models of bimanual activity cannot be built because datasets lack scale, coverage and detailed annotation; in-the-wild data is sparse, hard to calibrate and noisy, while studio and marker setups limit diversity and natural interaction.

stated_limitations.text: The studio confines capture to a limited space, so motions needing larger environments are hard to capture.
stated_limitations.quote: The studio setting confines data collection to a limited space, making it challenging to accurately capture motions that require larger environments.

stated_limitations.text: Fully automatic tracking of articulated and non-rigid objects is not solved.
stated_limitations.quote: While we can track rigid objects and object parts, fully automatic tracking of articulated and non-rigid objects remains challenging.

stated_limitations.text: Object tracking loses track under fast motion or severe occlusion during manipulation, accumulating errors.
stated_limitations.quote: for sequences with fast motion or where the object is severely occluded due to manipulation, the pose might lose track and accumulate errors.

stated_limitations.text: Off-the-shelf hand and object pose estimators did not work well enough; HaMeR meshes lack accurate depth.
stated_limitations.quote: Since no existing method for object pose estimation worked well [25], we decided to build our own robust method that exploits our dense multi-view setting.

stated_limitations.text: Hand-object motion forecasting remains challenging due to rapid, complex motion patterns.
stated_limitations.quote: However, hand-object motion forecasting still remains a challenging task.

failure_modes: Object pose tracking drifts with fast motion or severe occlusion (mask coverage 91.1% first frame vs 78.5% over sequence)
RGB-only capture without depth makes pose estimation hard; density-field initialization can fail and fall back to random offsets
Symmetric objects need appearance-based rotation initialization
12 of 51 views removed for radiance-field reconstruction due to lighting issues
LLM-generated instructions contain inconsistencies or hallucinations requiring manual annotation
future_work: Explore how the dataset's scale and diversity can enhance robotic manipulation and human-computer interaction
More effective strategies for hand-object motion forecasting
Automatic tracking of articulated and non-rigid objects
restrictive_assumptions: Dense 51-camera RGB studio cube with LED lighting and a glass table, 1280x720 at 30 fps
Pre-scanned or single-view-generated template meshes needed for object 6DoF tracking
Subjects instructed to keep both hands inside the capture area; detector takes the two most confident hand boxes
Tabletop activities only, no real-world context
Rigid objects for pose; non-rigid objects only get segmentation masks

benchmark_gaps.observation: Coarse pose initialization achieves 45.2% mask coverage; sequence refinement 78.5%, below 91.1% on the first frame

benchmark_gaps.metric: Forecasting MPJPE right/left, object translation and rotation error
benchmark_gaps.observation: GigaHands-trained MDM: 69.3/62.3 mm hand MPJPE, 47.6 mm translation, 67.5 deg rotation; TACO 71.7/58.4, 52.8, 73.2
27.2% versus a ground-truth upper bound of 77.4%

open_problems_listed: Capturing motions that require larger environments than a studio
Fully automatic tracking of articulated and non-rigid objects
Using large hand datasets to improve robotic manipulation and HCI
Hand-object motion forecasting with fast, complex motion
In-the-wild data is sparse, hard to calibrate and noisy, limiting 3D accuracy especially for objects
Marker-based tracking inhibits natural interaction
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet automatically track articulated or non-rigid objects, or rigid objects under fast motion and heavy hand occlusion, without a dense multi-camera studio.

papers.title: HOT3D: Hand and Object Tracking in 3D from Egocentric Multi-View Videos
papers.problem_statement: The accuracy and speed of current hand-object interaction methods are insufficient for AR/VR, skill transfer and robotics, and existing datasets rarely offer accurate 3D hand and object poses from real multi-view egocentric headsets.

stated_limitations.text: No dedicated limitations section; the paper states some annotations are missing or of lower quality, with 1.16M of 1.5M frames fully annotated and passing visual inspection.
stated_limitations.quote: Annotations in some frames may be missing or be of a lower quality.

stated_limitations.text: Motivating gap: existing methods are not accurate or fast enough to support target applications.
stated_limitations.quote: However, the accuracy and speed of existing methods for understanding hand-object interaction are not sufficient to reliably support such applications.

stated_limitations.text: Hand tracker overfits to the camera configuration seen at training, so two-view mode degrades across headsets.
stated_limitations.quote: the datasets are recorded with different headsets (Quest 2 vs. Quest 3) and the tracker overfits to the camera configuration seen at training.

stated_limitations.text: Monocular depth lifting errors lie mostly along the optical axis, caused by inaccurate depth predictions.
stated_limitations.quote: The 3D localization error of MonoDepth is primarily along the optical axis and therefore caused by inaccurate depth predictions.

stated_limitations.text: Ground-truth poses for dynamic onboarding sequences are given only for the first frame, reflecting that poses are hard to obtain when objects are hand-manipulated.
stated_limitations.quote: poses can be easily obtained by SfM [59] in the static setup, but are challenging to obtain in the dynamic setup.

failure_modes: Single-view hand tracking trained without hand-object data degrades on HOT3D (24.2 mm MKPE vs 13.6 mm in-domain)
Training on one headset's camera layout and testing on another makes two-view tracking worse than single-view
EgoHOS in-hand segmentation drops sharply on Quest 3 monochrome images due to domain gap
Single-view object pose fails on heavily occluded objects
Monocular-depth lifting has large depth-axis errors
future_work: Public challenges (BOP 2024, hand tracking challenge) to accelerate egocentric vision research
Encouraged: model-free (CAD-free) object tracking via onboarding sequences, 3D object reconstruction, and use of eye gaze for intent prediction or foveated sensing
restrictive_assumptions: Ground truth from OptiTrack marker mocap: 19 markers per hand, about 10 per object, objects with distinct marker constellations
33 rigid objects with in-house scanned meshes and PBR materials
Single capture lab with scenario furniture (randomized lighting and decor)
Benchmarks provide ground-truth hand shape and 2D boxes (hand tracking), ground-truth object masks (pose estimation, lifting)
Multi-view headsets (Aria, Quest 3) with known calibration; MonoDepth needs SLAM points

benchmark_gaps.observation: 25.2% single-view and 33.8% multi-view, even with ground-truth masks
28.9% single-view, 36.9% multi-view
EgoHOS 33.1% (either hand) and 13.5-14.4% for left/right; best MRCNN-DA 54.7%
StereoMatch 42.6%, MonoDepth 11.1%
UmeTrack-trained tracker: 24.2 mm single-view, 25.6 mm two-view; 10.9 mm only after joint training

open_problems_listed: Accuracy and speed of hand-object interaction understanding insufficient for AR/VR and robotics applications
Model-free (CAD-free) object tracking from few-shot onboarding
Obtaining object poses during dynamic hand manipulation
Cross-headset generalization of multi-view hand trackers
Leveraging eye gaze for intent prediction and foveated sensing
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet estimate 6DoF poses of hand-held objects accurately from egocentric views (about one third recall at 5 cm, 5 deg even multi-view with ground-truth masks).

papers.title: TASTE-Rob: Advancing Video Generation of Task-Oriented Hand-Object Interaction for Generalizable Robotic Manipulation
papers.problem_statement: Video diffusion models struggle to generate task-oriented hand-object interaction videos; Ego4D has inconsistent viewpoints and clip-instruction misalignment, reducing video quality for imitation learning demonstrations.

stated_limitations.text: Generation quality drops when objects undergo large transformations such as rotation or opening.
stated_limitations.quote: However, the generation quality degrades when objects undergo significant transformations, such as rotation and opening.

stated_limitations.text: Fine-tuned video model produces unnatural grip changes during manipulation, which is critical for imitation learning.
stated_limitations.quote: it exhibits inconsistencies in hand poses, with the grip changing unnaturally during manipulation.

stated_limitations.text: Imitation learning robots need nearly identical environments to the demonstration, limiting generalization.
stated_limitations.quote: require a nearly identical environment in the recorded video, limiting their generalization to novel scenes

stated_limitations.text: Pose refinement has a trade-off: more denoising improves pose consistency but degrades spatial awareness.
stated_limitations.quote: As [m] increases, we observe improved pose consistency but degraded spatial awareness.

failure_modes: Objects undergoing rotation or opening (articulation) degrade generation quality
Grasp pose temporally inconsistent without refinement (GTCE 67.8 percent before refinement)
General-purpose video diffusion models fail to perform manipulation tasks
Videos generated from Ego4D fine-tuning are too low quality to extract reasonable hand poses
future_work: Address degradation for objects undergoing significant transformations such as rotation and opening
restrictive_assumptions: Fixed, static egocentric camera viewpoint for every clip
Each clip under 8 s with exactly one action aligned to the instruction
All collectors right-handed
Hand poses extracted with HaMeR (2D/monocular estimation)
Robot evaluation only in Mujoco simulation with the Im2Flow2Act policy

benchmark_gaps.metric: Grasp Type Classification Error / Hand Movement Direction Accuracy
benchmark_gaps.observation: Coarse model GTCE 67.8% and HMDA 26.4 deg; refined model still 9.7% and 11.3 deg
84% with coarse videos, 96% with refined videos; real-robot results not reported

open_problems_listed: Ego-centric HOI datasets have inconsistent viewpoints and clip-instruction misalignment
General video diffusion models cannot generate task-accurate HOI videos
Temporally consistent grasp poses in generated HOI videos
Handling objects with large transformations (rotation, articulation)
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet generate hand-object videos with temporally stable, physically consistent grasps for objects that rotate or articulate.

papers.title: Reconstructing In-the-Wild Open-Vocabulary Human-Object Interactions
papers.problem_statement: 3D HOI methods are trained and tested on indoor scenes with few object categories because 3D object assets are hard to acquire, so they do not generalize to real-world images with diverse objects.

stated_limitations.text: The annotation pipeline depends on the quality of existing 3D human and object reconstruction tools.
stated_limitations.quote: Our proposed annotation process relies on the ability of 3D human and object reconstruction tools.

stated_limitations.text: Only 17% of source images passed, indicating most 2D HOI images are hard to reconstruct in 3D.
stated_limitations.quote: resulting in a pass rate of 17%, which indicates that most 2D HOI images are hard to reconstruct 3D representations.

stated_limitations.text: Coarse reconstruction has collisions, wrong scales and positions, and inaccurate object pose, so manual annotation is needed.
stated_limitations.quote: Rough reconstruction usually has serious mesh collision issues and inaccurate scales and positions. Additionally, the object pose provided by InstantMesh [46] is also not accurate.

stated_limitations.text: The optimizer fails when body parts severely occlude each other and the object lies between them, making contact assignment ambiguous.
stated_limitations.quote: human body parts occlude each other severely, and the object happens to be located between the occluded areas

stated_limitations.text: Existing 3D general models are poor at 3D HOI understanding.
stated_limitations.quote: our LLM-based 3d testing tasks proved that existing 3D general models are poor at 3D HOI understanding.

stated_limitations.text: No ground-truth objects exist, so object reconstruction quality cannot be evaluated with standard metrics.
stated_limitations.quote: since there is no GT object in our dataset, it is difficult to evaluate the quality of object reconstruction using traditional metrics.

failure_modes: Severe self-occlusion of body parts with object between them (contact ambiguity)
Occlusion-completion inpainting masks sometimes fail and need manual repair
Adding contact loss can increase collision in some images
Training-based HOI methods generalize poorly to open-world objects; training-free ones rely on manual annotation
future_work: More advanced 3D-AIGC tools to improve annotation efficiency
Train a judge model to accelerate reconstruction filtering
Use the 212-template library for poorly reconstructed objects
More fine-annotated data for general 3D HOI understanding models
Models that jointly understand images and recover human and object poses
restrictive_assumptions: Single RGB image; monocular depth estimate for coarse placement
Object meshes from single-image generation (InstantMesh) with inpainting
Heavy manual annotation in Blender and a web tool
Single-person annotation per image; part-level (34 regions) contact rather than vertex-level
Benchmark initializes human parameters from dataset annotations and gives object meshes

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best method still has 38.44 cm translation error and 19.3 cm Chamfer distance; PHOSA 77.79 cm and 49.1 cm
Top-1 between 0.20 and 0.47 depending on prompt
About 103 mm MPJPE and 131 mm MPVPE
Object mesh projection IoU after fine annotation only 0.48

open_problems_listed: Lack of 3D open-world HOI data; existing 3D HOI datasets indoors with few objects
In-the-wild 3D HOI benchmarks limited to few categories with fixed CAD models
Training-free methods limited and reliant on manual annotation; training-based methods fail in open world
3D HOI understanding by large 3D/LLM models is poor
Reliable object reconstruction from occluded in-the-wild images
Efficient filtering of reconstructions
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet reconstruct metrically accurate 3D human-object arrangements for arbitrary objects from single in-the-wild images without manual annotation.

papers.title: PICO: Reconstructing 3D People In Contact with Objects
papers.problem_statement: Recovering 3D HOI from single images is hampered by depth ambiguity, occlusion and object variety; past work needs known object shapes and contacts, and no method robustly recovers object shape or human-object arrangement in natural images.

stated_limitations.text: May fail on interactions that differ significantly from those in PICO-db.
stated_limitations.quote: Like all current methods, PICO-fit might fail under truly novel interactions if these differ significantly from those included in PICO-db.

stated_limitations.text: No single statistical object shape model exists and foundation models have limited 3D reasoning.
stated_limitations.quote: no method robustly recovers 3D object shape from single images because, unlike for human bodies, there exists no single statistical model for object shape.

stated_limitations.text: Learning 3D HOI directly is described as intractable given the lack of 3D HOI datasets, motivating optimization.
stated_limitations.quote: Learning this is intractable due to the lack of 3D HOI datasets.

stated_limitations.text: Existing regression HOI methods work on their training datasets but fail out of domain.
stated_limitations.quote: However, they fail for out-of-domain (OOD) scenarios, i.e.: (1) unseen in-lab datasets, and (2) unseen in-the-wild images

failure_modes: Incorrect human contact prediction by DECO (85 of 500 sampled reconstructions)
Invalid object contact retrieval even with correct human contact (20/500)
Incorrect object retrieval not matching the image (12/500)
Incorrect human pose initialization by OSX (5/500)
Unusual contact scenarios not covered by the nearest-neighbour lookup
future_work: Make 3D contact estimation more general, efficient and robust
Train a direct feed-forward contact regressor on expanded in-the-wild contact labels
Use PICO-fit to automate pseudo ground-truth label creation
Explore vision-language models to go beyond finite datasets
restrictive_assumptions: Single RGB image
Object shape via retrieval from Objaverse (OpenShape), so the object is approximated by a retrieved mesh
Nearest-neighbour contact lookup from PICO-db for unlabeled images
Depends on OSX body initialization, DECO body contact and SAM masks
Static single-frame (no temporal) reconstruction

benchmark_gaps.observation: PICO-fit without GT contact 21.85 cm object error vs 13.34 cm with GT contact; baselines 14.12-24.30 cm
10.33 cm without GT contact; 8.36 cm with GT contact
PHOSA preferred 37.3% of the time; HDM comparison limited to 30 images of its 9 trained classes

open_problems_listed: No robust single-image 3D object shape recovery; no statistical object shape model
No robust recovery of 3D human-object pose and arrangement
Contact regressors infer only 2D contact, only body contact, or train on synthetic data
Generalization of HOI reconstruction to OOD and in-the-wild images
Scaling to novel object classes and interactions beyond finite datasets
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet infer dense body-object 3D contact and object pose from single natural images reliably enough to recover object placement without ground-truth contact.

papers.title: CORE4D: A 4D Human-Object-Human Interaction Dataset for Collaborative Object REarrangement
papers.problem_statement: Modeling collaborative (two-person) object rearrangement is under-researched for lack of datasets; existing HOI datasets cover individual behaviour or handovers with few object instances, vision-based HOI tracking has low fidelity under occlusion, and mocap is expensive to scale.

stated_limitations.text: Real capture is indoor only because it depends on a mocap system.
stated_limitations.quote: Firstly, outdoor scenes are not incorporated in CORE4D-Real due to the usage of the mocap system.

stated_limitations.text: The synthetic (retargeted) part of the dataset has no visual signals.
stated_limitations.quote: Secondly, visual signals are excluded in CORE4D-Synthetic.

stated_limitations.text: Vision-based human-object tracking is still too low-fidelity under multi-person occlusion to scale HOI data, motivating mocap plus retargeting.
stated_limitations.quote: they still struggle with low fidelity due to severe occlusions, which are common in multi-human collaborations. Additionally, mocap [ 41 , 53 ] is expensive and hard to scale up

stated_limitations.text: Prior contact-based interaction retargeting only works between objects of similar topology and scale.
stated_limitations.quote: These methods are all limited to objects with similar topology and scales.

failure_modes: Forecasting baselines (MDM, InterDiff, CAHMP) degrade on unseen object shapes (S2) for human pose prediction.
Interaction-synthesis baselines produce unnatural collaboration, inter-penetration and unnatural contact; OMOMO errors are larger for multi-human collaboration than for single-person interaction.
Synthesized motions have higher FID than real data (naturalness gap).
2D pose models trained on CORE4D-Real or BEHAVE lose accuracy when transferred to the other dataset (domain gap).
Baselines do not generate hand poses; hands were replaced with flat hands for evaluation.
future_work: Transfer real-world videos onto synthesized collaboration motions to give CORE4D-Synthetic visual signals.
Generalizable human-object-human motion forecasting and interaction synthesis across novel object geometries.
restrictive_assumptions: Real data captured with 12 infrared cameras, inertial-optical mocap suits, two data gloves per person and object markers (indoor studio).
Rigid objects with industrial-scanner 3D models (37 real objects, six categories).
Benchmarks take the object's 3D model and past poses as given.
Synthetic augmentation relies on category-level spatial homogeneity of human-object relations.

benchmark_gaps.observation: MDM 186.4 and InterDiff 186.4 on unseen objects vs 170.8 on seen objects (S1); object rotation error about 10-11 degrees for all methods.
Synthesized results have higher FID than real motion; qualitative inter-penetration and unnatural contact persist for all baselines.

open_problems_listed: Outdoor collaborative HOI capture not covered (mocap dependence).
Synthetic collaboration data lacks visual signals; video transfer onto synthetic motion is open.
Generalizing human collaborative motion to novel object shapes.
Motion naturalness of synthesized multi-human interaction (FID gap).
Avoiding inter-penetration and unnatural contact in generated collaboration.
Low-fidelity vision-based HOI tracking under severe multi-person occlusion.
Cost of scaling mocap to many objects.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Vision-only methods cannot yet track multi-person collaborative object manipulation at mocap fidelity under severe occlusion, so data still depends on studio mocap.

papers.title: ParaHome: Parameterizing Everyday Home Activities Towards 3D Generative Modeling of Human-Object Interactions
papers.problem_statement: There is no large-scale dataset jointly capturing 3D body, dexterous hand and object motion (including articulated and multiple objects) in natural home settings; existing datasets are static, table-top, single-object or atomic grasps.

stated_limitations.text: The system depends on artificial markers; authors plan a markerless approach.
stated_limitations.quote: Firstly, we plan to evolve our system towards a markerless approach by eliminating artificial markers and constructing motion priors from the current database.

stated_limitations.text: Captured in a single room with a limited object set; generalization needs other rooms and objects.
stated_limitations.quote: Secondly, we aim to replicate our system in different room settings, with more diverse objects ensuring better generalizability.

stated_limitations.text: ArUco markers corrupt the RGB data and may influence natural motion; RGB is not a target modality.
stated_limitations.quote: Even though ArUco markers have its downsides in corrupting RGB data and influencing natural human motions, using RGB data is not within our interest

stated_limitations.text: Object tracking can still fail under severe occlusion despite 70 cameras.
stated_limitations.quote: Although we use multiple cameras with our 3D marker system, object tracking failure may still happen due to severe occlusions.

stated_limitations.text: Wearable mocap drifts in global root position and uses imperfect skeleton scale assumptions.
stated_limitations.quote: wearable motion capture systems suffer from the drift issue in localizing the global root position, and more critically they employ an imperfect assumption of the body and hand skeleton scale

failure_modes: Hand-attached marker tracking suffers jitter or failure under occlusion or low camera visibility; system falls back to IMU body motion.
Object tracking gaps under severe occlusion are filled by assuming the object moves rigidly with nearby body joints.
Off-the-shelf 6D object pose and 3D hand pose estimators perform worse on ParaHome synthetic RGB than on prior benchmarks, attributed to mutual occlusion; failure cases shown due to occlusion.
future_work: Markerless capture using motion priors learned from the database.
Replicating the system in other room settings with more diverse objects.
Generative formulations: inferring object motion from body motion, finger motion from desired object motion, forecasting, text-conditioned HOI.
restrictive_assumptions: 70 synchronized RGB industrial cameras covering one room.
Xsens IMU suit and Manus gloves worn by the participant.
ArUco 3D marker cubes attached to every object and body part.
Pre-modeled rigid and articulated object models.
Object assumed near-rigidly attached to nearby joints when filling tracking gaps.

benchmark_gaps.metric: 6D object pose and 3D hand pose error
benchmark_gaps.observation: Performance lower than on ROPE, FreiHAND and HO3D, attributed to complex HOI with mutual occlusion (numbers in supplementary).

open_problems_listed: Markerless capture of body, hands and objects in natural home settings.
Generalization to other rooms and more diverse objects.
Occlusion-robust tracking of hands and objects during multi-object interaction.
Combining heterogeneous capture systems (camera rig and wearable IMUs) without drift and skeleton-scale error.
Learning spatio-temporal relations between human motion and object movement (object-from-body, fingers-from-object, forecasting, text-conditioned synthesis).
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet capture body, finger and multi-object motion in natural home activity without markers, wearables and a dense camera rig.

papers.title: ClimbingCap: Multi-Modal Dataset and Method for Rock Climbing in World Coordinate
papers.problem_statement: Human motion recovery focuses on ground-based motion; climbing (off-ground) capture is sparse due to few 3D labeled datasets, and existing global HMR methods accumulate error and cannot model off-ground motion consistently in world coordinates.

stated_limitations.text: IMU-derived labels are inaccurate and translation drifts over long captures, requiring global optimization and manual repair.
stated_limitations.quote: The pose and the translation obtained from the IMU measurements may be inaccurate. Especially the translation may significantly drift for long-duration capture.

stated_limitations.text: Existing global HMR accumulates errors over long sequences, especially for climbing.
stated_limitations.quote: global HMR methods often accumulate errors during long-term sequence recovery, affecting the accuracy of global trajectories and postures, especially in climbing movements

stated_limitations.text: RGB-only variant of ClimbingCap performs worst because LiDAR global position is required for post-processing.
stated_limitations.quote: Using only RGB imagery without LiDAR, this variant performs worst overall due to missing global position data required for post-processing.

failure_modes: Vertical climbing scenes are harder than horizontal ones for all methods including ClimbingCap (errors rise).
GVHMR fails in vertical scenes because it predicts horizontal velocity while the motion is upward.
WHAM and GVHMR are good in camera coordinates but poor in world coordinates.
LiDAR and LiDAR+RGB baselines do not model global trajectories and perform poorly.
restrictive_assumptions: Requires LiDAR (Ouster 128-beam) plus RGB; RGB-only performs much worse.
Pre-scanned high-resolution scene point cloud (Trimble X7) for each wall.
PTP hardware time synchronization and LiDAR-scene registration.
Labeled data requires Xsens IMU suit and manual annotation repair.
Static sensor placement per climbing scene.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best method ClimbingCap 106.95 vs 78.99 horizontal; GVHMR 1442.50 and WHAM 1499.85 in vertical scenes.
ClimbingCap 88.92 vertical vs 75.45 horizontal.
ClimbingCap is not best on WA-MPJPE in zero-shot transfer to CIMI4D.

open_problems_listed: Few public 3D climbing datasets (only SPEED21 and CIMI4D before this).
Global HMR ambiguity between camera and world coordinates.
Error accumulation of global HMR in long sequences.
Off-ground motion not handled by ground-based global HMR priors.
IMU drift in long-duration capture.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet recover off-ground, scene-contact-rich human motion in world coordinates from RGB alone without LiDAR and pre-scanned scenes.

papers.title: FRAME: Floor-aligned Representation for Avatar Motion from Egocentric Video
papers.problem_statement: Egocentric body-facing stereo motion capture suffers heavy occlusion and scarce real data; prior methods rely on synthetic data and impractical rigs, and show poor in-the-wild generalization, temporal inconsistency, floor penetration and foot skating.

stated_limitations.text: The method does not exploit other headset modalities such as environment meshes, forward cameras, eye gaze or controller hand poses.
stated_limitations.quote: Current VR headsets offer rich multimodal data such as environment meshes, forward-facing cameras, eye-gaze tracking, and hand pose estimation from controllers—inputs our current method does not exploit.

stated_limitations.text: Struggles with significant occlusion and self-contact.
stated_limitations.quote: it can struggle with inherent motion capture issues such as significant occlusions and self-contact.

stated_limitations.text: Prior egocentric work suffers synthetic-to-real gap and artifacts.
stated_limitations.quote: common limitations persist: poor generalization to in-the-wild data, temporal inconsistencies, and artifacts like body-floor penetration, and foot skating.

failure_modes: Significant occlusions of the body from the head-mounted view.
Self-contact poses.
Single-view (no stereo) input gives highest error (MPJPE 87.94 mm in ablation).
future_work: Exploit environment meshes, forward-facing cameras, eye gaze and controller hand poses.
Integrate physics-based modeling to enforce physical constraints and resolve ambiguous cases.
restrictive_assumptions: Requires on-device 6D head pose (Quest SLAM) at inference.
Downward-facing stereo fisheye camera rig mounted on the headset.
Ground truth from a 120-camera 4K markerless studio and an ArUco board during collection.
Floor-aligned frame assumes a known floor / gravity alignment from the device.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best full model still 47.53 mm; left-view-only variant 87.94 mm.

open_problems_listed: Scarcity of real-world annotated ego-facing data and synthetic-to-real gap.
Impractical prior rigs (protruding cameras, head-mounted checkerboards).
Accurate device pose tracking during dataset collection.
Occlusion and self-contact in egocentric body capture.
Physical plausibility (floor penetration, foot skating).
papers.field_cannot_yet: Egocentric body capture still cannot resolve heavy self-occlusion and self-contact reliably from head-mounted cameras.

papers.title: MotionPRO: Exploring the Role of Pressure in Human MoCap and Beyond
papers.problem_statement: Vision-based mocap ignores physical interaction with the scene, producing temporal drift, jitter, sliding, floating, penetration and poor global trajectories when driving avatars or humanoids; pressure could supply the missing contact cue.

stated_limitations.text: Dependence on specialized pressure sensors; inferring pressure from vision is the key next step.
stated_limitations.quote: A key next step is to infer pressure information from visual input, which would expand its applicability by reducing the reliance on specialized sensors.

stated_limitations.text: All motion must stay within the pressure mat area.
stated_limitations.quote: All motions must occur within the range of the pressure mat to ensure that each motion data point has a corresponding pressure measurement.

stated_limitations.text: Without pressure-RGB fusion, global accuracy drops while local MPJPE improves, showing a trade-off between 2D alignment and physical plausibility.
stated_limitations.quote: a trade-off between 2D loss and 3D loss is necessary.

stated_limitations.text: Pressure-only estimation yields plausible lower-body pose and trajectory (benefit stated for lower body).
stated_limitations.quote: pressure could provide accurate global trajectory and plausible lower body pose

failure_modes: In humanoid imitation, more accurate poses make the NAO robot fall on actions it cannot perform (jumping, lying down, plank), lowering completeness.
Compared with IC[FT], slight loss in global trajectory accuracy for pressure-only pose estimation.
Prior vision-only methods: floating legs, wrong leg pose under occlusion, vertical root drift (WHAM, TRACE).
future_work: Infer pressure from visual input to drop specialized sensors.
Study contact duration in base of support, CoM-CoP distance and demographic factors.
Health monitoring and sports training applications.
restrictive_assumptions: Pressure mat under the subject; motion confined to the mat.
Four RGB cameras and a 12-camera optical mocap system for ground truth.
Ground contact is the interaction modelled (no hand-object contact).
Static, calibrated indoor capture.
open_problems_listed: Inferring pressure from vision to remove specialized sensors.
Physical plausibility of mocap (drift, jitter, sliding, floating, penetration).
Whole-body contact (hips, hands, knees) beyond foot contact in global trajectory estimation.
Lower-body robot motion tracking remains unstable from vision alone.
Relationships between base-of-support contact, CoM-CoP distance and demographics.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Vision-only mocap cannot yet supply the physical contact and force cues needed for drift-free, penetration-free global motion without dedicated pressure sensors.

papers.title: HandX: Scaling Bimanual Motion and Interaction Generation
papers.problem_statement: Realistic hand motion and bimanual interaction are underexplored in motion synthesis; existing datasets lack high-fidelity bimanual sequences with fine finger dynamics, contact timing and fine-grained text, and use mismatched skeletons and protocols.

stated_limitations.text: Dataset is finite and cannot cover the full range of dexterity and interactions.
stated_limitations.quote: the dataset is still finite in both volume and diversity. Consequently, it cannot exhaustively cover the full spectrum of human dexterity or every possible interaction scenario

stated_limitations.text: Aggregated public data keeps residual quality problems.
stated_limitations.quote: inherent quality issues in the raw sources, such as minor jitter or kinematic implausibility, cannot be completely eliminated.

stated_limitations.text: Model scaling saturates; an ultra-large variant performs worse on all metrics.
stated_limitations.quote: When we further increase the model size to an ultra-large variant with more parameters than the 12-layer model, performance drops across all metrics

failure_modes: Ultra-large diffusion model degrades across all metrics (over-scaling).
Increasing FSQ codebook size alone does not reliably improve the autoregressive model.
Gains from scaling are not strictly monotonic for every metric.
future_work: Dexterous hand motion synthesis research on the HandX benchmark (stated as purpose).
restrictive_assumptions: New data from a 36-camera OptiTrack studio with 25 hand markers per hand.
Hand-only joint-position representation (no object geometry in the generated output).
Constant bone length assumption in skeleton reconstruction.
Text annotations produced automatically by kinematic features plus LLM.
open_problems_listed: Finite volume and diversity of bimanual motion data.
Residual jitter and kinematic implausibility in aggregated public datasets.
Mismatched skeletons, frame rates and annotation protocols across hand datasets.
Lack of fine-grained text supervision for hand motion.
Saturation of model scaling beyond a regime.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field still lacks enough clean, high-fidelity bimanual finger-level data to cover the full range of human dexterity.

papers.title: Glove2Hand: Synthesizing Natural Hand-Object Interaction from Multi-Modal Sensing Gloves
papers.problem_statement: HOI capture is vision-only, so it lacks force and contact information and suffers hand occlusion; sensing gloves give these signals but change appearance, so glove videos must be translated to bare hands.

stated_limitations.text: Synthesis quality degrades in unseen in-the-wild settings.
stated_limitations.quote: While performance degrades in the challenging In-the-Wild setting, the results remain respectable.

stated_limitations.text: Naive hand render overlay causes penetration, floating and wrist artifacts, needing a diffusion restorer.
stated_limitations.quote: implausible object interactions like penetration or floating, as the render is not interaction-aware; and an unnatural wrist connection, as the arm is not modeled.

stated_limitations.text: Mocap ground truth can be inaccurate due to marker occlusion or sync latency.
stated_limitations.quote: the ground truth hand pose may exhibit inaccuracies due to marker occlusion or synchronization latency during rapid motion.

stated_limitations.text: Prior contact methods need pre-scanned rigid objects; multi-camera studios are impractical in the wild.
stated_limitations.quote: it only works with pre-scanned rigid objects and is not capable of providing continuous force measurements.

failure_modes: In-the-Wild (unseen subjects, objects, backgrounds) MOS drops to about 2.2-2.8 with gaps to real of 0.8-1.65.
Low identity consistency scores even in-domain (2.70).
Training a tracker on raw glove videos degrades accuracy due to domain gap (UmeTrack MKPE 19.2 to 27.2 mm on occlusion).
Glove's larger shape leaves artifacts and can wrongly occlude foreground objects when overlaying renders.
future_work: Scale training data and improve HOI segmentation masks to close the in-the-wild domain gap.
restrictive_assumptions: Per-subject 3D Gaussian hand model must be optimized; same-subject translation.
Paired glove and bare-hand sessions with identical object configurations.
Mocap markers on gloves and hands for 3D pose.
Egocentric grayscale headset stereo cameras.
Tactile sensors only at fingertips (binary fingertip contact).

benchmark_gaps.metric: Mean Opinion Score / gap to real
benchmark_gaps.observation: Video hand realism 2.69 (gap 1.65); motion stability 2.54 (gap 1.60); visual artifacts 2.19 (gap 1.53).
UmeTrack 19.2 mm on occluded frames; fine-tuned 16.6 mm, still higher than non-occluded MKPE.T values near 10 mm.
PressureVision++ reaches 0.8% IoU on dexterous HOI; best model 88.2%.

open_problems_listed: Vision-only HOI lacks force and contact signals.
Hand occlusion makes robust tracking hard; occluded ground truth is hard to obtain.
Contact estimation from vision lacks large accurately labeled data; prior work limited to planar surfaces.
Temporal and multi-view consistency for generative hand video.
Interactions with non-rigid, unknown-shape objects.
In-the-wild domain gap for synthesized data.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet obtain contact force and occluded-hand pose ground truth from bare-hand video without instrumented gloves or studios.

papers.title: Detecting Precise Hand Touch Moments in Egocentric Video
papers.problem_statement: Existing contact-understanding methods work on frames or long segments and cannot determine when contact first occurs; no dataset gives large-scale frame-level touch annotations in egocentric video.

stated_limitations.text: Existing contact methods lack temporal granularity to find contact onset.
stated_limitations.quote: Consequently, existing contact-understanding methods cannot determine when contact first occurs.

stated_limitations.text: Only intentional, visually unambiguous touches are annotated; unobservable contacts are excluded.
stated_limitations.quote: We include only intentional and visually unambiguous interactions, and exclude accidental contact or cases where the contact moment cannot be reliably observed.

stated_limitations.text: HOI4D training labels come from an automatic tool that differs from manual labels by 1.94 frames on average.
stated_limitations.quote: this automatic tool differs from manual labels by an average of 1.94 frames

stated_limitations.text: MixUp augmentation degrades performance by 7.37% mAP due to noise in hand-object regions.
stated_limitations.quote: applying MixUp [41] significantly degraded performance, reducing mAP across thresholds by 7.37%.

failure_modes: Exact-frame accuracy (delta=0) stays low: best AP 14.25 on HOI4D and 24.25 on TACO without NMS.
NMS can reduce AP at delta=0 when closely spaced peaks merge or shift.
On smaller TACO, grasp branch dilutes exact-frame precision at delta=0.
Egomotion, close-range occlusion, perspective distortion, pre-touch micro-motion and motion blur make near-touch frames ambiguous.
restrictive_assumptions: Hand boxes from off-the-shelf detectors (ground-truth boxes in training).
Grasp pseudo-labels from an external model (Hands23).
Segments selected where the hand-object interface is visible and contact is discernible.
Monocular egocentric RGB; data sourced from HOI4D and TACO only.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best 24.25; mAP 41.08; with SNMS delta=0 only 16.78.

open_problems_listed: No large-scale frame-level egocentric touch dataset existed.
Frame-precise contact onset detection under egomotion, occlusion and motion blur.
Distinguishing near-touch from actual-contact frames.
Closely spaced bimanual touch events.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Vision models cannot yet localize the exact frame of hand-object contact onset reliably in egocentric video.

papers.title: EgoXtreme: A Dataset for Robust Object Pose Estimation in Egocentric Views under Extreme Conditions
