papers.problem_statement: Existing 6D object pose benchmarks are captured under controlled, well-lit, largely static third-person conditions and miss the motion blur, dynamic or extreme illumination, smoke and truncation that dominate real egocentric smart-glass use.

stated_limitations.text: Ground truth relies on an OptiTrack mocap system, which confines capture to specialised indoor spaces and prevents evaluating true outdoor robustness.
stated_limitations.quote: the reliance on the OptiTrack system for high-accuracy GT confines data collection to specialized indoor environments, limiting the evaluation of true outdoor robustness.

stated_limitations.text: No 3D hand pose annotations are provided; labelling hand articulation under extreme blur and speed is itself an unsolved problem.
stated_limitations.quote: we note the absence of 3D hand pose annotations. Accurately labeling intricate hand articulations, particularly due to the extreme motion blur and speed prevalent in the sports scenario, remains a significant independent challenge.

stated_limitations.text: Image restoration preprocessing (deblur, dehaze, low-light enhancement) does not help pose estimation and often hurts it.
stated_limitations.quote: The result of image restoration techniques ultimately fail to help, and often hurt performance.

failure_modes: RGB-only zero-shot pose estimators (FoundPose, GigaPose, PicoPose) degrade strongly under extreme lighting and smoke compared with standard lighting.
Sports scenario with severe object cropping and motion blur: models fail to reach meaningful recall overall.
FoundPose sparse feature matching often fails to obtain the minimum correspondences for PnP-RANSAC under egocentric cropping and blur, producing no pose output.
Dehazing introduces noise artifacts under non-uniform partial smoke, collapsing recall in the emergency scenario.
Light enhancement under high-contrast highlights or extreme low light introduces noise that makes prediction harder.

Direct temporal propagation of the previous pose fails with large inter-frame displacement in fast sports motion; fusion propagation of previous rotation gives poor initial poses that the current frame cannot correct.
future_work: Generate accurate 3D hand labels by combining existing mocap data with parametric hand models.
Move beyond single-frame visual features toward effective temporal modelling for egocentric object pose.
Hybrid temporal strategies that use dynamic quality assessment to selectively apply temporal priors.
Robust and resilient pose tracking under real-world extreme conditions, including outdoor evaluation.
restrictive_assumptions: Evaluated methods require object CAD models (13 objects with CAD).
Baseline evaluation uses ground-truth bounding boxes to decouple detection errors (end-to-end with CNOS only in appendix).
RGB-only, since smart glasses lack depth; RGB-D methods such as FoundationPose excluded.
Ground truth needs OptiTrack markers on objects and headset, indoor capture only.
Single egocentric head-mounted camera (Aria glasses).

benchmark_gaps.observation: 2.81 / 8.80 / 23.02 without preprocessing; preprocessing lowers it further (e.g. 2.58/8.22/20.99 with two methods).
Drops from 15.12 to 4.74 with dehazing.

benchmark_gaps.dataset: EgoXtreme sports normal light, golf club and pingpong
benchmark_gaps.observation: Per-frame 0.08 (golf) and 0.53 (pingpong); best temporal strategy stays below 1.6 percent at 0.1d.
63.32 with no preprocessing, falling to 53.28 with combined preprocessing.

open_problems_listed: Robust 6D object pose under severe motion blur, dynamic or low light and smoke in egocentric view.
Outdoor evaluation of egocentric object pose (mocap restricts to indoor).
Accurate 3D hand pose labelling under extreme blur and speed.
Temporal modelling and tracking that survives large inter-frame displacement.
Restoration methods whose output actually helps downstream pose estimation rather than adding artifacts.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet estimate or track the 6D pose of hand-held objects from egocentric RGB under fast motion, low light or smoke with usable accuracy.

papers.title: Teleoperation, Simulation, or Human Video? Data Utilization Law for Robot Manipulation
papers.problem_statement: The robotics community follows a more-is-better data paradigm but lacks a principled, quantitative understanding of the relative value of teleoperation, simulation and human video data once training cost and embodiment gaps are counted.

stated_limitations.text: Naively added human video degrades in-domain policy performance due to embodiment and viewpoint mismatch.
stated_limitations.quote: Naively adding human video can degrade in-domain performance due to embodiment and viewpoint mismatch.

stated_limitations.text: Simulation data hurts simple in-domain tasks, attributed to sim-to-real artifacts.
stated_limitations.quote: simulation exhibits a strong negative utilization (ηlocal = −23), indicating that the sim-to-real gap introduces detrimental artifacts that harm performance.

stated_limitations.text: Utilization ratios are task- and goal-dependent rather than universal; data mixing must be tailored per task.
stated_limitations.quote: These nuances indicate that data mixing must be tailored to the speciﬁc task and performance objectives.

stated_limitations.text: Scope limited to three rigid-object dual-arm tasks; deformable and long-horizon tasks left to future work.
stated_limitations.quote: future work will extend this analysis to deformable-object manipulation as well as broader, high-dimensional, and long-horizon challenges

failure_modes: Human-video pretraining reduces in-domain success on all three tasks (e.g. Pick Dual Bottles 0.70 to 0.45).
Human video harms the complex Rank RGB Blocks task even in unseen positions (local ratio -4).
Positive effect of human video on unseen positions diminishes as data scale grows.
With pi0 on ARX-R5, human video was uniformly detrimental in unseen positions, attributed to spatial domain mismatch.
Neither simulation-only nor human-video-only training is sufficient to accomplish the tasks.
future_work: Extend the utilization analysis to deformable-object manipulation.
Extend to broader, high-dimensional and long-horizon manipulation challenges as simulators support richer task families.
restrictive_assumptions: Locally linear performance model near a chosen teleoperation count to define local ratios.
Optimality gap assumed to follow a power law in teleoperation count.
Human video recorded with a chest-mounted camera in the same environment as teleoperation; hand actions from MediaPipe landmarks and estimated gripper state.
Human-video action space (end-effector deltas) differs from robot joint-angle action space; pretrain then fine-tune protocol.
Only 10 real trials per scenario per policy; three tabletop rigid-object bimanual tasks.

benchmark_gaps.dataset: Real Aloha-Agilex-2.0, Rank RGB Blocks unseen background
benchmark_gaps.observation: Teleoperation only 0.13; with simulation 0.20.

benchmark_gaps.dataset: Real Aloha-Agilex-2.0, Rank RGB Blocks unseen position
benchmark_gaps.observation: Teleoperation 0.17, drops to 0.13 with human video.

benchmark_gaps.dataset: Real Aloha-Agilex-2.0, Pick Dual Bottles unseen background
benchmark_gaps.observation: 0.20 teleoperation-only; 0.30 with budget-aware sim mix.

open_problems_listed: Principled valuation of heterogeneous robot data sources (exchange rates) across tasks.
Embodiment and viewpoint gap that makes unaligned human video harmful.
Sim-to-real gap that harms in-domain performance on simple tasks.
Extending data utilization laws to deformable, high-dimensional and long-horizon manipulation.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet turn human manipulation video into robot training data that reliably helps rather than hurts in-domain policy performance.

papers.title: Hoi! - A Multimodal Dataset for Force-Grounded, Cross-View Articulated Manipulation
papers.problem_statement: Human-centric video datasets and robotics datasets study different interactions and lack paired vision, force and tactile data from real interactions with articulated furniture, so transfer across embodiments and viewpoints cannot be studied.

stated_limitations.text: Hoi! gripper demonstrations are still human-operated, so they do not capture the kinematic and dynamic constraints of real manipulators.
stated_limitations.quote: they are still generated by a human operator and therefore do not fully capture the kinematic and dynamic constraints of real manipulators.

stated_limitations.text: Generalization across full-body morphology remains open.
stated_limitations.quote: true generalization across full-body morphology is still an open challenge.

stated_limitations.text: Does not cover the full range of mechanical complexities or rare edge-case mechanisms.
stated_limitations.quote: it does not yet cover the full range of mechanical complexities or rare edge-case mechanisms found in real-world environments.

stated_limitations.text: Benchmarks are object-centric perception tasks, not end-to-end policy learning.
stated_limitations.quote: our current benchmarks are object-centric and focus on perception tasks such as force estimation and articulation reasoning.

stated_limitations.text: Hand keypoints come from Aria MPS automatic estimates, not manual or mocap labels, so the hand benchmark is exploratory only.
stated_limitations.quote: we treat this evaluation as an exploratory analysis rather than a definitive benchmark.

failure_modes: Articulation estimators fail in the wild: ArtGS fails under clutter and non-robust object segmentation; ArtiPoint degrades with scaled monocular depth whose non-steady noise breaks 3D lifting and trajectory filtering.
Authors conclude current articulation methods are too dependent on accurate depth or fail in the presence of clutter and hands.
Tactile force model Sparsh gives errors of several newtons versus millinewton accuracy in-lab, due to out-of-distribution contact geometries and load regimes.
ForceSight visual force estimation degrades on stiff or force-demanding mechanisms (fridge, oven, magnetic drawers) and on raw force signals with operator disturbances.
HaMeR hand pose PCK drops on egocentric manipulation (fast hand motion, low-resolution egocentric imagery), lowest in kitchen scenes.
future_work: Extend object-centric perception benchmarks toward end-to-end policy learning where perception and action are trained jointly.
Cover more mechanical complexities and rare articulation mechanisms.
Methods that better leverage the multimodal (force, tactile, multi-view) signals for egocentric manipulation.
restrictive_assumptions: Aria glasses provide no dense depth; depth for articulation baselines comes from MapAnything scaled using scanned scene meshes.
Scenes laser-scanned before and after manipulation for ground truth.
Force and tactile ground truth only available for the instrumented gripper embodiments, not bare hands.
Hand keypoints derived from Aria MPS, not ground truth.

benchmark_gaps.metric: ArtiPoint articulation type recall / axis angle error (deg)
benchmark_gaps.observation: Type recall 26.9 percent; axis angle errors 47.06 and 63.76 deg versus 14.54 and 17.14 on Arti4D.
0.321 m with 0 percent recall on one type.
Combined 3.86 N (DINO) and 4.11 N (DINOv2).
3.53 projected, 3.64 raw versus 0.40 on the ForceSight dataset.
0.535 versus 0.844 to 0.893 on Ego4D, VISOR, New Days.

open_problems_listed: Transfer of interaction understanding between human and robot embodiments and viewpoints.
Generalization across full-body morphology.
Coverage of complex and rare articulation mechanisms.
End-to-end policy learning combining perception and action.
Articulation estimation robust to clutter, hands and noisy monocular depth.
Tactile and visual force estimation that generalizes beyond lab indenters and to force-demanding mechanisms.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet estimate articulation and interaction forces from in-the-wild egocentric video with clutter, hands and no reliable depth.

papers.title: Ego-1K: A Large-Scale Multiview Video Dataset for Egocentric Vision
papers.problem_statement: No large-scale dataset provides synchronized multiview egocentric video of real dynamic scenes; NVS datasets are exocentric or static and egocentric datasets are monocular or stereo, so egocentric 4D reconstruction cannot be benchmarked.

stated_limitations.text: iToF depth streams were not used because depth is unreliable under motion and phase ambiguity.
stated_limitations.quote: we include the iToF streams in the raw dataset but do not use them in our experiments due to unreliable depth estimates in the presence of motion and phase ambiguity.

stated_limitations.text: No ground-truth depth; stereo is evaluated only by cross-pair consistency.
stated_limitations.quote: Since we do not have ground-truth depth for evaluation, we instead measure consistency among disparity maps estimated for the same frame.

stated_limitations.text: Rig weighs about 6 kg and needs a backpack-mounted crane.
stated_limitations.quote: Due to the rig's weight (approximately 6 kg), we use a backpack-mounted crane to support most of it while allowing natural head motion.

stated_limitations.text: Online calibration assumes calibration is constant over a recording; 1-3 pixel shifts from lens movement and temperature affect reconstruction.
stated_limitations.quote: This can result in image shifts of 1–3 pixels, which can significantly affect reconstruction accuracy.

failure_modes: Existing 3D and 4D NVS methods fail with combined ego-motion, near-range hand motion, large disparities and frequent occlusions.
Per-frame 3DGS is insufficient to overcome ill-posedness.
Dynamic models (K-Planes, Spacetime Gaussians) fail because they are designed for object-centric scenes or fixed-pose multiview video.
Performance gap is larger for close dynamic objects (hands) than for farther ones (other persons).
43 recordings discarded for dark images or too few frames.
future_work: Create high-quality per-frame depth via multiview or multi-baseline stereo as pseudo ground truth for two-view or monocular depth evaluation.
Ablation studies on subsets of cameras.
Evaluation of HOI-focused tasks.
Consistency studies for semantic or person segmentation; robustness to stereo baseline changes and temporal stability.
restrictive_assumptions: 12 hardware-synchronized global-shutter cameras on a head rig (not deployable glasses).
Rig poses from headset VIO.
Short recordings of 8-10 s.
Stereo-guided baseline requires calibrated rectified stereo pairs.

benchmark_gaps.observation: K-Planes 16.46, per-frame 3DGS 21.22, Spacetime Gaussians 24.76; stereo-guided 3DGS 29.12.
Selective-Stereo 0.0 percent, BiDAStereo 3.1 percent; FoundationStereo 74.0 percent.

open_problems_listed: Egocentric dynamic 4D novel view synthesis with ego-motion and near-field hands.
Ground-truth or pseudo-ground-truth depth for egocentric dynamic scenes.
Robustness to stereo baseline changes and temporal stability.
HOI-focused evaluation on egocentric multiview data.
Reliable active depth (iToF) under motion.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet reconstruct dynamic egocentric scenes with close-range moving hands and objects from a moving head without strong stereo depth priors.

papers.title: HUMOTO: A 4D Dataset of Mocap Human Object Interactions
papers.problem_statement: Realistic 4D HOI data is scarce and expensive; most datasets cover single-object interactions or lack detailed hand motion, leaving multi-object interaction with full-body and hand motion a gap.

stated_limitations.text: Only a single performer due to mocap suit size constraints, biasing body shape and movement style.
stated_limitations.quote: due to motion capture suit size constraints, our dataset includes only a single performer, which may introduce a bias toward a particular human body shape and movement style.

stated_limitations.text: Considerable manual cleaning by artists was required; more robust automatic pose estimation is needed.
stated_limitations.quote: the dataset preparation process required considerable manual cleaning and refinement of the captured motion data.

stated_limitations.text: Quantitative quality metrics depend on motion and interaction complexity and should not be read in isolation.
stated_limitations.quote: The quantitative results are influenced by features of the datasets that do not necessarily represent quality issues.

failure_modes: FoundationPose frame-to-frame tracking fails during rapid movements; a mask-difference reset and SAM2 masks with human annotation were needed.
Raw capture contains drift, tracking errors, joint jitter and foot sliding that artists must fix.
State-of-the-art motion generation (MotionGPT) cannot generate fine-grained multi-object interaction.
4D Humans and TRAM fail to predict correct poses on HUMOTO renderings with occlusion and include no hand pose.
future_work: More advanced and robust pose estimation to reduce manual cleaning in HOI data collection.
Use HUMOTO as training data for automated high-fidelity HOI capture techniques.
restrictive_assumptions: Inertial Rokoko suit and gloves (EMF), requiring a custom wooden stage to avoid magnetic interference.
Object 6DoF from dual Kinect RGB-D with FoundationPose, needing artist-built object models.
Calibration stance at a fixed position to align mocap and camera frames.
Extensive manual artist cleanup.
Single performer, scripted tasks.
open_problems_listed: Capturing multi-object interaction with full-body and detailed hand motion at scale.
Reducing manual cleanup cost for high-fidelity HOI data.
Body-shape and style diversity in HOI mocap.
Generating detailed multi-object HOI motion from text.
Pose estimation under object occlusion including hands.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet capture clean multi-object full-body and hand interaction data without heavy manual artist cleanup.

papers.title: Perceiving and Acting in First-Person: A Dataset and Benchmark for Egocentric Human-Object-Human Interactions
papers.problem_statement: Existing human-centric datasets offer specialist interaction categories and ignore that AI assistants perceive and act from a first-person view, hindering generalist assistant learning.

stated_limitations.text: Limited to indoor scenes with 50 daily objects; indoor capture lacks some realism.
stated_limitations.quote: InterVLA is limited to indoor scenarios with 50 daily objects involved.

stated_limitations.text: Building the dataset is time-consuming; around 10 hours is still insufficient for large generalist models.
stated_limitations.quote: it is still insufficient for training large generalist interaction models.

stated_limitations.text: Inertial gloves discarded to preserve RGB realism; finger poses not captured by mocap.
stated_limitations.quote: attaching additional reflective markers on the hands fails to yield robust finger gestures empirically, and employing heavy inertial gloves significantly compromises the fidelity of RGB videos.

failure_modes: Egocentric global human motion estimators (TRACE, GLAMR, TRAM, WHAM) fail when rapid head turns push the person out of view; GLAMR and WHAM lose global orientation, TRACE misses frames.
Errors attributed to occlusions, rapid camera motion, incomplete body capture and subjects re-entering the frame.
WiLoR hand pose on egocentric video fails to give smooth, accurate estimates.
Interaction synthesis methods have higher FID than real data; interaction prediction leaves significant errors in human motion, object pose and contact.
future_work: Extend to outdoor settings and richer scenes.
Sparse-view 4D scene reconstruction using exocentric views.
Hand-object interaction reconstruction from egocentric multi-object video.
Motion reconstruction from sparse egocentric signals.
restrictive_assumptions: 20-camera optical mocap with glued markers on skin and clothes.
Objects as rigid bodies with at least four markers and scanned meshes.
Hands tracked only by three wrist markers (no finger ground truth).
Indoor mocap venue.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best WHAM 333.6; TRACE 720.1, TRAM 684.1, GLAMR 589.9.
Best CAHMP 172.5; object translation error 115.6 mm.
Best USST 0.24 / 0.32.

open_problems_listed: Egocentric world-grounded motion estimation of another person under rapid head motion and re-entry.
Natural multi-human multi-object interaction synthesis.
Interaction prediction from egocentric vision and language.
Sparse-view 4D scene reconstruction.
Egocentric hand-object reconstruction with multiple objects.
Outdoor and larger-scale capture; finger ground truth without compromising RGB.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet recover world-grounded human and hand motion from a moving egocentric camera when people leave and re-enter the view.

papers.title: DexH2R: A Benchmark for Dynamic Dexterous Grasping in Human-to-Robot Handover
papers.problem_statement: Dynamic dexterous grasping for human-to-robot handover lacks real-world data; existing datasets use static grasps or synthetic givers and two-finger grippers, creating a sim-to-real gap.

stated_limitations.text: RGB-only diffusion policy cannot handle occlusions and depth ambiguity.
stated_limitations.quote: it faces inherent limitations in handling occlusions and depth ambiguity due to the lack of explicit spatial information.

stated_limitations.text: MotionNet's aggressive strategy neglects collision avoidance, lowering safety.
stated_limitations.quote: this approach often neglects collision avoidance, resulting in lower safety rates and higher penetration frames.

stated_limitations.text: DP's conservative approach often fails to grasp within the frame limit.
stated_limitations.quote: While this improves safety, it often results in failure to grasp within the specified frame limit.

failure_modes: Success rates collapse in Hard Mode (alignment starts at 5 cm): MotionNet 26.6, DP 8.3, DP3 27.1 percent.
Safety rates are low: MotionNet 25.9 percent in Easy Mode.
Goal Pose Alignment linear interpolation needed as a corrective strategy to obtain reliable grasps.
Object pose annotation needs manual inspection and correction of first-frame global registration.
restrictive_assumptions: Single right ShadowHand on UR10e controlled by low-latency teleoperation.
Object annotation by SAM2, depth fusion, global registration with manual correction, frame-by-frame ICP; requires object point clouds.
Hand pose via MediaPipe 2D keypoints and off-the-shelf MANO fitting.
Large fixed multi-camera setup: 12 RGB cameras, 4 Azure Kinects, 2 wrist RealSense.
Linear motion assumed over short horizon during goal pose alignment.

benchmark_gaps.observation: MotionNet 71.1, DP 39.4, DP3 66.3.
cVAE 35.0; DexGraspAnything 52.81.

open_problems_listed: Real-world dynamic dexterous handover data for five-finger hands.
Balancing grasp success and collision safety near a human hand.
Fine-grained pose alignment in close proximity to a moving object.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet make a dexterous robot hand safely and reliably grasp an object a human is moving during handover.

papers.title: VOccl3D: A Video Benchmark Dataset for 3D Human Pose and Shape Estimation under real Occlusions
papers.problem_statement: HPS methods struggle under significant occlusion, and existing occlusion datasets use random patches or clipart overlays or have sparse, mild occlusion, so there is no realistic heavily occluded benchmark.

stated_limitations.text: Visual quality limited by lack of open high-fidelity assets; motions constrained by AMASS.
stated_limitations.quote: the visual quality of our synthetic humans is limited by the lack of open-source high-fidelity assets, such as garments, hairstyles, footwear, and diverse human motions

stated_limitations.text: Rendering relies on predefined camera poses to produce occlusions.
stated_limitations.quote: our rendering pipeline relies on predefined camera poses to generate images with substantial occlusions.

stated_limitations.text: A noticeable synthetic-to-real gap remains.
stated_limitations.quote: a noticeable gap remains between synthetic and real-world data.

stated_limitations.text: Improvements on real datasets with minimal occlusion are marginal.
stated_limitations.quote: since these datasets contain minimal occlusions, the improvements over CLIFF remain marginal.

failure_modes: All HPS methods degrade as occlusion severity increases from low to medium to hard.
Human detectors struggle under occlusion; HPS error rises sharply when using detected rather than ground-truth boxes.
Poor results stem from both HPS errors and bounding-box detection failures.
future_work: End-to-end framework to automatically generate occlusion-rich sequences without external camera parameters.
Bridge the sim-to-real gap for realistic human pose estimation.
Use for occlusion-aware silhouette extraction, body-part segmentation, 2D keypoints and detection.
restrictive_assumptions: Synthetic rendered humans on 3DGS-reconstructed backgrounds.
Main benchmark uses ground-truth bounding boxes.
Real occlusion evaluation relies on artificial black patches over 3DPW keypoints.
Monocular single-person HPS.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best fine-tuned VOccl3D-B-CLIFF 136.34 / 175.92; CLIFF 192.22 / 247.41.
71.10 with GT boxes versus 116.52 with YOLO11 and 114.85 with fine-tuned detector.

open_problems_listed: Robust HPS under heavy realistic occlusion.
Occlusion-robust person detection.
Sim-to-real gap for synthetic occlusion data.
Automatic generation of occlusion-rich sequences.
Higher-fidelity open human assets and more diverse motions.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet estimate 3D human pose and shape accurately when most of the body is occluded, especially without ground-truth detection boxes.

papers.title: LDPose: Towards Inclusive Human Pose Estimation for Limb-Deficient Individuals in the Wild
papers.problem_statement: Existing human pose datasets and methods assume complete limbs, so they cannot handle missing keypoints and produce unfair, biased results for people with limb deficiencies; no dataset exists for estimating residual limb endpoints.

stated_limitations.text: Demographic skew: mostly young adults and 67% Caucasian.
stated_limitations.quote: the LDPose dataset captures images mainly in young adults. The ethic distribution is not even, with 67% of the individuals being Caucasian.

stated_limitations.text: Over half the data is competitive para-sport, limiting transfer to everyday movement.
stated_limitations.quote: more than 50 % of LDPose images capture para-athletics and high-intensity para-athletic performances, which may limit the dataset's applicability to everyday movement scenarios.

stated_limitations.text: Only 2D image annotations; no depth or 3D joint relations.
stated_limitations.quote: LDPose is an image-based dataset with 2D annotations.

stated_limitations.text: Prosthetic limbs are not annotated even though they define the pose.
stated_limitations.quote: LDPose annotates only natural body keypoints, without explicitly considering prosthetic limbs, even though they play a significant role in defining the pose

stated_limitations.text: Privacy: real-world images need automated face anonymization and identity protection.
stated_limitations.quote: it is essential to implement automated face anonymization and identity protection techniques to align with ethical AI principles

stated_limitations.text: Standard COCO metrics do not penalize predicted keypoints on missing limbs.
stated_limitations.quote: If a model predicts these points with high confidence, COCO Metrics ignore the error and give a misleading high score.

stated_limitations.text: LDLoss trades COCO accuracy for better residual/intact discrimination.
stated_limitations.quote: models gain a better ability to differentiate between intact and residual limbs, but their performance degrades on COCO Metrics

failure_modes: Pretrained RTMPose and ViTPose place incorrect keypoints on residual limbs (Figure 1, confidence threshold 0.3).
Fine-tuned ViTPose (ViT-l) predicts both intact and residual keypoints on the same limb, giving anatomically incorrect poses while scoring COCO AP 82.6.
At least 64% of individuals wear prosthetics often hidden by clothing, making limb structure hard to assess; cosmetic prosthetics look like natural limbs.
Video frames contain motion blur (9.6%), occlusion (20.9%) and crowded backgrounds (25.8%); severely blurred frames were filtered out.
future_work: Expand data collection beyond competitive sports to workplace settings, daily activities and rehabilitation.
Add multi-view imaging and motion capture to provide depth and 3D joint relationships for 3D pose estimation.
Explore prosthetic-aware keypoint annotations.
Automated face anonymization and privacy-preserving learning techniques.
restrictive_assumptions: Single 2D RGB images only; no 3D or temporal annotation
Frames with severe motion blur removed during curation
Prostheses excluded from the keypoint definition
Data sourced largely from Paralympic sport footage and web images

benchmark_gaps.observation: YOLO-Pose without fine-tuning reaches AP 42.6 (49.8 after fine-tuning), the lowest of benchmarked methods.
Best COCO AP 82.6 (ViTPose ViT-l fine-tuned) coexists with anatomically impossible predictions; COCO metrics fail to reflect this.

open_problems_listed: Distinguishing residual-limb from intact-limb keypoints (existing methods struggle)
Demographic and activity diversity beyond young para-athletes
3D limb-deficient pose estimation with multi-view or mocap data
Prosthetic-aware keypoint annotation
Privacy and face anonymization for real-world imagery
Evaluation metrics that penalize anatomically inconsistent predictions
papers.field_cannot_yet: Pose estimators cannot yet reliably handle bodies that deviate from the complete-limb template, including residual limbs and prostheses, especially in 3D.

papers.title: ProGait: A Multi-Purpose Video Dataset and Benchmark for Transfemoral Prosthesis Users
papers.problem_statement: Vision-based gait analysis is scalable and non-invasive, but current models trained on able-bodied data fail to detect and analyze transfemoral prostheses because of their unique appearance and movement patterns.

stated_limitations.text: Only four subjects, due to recruitment cost of a vulnerable population.
stated_limitations.quote: While the dataset is limited to four subjects due to the inherent challenges and costs associated with recruiting and testing this vulnerable population

stated_limitations.text: Pose ground truth, including test set, comes largely from a fine-tuned RTMW model with manual correction.
stated_limitations.quote: the majority of our pose annotations, including those in the test set, are derived from the fine-tuned RTMW model

stated_limitations.text: Pretrained pose models miss prosthetic knee and foot keypoints.
stated_limitations.quote: the pre-trained model frequently fails to accurately detect keypoints on the prosthetic knees and feet.

stated_limitations.text: Grounded SAM2 loses track of the prosthetic leg even at high mIoU.
stated_limitations.quote: even with mIoU up to 96%, it can occasionally loss tracking of the prosthetic leg

stated_limitations.text: YOLO11 cannot represent a single subject made of discrete parts.
stated_limitations.quote: YOLO11 can only be trained on closed shapes and cannot inherently handle discrete parts of a single subject.

stated_limitations.text: Gait classification only uses the primary deviation, though deviations co-occur clinically.
stated_limitations.quote: in our benchmark studies, we only consider the primary gait deviation for our classification task.

stated_limitations.text: Fusing frontal and sagittal views reduces classification accuracy.
stated_limitations.quote: when both frontal and sagittal views are fed into the model, accuracy drops significantly.

failure_modes: Healthcare staff partially or fully occlude the subject, especially in the sagittal view outside the parallel bars.
Distinguishing the subject from healthcare staff and keeping consistent tracking under occlusion is hard outside the parallel bars.
Grounded SAM2 with prompt 'a person.' reaches only 0.358 mIoU; performance depends heavily on the text prompt.
Fine-tuned YOLO11 detects the body as separate instances, dropping accuracy inside the parallel bars.
Thin prosthetic legs occupy a small image area.
future_work: Leverage textual gait descriptions with large language models for quick assessment of stability, comfort and mobility.
Enable adaptive, interactive microcomputer-powered prosthetic legs.
Scale up to broader demographic and prosthetic diversity.
restrictive_assumptions: Two fixed cameras (frontal and sagittal) at 1080p 30 fps in a clinical indoor setting
Four middle-aged or elderly vascular-cause transfemoral amputees
2D keypoints only; no 3D
Single subject of interest per clip

benchmark_gaps.observation: Gait classification on the whole dataset with both views reaches only 0.384 top-1 and 0.413 balanced accuracy; inside parallel bars 0.364 top-1.
Fine-tuned YOLO11-ProGait reaches 0.847 mIoU; Grounded SAM2 'a person.' 0.358.
Pretrained HRNet 0.750, ViPNAS 0.761, ViTPose 0.830 versus fine-tuned RTMPose-ProGait 0.947.

open_problems_listed: Precisely detecting the prosthesis as part of the human body
Correctly distinguishing the subject from healthcare staff
Ensuring consistent tracking despite occlusions
Small sample size; need broader demographic and prosthetic diversity
Multiple co-occurring gait deviations (benchmark uses primary only)
Using textual gait reasoning with LLMs for clinical assessment
papers.field_cannot_yet: Off-the-shelf vision models cannot yet segment, track and pose prosthesis users in clinical video, or classify their gait deviations, without population-specific fine-tuning.

papers.title: Benchmarks and Challenges in Pose Estimation for Egocentric Hand Interactions with Objects
papers.problem_statement: Accurate 3D reconstruction of hand-object interactions from egocentric views is challenging due to heavy occlusion, viewpoint bias, camera distortion and head-motion blur; the HANDS23 challenge analyses where current methods succeed and fail.

stated_limitations.text: Several scenarios remain intractable for state-of-the-art methods.
stated_limitations.quote: Our study further reveals challenging scenarios intractable with state-of-the-art methods, such as fast hand motion, object reconstruction from narrow egocentric views, and close contact between two hands and objects.

stated_limitations.text: Most hand-object methods require a known object template.
stated_limitations.quote: Methods in this area mostly assume a given object template and jointly estimate the hand poses and the object rigid poses

stated_limitations.text: Egocentric object reconstruction is harder than allocentric.
stated_limitations.quote: In the egocentric view, it is notably more difficult to reconstruct accurate object surfaces, articulation (AAE), and hand-object contact (CDev).

stated_limitations.text: Object pose estimation suffers from arm/hand occlusion and changing views.
stated_limitations.quote: object poses are significantly impacted by occlusions from hands and arms, and the egocentric view undergoes substantial changes throughout a sequence.

stated_limitations.text: Fisheye distortion at image edges degrades hand estimates.
stated_limitations.quote: Hands near image edges are highly distorted due to the fish-eye cameras.

stated_limitations.text: Articulated microwave is hardest due to global rotation sensitivity.
stated_limitations.quote: The hardest object to reconstruct with good contact consistency (see CDev) is the microwave in both settings due to global rotation sensitivity

stated_limitations.text: Upper headset cameras often miss hands, creating unbalanced views.
stated_limitations.quote: the samples from cam1 and cam2 are fewer and unbalanced as their cameras often fail to capture hands due to the camera layout.

failure_modes: High-error actions inspect, screw, rotate and position: heavy object occlusion, fast fingertip motion, and two hands in close contact with the object.
Objects partially observed at image boundaries and heavily occluded by hands/arms fail in egocentric reconstruction (Fig. 5).
Grab motions (diverse object poses) are harder than use/articulation motions.
Base method error rises from 20.31 to 24.85 mm as hands approach fisheye image edges.
UVHand underperforms due to incomplete training.
future_work: More efficient training using multi-view egocentric cameras.
Leverage 3D foundation priors to regularize template-free hand-object reconstruction.
More expressive hand-object pose representations, e.g. heatmap-based.
Incorporate motion and temporal modelling.
More diverse egocentric interaction scenarios.
Recognize actions through captured hand poses.
Learn robotic grasping from reconstructed hand-object pose sequences.
Leverage large frozen foundation backbones for hand-object reconstruction.
restrictive_assumptions: ARCTIC task assumes a known articulated object model (template)
Known camera intrinsics and extrinsics provided at test time
Single RGB image input for ARCTIC methods (no temporal modelling)
Monochrome multi-view headset images for AssemblyHands
Best AssemblyHands method uses offline Savitzky-Golay smoothing over full sequences

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best method JHands reaches 12.21 mm overall but 16.27 mm on 'inspect'; baseline 20.69 mm.
Best CDev 32.56 mm (JointTransformer) versus 27.97 mm allocentric; contact remains centimetres off.
Best object success rate 74.07% egocentric; baseline ArcticNet-SF 53.89%.
JointTransformer with ViT-G still has 29.0 mm contact deviation.

open_problems_listed: Fast hand motion
Object reconstruction from narrow and moving egocentric views
Close contact between two hands and objects
Egocentric camera distortion near image edges
Object occlusion by hands and arms and objects at image boundaries
High diversity of camera-view object 6D poses in egocentric video
Uneven multi-view sample distribution in headset cameras
Efficient multi-view egocentric training
3D foundation priors for template-free hand-object reconstruction
More expressive representations (heatmap-based)
Temporal and motion modelling
More diverse egocentric interaction scenarios
Action recognition from hand poses
Robot grasp learning from reconstructed sequences
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet reconstruct objects and hand-object contact accurately from moving egocentric views under fast motion and close bimanual contact.

papers.title: Dense Hand-Object(HO) GraspNet with Full Grasping Taxonomy and Dynamics
papers.problem_statement: Existing 3D hand-object datasets are limited in data cardinality, interaction variation or annotation quality; e.g. HO3D and DexYCB cover only 15 and 14 of 33 grasp taxonomies, and the only full-taxonomy benchmark is synthetic.

stated_limitations.text: Compound and articulated objects are treated as rigid; articulation not annotated.
stated_limitations.quote: We aimed to incorporate various compound and articulated objects to capture dynamic actions. However, we currently treat them as rigid objects.

stated_limitations.text: No non-grasping actions or deformable objects.
stated_limitations.quote: the dataset can be improved by including non-grasping actions such as pushing, throwing, squeezing, or deforming non-rigid objects like plastic bottles and sponges

stated_limitations.text: Smaller object set than MOW and OakInk.
stated_limitations.quote: Compared to the existing benchmarks (MOW [6] and OakInk [84]), we have a relatively smaller set of objects.

stated_limitations.text: Object markers can constrain hand poses.
stated_limitations.quote: markers on objects can still limit hand poses, so we minimized this impact by placing markers on regions least likely to be grasped

stated_limitations.text: Single right-hand grasps only.
stated_limitations.quote: participants were requested to grasp each object with their right hand according to the specified grasp

stated_limitations.text: Initial keypoints are noisy under high hand-object occlusion.
stated_limitations.quote: such keypoint estimates may be noisy for viewpoints with high hand-object occlusion.

stated_limitations.text: HALO captures less hand shape variation than MANO.
stated_limitations.quote: HALO is shown to capture less hand shape variation than MANO

failure_modes: Dice object pose fails (ADD-0.1D 2.44) because small visible regions under hand occlusion make the task ill-posed.
Larger objects with more occlusion show higher hand pose errors.
Three of the top four highest-error grasp classes are absent from DexYCB and HO3D, so models trained on them struggle.
Thin or small objects score low ADD-0.1D (small_marker 28.29, credit_card 34.06, knife 38.17).
future_work: Add object articulation annotations.
Include non-grasping actions (pushing, throwing, squeezing) and deformable objects.
Synthetic augmentation of object textures, shapes beyond grasp areas, and backgrounds.
Provide environments for learning grasping agents in physical simulators.
Transfer learned knowledge to human-object or other interactions.
restrictive_assumptions: Pre-scanned object meshes and optical mocap markers on objects
Four static, calibrated Azure Kinect RGB-D cameras in a studio
Single right hand per grasp
Objects treated as rigid
Manual LED-based synchronization; frames downsampled to 10 fps

benchmark_gaps.observation: Dice 2.44, small_marker 28.29, credit_card 34.06 with HFL-Net.
HFL-Net trained on HOGraspNet gets 42.65 / 9.36 mm on DexYCB; trained on HO3D gets 57.31 / 10.31 mm.
Mean 5.67 mm, but errors highest for grasp classes missing from existing datasets.

open_problems_listed: Annotation of articulated and compound object articulation
Non-grasping actions (pushing, throwing, squeezing)
Deformable, non-rigid objects
Synthetic augmentation beyond grasp areas
Simulation environments for grasp-agent learning
Extension to human-object and human-human interaction
Small heavily occluded objects remain ill-posed for pose estimation
papers.field_cannot_yet: Hand-object pose estimation is not yet robust across the full grasp taxonomy for small, heavily occluded, articulated or deformable objects.

papers.title: Are Synthetic Data Useful for Egocentric Hand-Object Interaction Detection?
papers.problem_statement: Egocentric hand-object interaction detection depends on large amounts of expensive annotated real data, and the use of synthetic data is under-explored because photorealistic generation of hands, objects and contact is difficult.

stated_limitations.text: Synthetic data cannot replace real data.
stated_limitations.quote: synthetic data cannot yet entirely replace real data for egocentric hand-object interaction detection, with synthetic-only baselines achieving poor results in all scenarios.

stated_limitations.text: A large synth-to-real gap of about 30-40% AP persists.
stated_limitations.quote: a domain gap between synthetic and real data still exists, with models trained only on synthetic data lagging behind models trained on real data by large margins

stated_limitations.text: Gap attributed to photorealism, grasp accuracy and limited diversity.
stated_limitations.quote: which we attribute to limits in photorealism, accuracy of grasping, and diversity of environments and objects

stated_limitations.text: Benefit of synthetic data shrinks as real labels increase.
stated_limitations.quote: the performance gap diminishes as the quantity of real data increases

stated_limitations.text: In-domain synthetic data helps little when some real labels exist.
stated_limitations.quote: advantages of in-domain synthetic data are limited if few real labeled data are available for semi-supervised adaptation.

stated_limitations.text: Domain adaptation models limited to batch size 4.
stated_limitations.quote: we adopted a batch size of 4, the largest batch size achievable with domain adaptation models in our configuration.

failure_modes: Synthetic-only training on VISOR gives Overall AP 9.88 versus 45.33 for real-only.
Out-domain synthetic data on ENIGMA-51 gives Overall AP 0.21 without real data.
Active object segmentation stays weak: Object Mask AP about 24-28 on VISOR even fully supervised.
No single domain adaptation method wins all breakdown metrics.
future_work: Use the released simulator and generation pipeline to support further research on synthetic data for egocentric vision.
restrictive_assumptions: 2D detection and segmentation only (no 3D pose)
Static grasps sampled from DexGraspNet; single frames, no motion
In-domain generation requires 3D models of the target environment and objects
Unity rendering in HM3D environments

benchmark_gaps.observation: Synthetic-only 9.88; UDA 33.33; best fully supervised 46.48.
Fully supervised Object AP 24.03-27.77, far below Hand AP of about 92.
Synthetic-only 7.16; best fully supervised 39.61.
Out-domain synthetic-only 0.21; in-domain synthetic-only 12.85.

open_problems_listed: Synth-to-real domain gap of about 30-40% AP
Photorealism of generated hand-object images
Accuracy of synthesized grasps
Diversity of environments and objects in synthetic data
Synthetic data cannot replace real labeled data
Scale of synthetic data needed (plateau at 22k-30k images on VISOR)
Value of in-domain versus out-domain synthetic data
Domain adaptation methods do not dominate all breakdown metrics
papers.field_cannot_yet: Egocentric hand-object detectors cannot yet be trained from synthetic data alone, and active-object segmentation remains weak even with full real supervision.

papers.title: 3D Hand Sequence Recovery from Real Blurry Images and Event Stream
papers.problem_statement: 3D hand recovery methods disregard motion blur, and no dataset pairs real motion-blurred hand images with accurate 3D ground truth; synthetic blur (BlurHand) has a domain gap and images alone are temporally ambiguous.

stated_limitations.text: Ten subjects only; shape diversity may be lacking.
stated_limitations.quote: since our data were captured from 10 individuals, it may lack shape diversity.

stated_limitations.text: Event-only input fails on static hands.
stated_limitations.quote: events lack information for static hands, leading to a failure in recovering 3D hands.

stated_limitations.text: A blurry image is temporally ambiguous.
stated_limitations.quote: a single blurry image can exhibit multiple potential motion trajectories, leading to temporal ambiguity.

stated_limitations.text: Deblurring before recovery does not work.
stated_limitations.quote: even advanced deblurring networks struggle to restore sharp hand images from blurry ones.

stated_limitations.text: 3D ground truth is produced by a self-supervised network annotator, not mocap.
stated_limitations.quote: we train a MANO parameter estimation network on our dataset and test it on the training set, where the output becomes the 3D ground truth.

failure_modes: Event-only EBHNet MPJPE about 28.6-30.8 mm versus 12.0-16.4 mm with image plus events.
Image-only training must resolve forward/reverse temporal ambiguity by taking the smaller of two losses.
Pose2Pose and I2L-MeshNet fail to capture hand pose under blur; BlurHandNet outputs nearly identical hands across time steps.
Error increases toward the end of the exposure (t=0.8: 16.35 mm with image and events).
future_work: Design additional modules for hand shape generalization.
Construct a larger-scale dataset from more people.
restrictive_assumptions: Lab capture with seven synchronized Kinects plus a calibrated, trigger-synchronized event camera
Hand gestures without object interaction
Root-aligned metrics; absolute hand position not evaluated
Pseudo ground truth from a network annotator trained on the same data
80 ms exposure blur setting

benchmark_gaps.observation: Event-only methods: EventHands 28.80-30.97, EBHNet 28.59-30.80.
Image plus events at unseen t=1.0 reaches 16.76 mm.
Best image-only EBHNet 16.45-17.23 mm; I2L-MeshNet 24.32 mm at mid step.

open_problems_listed: Research gap on fast-moving hands despite prevalence
Domain gap between synthetic and real motion blur
Temporal ambiguity of blurry single images
Event data lacks information for static hands
Limited hand shape diversity in real blur datasets
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet recover accurate 3D hand sequences from real motion-blurred RGB alone, without an auxiliary event sensor, across diverse hand shapes.

papers.title: F-HOI: Toward Fine-grained Semantic-Aligned 3D Human-Object Interactions
papers.problem_statement: Existing 3D HOI datasets and models only align global descriptions with long HOI sequences, lacking detailed understanding of intermediate HOI states and the transitions between them.

stated_limitations.text: Tasks require 3D object mesh, 3D HOI pose and text as input.
stated_limitations.quote: These input requirements significantly hurt the convenience of inference.

stated_limitations.text: Closed-set only; no open-set generalization.
stated_limitations.quote: such a model lacks generalization to open-set scenarios, which is limited by interaction diversity and unseen object meshes.

stated_limitations.text: State-by-state sequence generation accumulates error and lacks smooth transitions.
stated_limitations.quote: This approach introduces complexity and error accumulation, and it does not address the issue of smooth transitions between states.

stated_limitations.text: May underperform prior methods on generation and reconstruction.
stated_limitations.quote: It may perform poorly compared to previous methods [12, 69, 87, 89] in generation and reconstruction tasks.

stated_limitations.text: Hand detail poorly captured.
stated_limitations.quote: our preliminary results indicate that our model underperforms in capturing the details of the hands.

stated_limitations.text: LLM-based understanding and reasoning errors.
stated_limitations.quote: several understanding and reasoning errors, such as inaccurate judgments of interactions and incorrect assessments of the spatial relationships between body parts.

stated_limitations.text: Direct object pose output from images is too hard; reconstruction is object-conditioned.
stated_limitations.quote: directly outputting the object pose is challenging. We perform object-conditioned human reconstruction

failure_modes: Interpenetration persists when human actions conflict with objects.
Physics gap: generated states ignore gravity, e.g. a keyboard floats without contact.
Fails to generate the next state when the object trajectory is complex or highly variable, due to too few long complex movements in the data.
future_work: Reduce required input modalities, e.g. object meshes via text-to-3D and HOI pose from image-based estimators.
Increase data scale by merging more HOI datasets and enriching text.
Explore hierarchy of body-part states, object states and actions.
Explore lighter model architectures as data scales.
restrictive_assumptions: Known 3D object mesh as input
Object pose given for reconstruction (object-conditioned)
Average body shape (beta set to zero)
Fine-grained text generated by GPT-4V from images
Closed-set evaluation on GRAB, CHAIRS and BEHAVE
Large MLLM (Vicuna-7B) trained on 8 A100 GPUs

benchmark_gaps.observation: Authors report the model underperforms in capturing hand details; no hand parameters predicted.

open_problems_listed: Reducing strict input modality requirements (mesh, HOI pose, text)
Open-set generalization to unseen objects and interactions
Smooth transitions and error accumulation in state-by-state generation
Hand-detail modelling
LLM reasoning errors on interactions and spatial relations
Interpenetration and lack of physical constraints
Complex, long object trajectories
Data scale and richer text
Lightweight architectures
papers.field_cannot_yet: Models cannot yet recover full HOI states (object pose and hand detail) from images with physically plausible contact while aligning to fine-grained language.

papers.title: HIMO: A New Benchmark for Full-Body Human Interacting with Multiple Objects
papers.problem_statement: Existing HOI datasets and models are limited to a human interacting with a single object, neglecting ubiquitous multi-object manipulation; no full-body multi-object 4D HOI dataset with detailed text exists.

stated_limitations.text: No large objects.
stated_limitations.quote: Our HIMO dataset is built mainly based on small household objects, without human interacting with large objects such as chairs and suitcases.

stated_limitations.text: RGB appearance unnatural due to mocap suits and markers.
stated_limitations.quote: the human and object appearances are unnatural since humans are wearing tight MoCap suits and objects are attached with reflective markers.

stated_limitations.text: Facial expressions ignored.
stated_limitations.quote: We neglect the facial expressions since our dataset mainly focuses on the manipulation of multiple objects

stated_limitations.text: 4D HOI capture is hard.
stated_limitations.quote: Capturing 4D HOIs is challenging due to the subtle finger motions, severe occlusions, and precise tracking of various objects.

stated_limitations.text: Naive dual-branch generation misaligns motions and produces implausible contacts.
stated_limitations.quote: the generated human motion and object motions could be spatio-temporally misaligned. Second, implausible contacts between human-object and object-object are commonly encountered.

failure_modes: Removing the mutual interaction module causes a large R-precision drop.
Generating human motion conditioned on generated object motion causes a large performance drop.
Conditioning on 20 past frames gives no gain over 10 in auto-regressive segment generation.
On the 3-object partition the method beats baselines only on R-precision and MM-Dist, not all metrics.
future_work: No explicit future-work section; the stated limitations name large objects, natural RGB appearance and facial expressions as uncovered.
restrictive_assumptions: Optical mocap with 20 infrared cameras and 41-marker suits plus inertial gloves
3D-printed objects with known geometry and attached reflective markers
Objects on a 74 cm table; 2 or 3 small household objects per sequence
Generation conditioned on known initial human and object states and object geometry

benchmark_gaps.observation: Proposed method outperforms baselines only on R-precision and MM-Dist in the 3-object setting.

open_problems_listed: Interaction with large objects
Natural RGB appearance without suits and markers
Facial expressions
Spatio-temporal alignment between generated human and object motions
Implausible human-object and object-object contacts
Smooth transitions between generated HOI segments
Subtle finger motion capture under severe occlusion
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet capture or synthesize multi-object full-body interactions with natural, marker-free appearance and large objects.

papers.title: Revisit Human-Scene Interaction via Space Occupancy
papers.fulltext_source: https://arxiv.org/html/2312.02700 (arXiv id found via export.arxiv.org API)
papers.problem_statement: Human-scene interaction generation is held back by limited data scale: simultaneous capture of humans and 3D scenes is expensive, so paired datasets (e.g. PROX, 60 clips) have limited diversity and complexity.

stated_limitations.text: In dynamic scenes the controller can produce slight collisions, attributed to a gap in occupancy change rate between training (human motion only) and test scenes (moving occupancy).
stated_limitations.quote: when interacting with dynamic scenes, our controller could perform sub-optimally with slight collisions.

stated_limitations.text: Foot sliding artifacts occur, and the foot-sliding metric is a simple heuristic that differs from real foot sliding.
stated_limitations.quote: foot sliding is another artifact that could happen. However, the metrics are based on simple heuristics with gaps compared to real foot sliding.

stated_limitations.text: MOB focuses on static HSI; the space-occupancy view of human-object interaction is left unexplored.
stated_limitations.quote: the current MOB poses its main focus on static HSI.

stated_limitations.text: The controller only accepts target poses, space occupancy and joint trajectories as control signals.
stated_limitations.quote: the proposed versatile controller only accepts target poses, space occupancy, and joint trajectories as control signals.

stated_limitations.text: Failure cases: turning around in narrow space, and keeping arms at a proper height to pass through narrow gaps.
stated_limitations.quote: Our method could be challenged when turning around in a narrow space is required

failure_modes: Slight collisions in dynamic scenes where occupancy moves independently of the human
Turning around in a narrow space
Controlling upper-limb height in strictly restricted space (arms fail to fit through narrow gaps)
Foot sliding (8.13% of frames vs 3.36% for ground truth on MOB), traded off against penetration avoidance
