papers.title: XYZ-IBD: Benchmarking Robust 6D Object Pose Estimation under Real-World Industrial Complexity
papers.problem_statement: 6D pose benchmarks are near saturation on household objects but miss industrial complexity: reflective, texture-less, symmetric parts in dense stochastic stacks, and existing industrial datasets inherit depth-sensor bias on specular surfaces.

stated_limitations.text: Commodity depth sensing breaks down on specular metal, so the dataset needs anti-reflection spray to obtain ground truth.
stated_limitations.quote: Standard depth sensors suffer from severe noise and geometric distortion on specular surfaces

stated_limitations.text: All benchmarked methods struggle on the dataset.
stated_limitations.quote: As shown in Table 4, all methods struggle on our dataset.

stated_limitations.text: Seen-object methods trained on synthetic data fail on real scenes.
stated_limitations.quote: both GDRNet and SurfEmb, representing seen object methods, fail to predict accurate poses, despite being trained on synthetic data.

stated_limitations.text: Unseen-object methods depend on an upstream segmentation or detection prior.
stated_limitations.quote: Unseen object methods assume the availability of object segmentation or detection as a prior for pose estimation.

stated_limitations.text: Object categories and conditions are limited; expansion left to future work.
stated_limitations.quote: Potential future work lies to expand the scale of object categories and working conditions

failure_modes: Unseen-object 2D detection degrades sharply under heavy occlusion, repeated instances and strong reflections (SAM6D drops more than 33% AP on average).
Seen-object 6D methods trained on synthetic bin-picking data fail on real test scenes (GDRN 0.266 AP).
Detections are assigned wrong object IDs in dense multi-instance scenes (Figure 10 red boxes).
Centimeter-level errors acceptable for household objects cause grasp failure under industrial sub-millimeter tolerance.
future_work: Expand object categories and working conditions.
Cover more typical but challenging vision tasks for evaluating foundational industrial solutions.
restrictive_assumptions: CAD models of every part (micron-level accuracy) are available.
Ground truth needs temporary anti-reflective coating and robot-arm repeated viewpoints (FANUC, 0.06 mm repeatability) over 50 calibrated views.
Static bins of rigid objects; no hands or manipulation in the scenes.
Seen-object baselines trained only on synthetic data.
Unseen-object 6D baselines use SAM-6D masks as given segmentation prior.

benchmark_gaps.observation: GDRN 0.827 on BOP-Core5 falls to 0.266; SurfEmb 0.758 to 0.247.
Best SAM6D 0.578, FoundationPose 0.564, MatchU 0.529, below their BOP-Core5 scores (0.70-0.73).
CNOS 0.275, SAM-6D 0.296, NIDS-Net 0.258, versus 0.36-0.49 on BOP-Core5.

open_problems_listed: Household benchmarks are near saturation and do not reflect industrial complexity.
Highly reflective, texture-less, geometrically symmetric parts.
High-density stochastic stacking with multi-instance ambiguity and heavy occlusion.
Accurate ground truth for specular objects; depth sensors are biased on specular surfaces.
Sub-millimeter accuracy required for industrial grasping.
Sim-to-real gap for methods trained on synthetic data.
Dependence of unseen-object pose estimation on segmentation priors.
Expanding object categories and working conditions.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet estimate 6D pose of reflective, symmetric, densely stacked rigid objects with the sub-millimeter reliability manipulation needs.

papers.title: MessyKitchens: Contact-rich object-level 3D scene reconstruction
papers.problem_statement: Decomposing real cluttered scenes into physically plausible individual 3D objects remains hard; existing benchmarks have limited registration accuracy and inter-object penetration, and single-object methods ignore inter-object relations.

stated_limitations.text: Object-level scene decomposition is hard due to variety, occlusion and object relations.
stated_limitations.quote: reconstructing and decomposing common scenes into individual 3D objects remains a hard challenge due to the large variety of objects, frequent occlusions and complex object relations.

stated_limitations.text: Prior benchmarks have inaccurate registration and penetrations.
stated_limitations.quote: their 3D ground truth often suffers from the limited registration accuracy and inter-object penetrations.

stated_limitations.text: SAM 3D treats objects independently, giving inconsistent layouts.
stated_limitations.quote: because SAM 3D typically processes objects as independent tokens, it lacks explicit, end-to-end reasoning regarding the spatial inter-dependencies between multiple objects.

stated_limitations.text: MOD corrects only pose and scale; geometry comes unchanged from SAM 3D.
stated_limitations.quote: Multi-Object Decoder builds on these predictions by refining only the pose and scale of the detected objects, leaving their geometry unchanged.

stated_limitations.text: Evaluation requires Sim(3) ICP alignment because predictions are not in the ground-truth frame.
stated_limitations.quote: As predicted 3D reconstructions and ground-truth scenes may not share a common coordinate frame, we perform scene-level alignment using Sim(3) ICP.

failure_modes: PartCrafter and MIDI produce incomplete or geometrically inconsistent reconstructions on real scenes.
SAM 3D baseline yields inter-object penetrations and unstable floating poses.
Distance-only registration of thin concave objects places the scan between the object's walls; needs normal-aware term.
Absolute object-level IoU stays below 0.45 on all four benchmarks even for the best method.
future_work: Paper states MessyKitchens and MOD should support future physics-consistent 3D vision for robotic manipulation, VR and animation; no specific future work listed.
restrictive_assumptions: Single RGB image input with object segmentation masks from SAM 3.
Static, rigid tabletop kitchenware scenes without hands or dynamics.
MOD trained only on synthetic scenes built from 42 GSO objects.
Ground truth needs pre-scanned object meshes (6-10 min each) and scene scans (up to 20 min) with manual coarse alignment.
Evaluation aligns prediction to ground truth with Sim(3) ICP, best of three runs.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best MOD 0.445; SAM 3D 0.409; PartCrafter 0.071, MIDI 0.186.
MOD 0.340 vs SAM 3D 0.328 on the out-of-distribution high-clutter set.
Best MOD 66.1; SAM 3D 55.8; PartCrafter 21.2.

open_problems_listed: Large variety of object shapes and frequent occlusions in object-level scene reconstruction.
Physically plausible reconstruction: non-penetration, correct contacts, deformations and other physical parameters.
Existing benchmarks: limited annotation and registration accuracy, inaccurate contacts, insufficient scene complexity, or poor scalability (mocap or robot-based capture).
Generative scene methods (MIDI, PartCrafter) trained on synthetic data fail to generalize to real captures.
Retrieval and feed-forward methods limited by scarce 3D supervision and database diversity.
Single-object reconstruction lacks reasoning about inter-object spatial dependencies.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet reconstruct cluttered real scenes from a single image into accurate, contact-consistent object-level 3D without penetrations or floating objects.

papers.title: emg2pose: A Large and Diverse Benchmark for Surface Electromyographic Hand Pose Estimation
papers.problem_statement: Vision hand tracking struggles with occlusion, field of view and lighting; wrist sEMG avoids these but depends on anatomy and sensor placement, and existing datasets lack scale to learn generalizing sEMG-to-pose models.

stated_limitations.text: sEMG models remain less accurate than vision methods.
stated_limitations.quote: our models obtain mean landmark distance errors that are higher than reported in the CV literature

stated_limitations.text: Predictions can be physically infeasible and metrics do not capture plausibility.
stated_limitations.quote: we have observed that vemg2pose sometimes predicts unfeasible kinematics, such as intra-finger penetration.

stated_limitations.text: Test sets omit real-world signal aggressors.
stated_limitations.quote: it does not cover a potential range of signal aggressors such as: electrode-skin contact artifacts; impedance changes from sweat; electrical interference from external devices

stated_limitations.text: Mocap labels suffer occlusion and lose frames.
stated_limitations.quote: The IK solver failed for 12.7% of frames, typically due to simultaneously occluded markers.

stated_limitations.text: No wrist motion is recorded.
stated_limitations.quote: We additionally do not track wrist movements, which are important for how we interact with the world.

stated_limitations.text: Hardware access limits human-in-the-loop testing.
stated_limitations.quote: the lack of broader access to the sEMG-RD wrist-band (CTRL-labs at Reality Labs et al., 2024) might be limiting, as this precludes human-in-the-loop testing of models.

failure_modes: Angular drift because sEMG relates to pose derivatives (velocity integration).
Movements driven by hard-to-sense intrinsic hand muscles, e.g., finger abduction/adduction in the vulcan gesture.
Pinky and distal joints poorly predicted due to smaller and fewer muscles.
Stages with complex poses and dynamic individual-finger articulation (Gesture2, Pointing) have higher error.
Accuracy degrades most for held-out user plus held-out stage combinations and varies strongly across users.
future_work: Explore state space and diffusion-based sequence models.
Probabilistic methods for uncertainty from sensor noise and anatomy.
Model personalization.
Metrics for physical plausibility; use hand simulators to enforce physical constraints.
Correct bias from default hand model in landmark metrics.
Include signal aggressors (sweat, artifacts, interference, fatigue) in future datasets.
Combine camera and sEMG sensors for occlusion cases; alternative labelling such as stretch-sensing gloves.
restrictive_assumptions: Labels from a 26-camera marker mocap rig in a lab; participants stand in the capture array.
Proprietary sEMG-RD wristband not broadly available.
Tracking task requires the ground-truth initial hand pose.
Wrist does not move and wrist angles are not estimated.
Landmarks derived from joint angles via a default hand model, not user anatomy.
Prompted gesture stages rather than free object manipulation for most data.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best vemg2pose 21.6 mm and 15.8 deg; SensingDynamics 27.2 mm.
vemg2pose 15.2 mm even with ground-truth initial pose, vs 10.3 mm for held-out users only.

open_problems_listed: Generalization across users, sensor placements and kinematics; sEMG models are data-hungry.
sEMG encodes muscle activity closer to motion than pose, making direct pose regression partially observable.
Accuracy gap to computer-vision hand pose estimation.
Physical plausibility of predictions and metrics capturing it.
Bias of default hand model in landmark metrics.
Real-world signal aggressors: electrode-skin artifacts, sweat, interference, muscle fatigue.
Mocap labels degraded by occlusion (e.g., fist clenching); wrist movement not tracked.
Dataset smaller than proprietary ones, may limit generalization.
Limited access to sEMG hardware prevents human-in-the-loop testing.
Fusing camera and sEMG where camera tracking fails.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet infer accurate, physically plausible hand pose from wearable non-visual sensing that generalizes to new users and movements without an initial pose.

papers.title: A Benchmark Dataset for Event-Guided Human Pose Estimation and Tracking in Extreme Conditions
papers.problem_statement: Pose estimation and tracking datasets cover only well-lit, blur-free scenes; real low-light and motion-blur multi-person data with accurate annotation and event data do not exist.

stated_limitations.text: Only a simple fusion baseline is offered; better fusion is left open.
stated_limitations.quote: we propose a simple multi-modal fusion baselines. However, for tasks such as human pose estimation, more sophisticated modality fusion methods may be more effective.

stated_limitations.text: Annotating poses directly on degraded frames is unreliable, requiring a sharp reference camera.
stated_limitations.quote: annotating accurate poses on images degraded by such blur is extremely challenging and, in severe cases, may be impossible.

stated_limitations.text: RGB-only tracking misses people in extreme conditions.
stated_limitations.quote: using only RGB data leads to relatively low false positive (FP), but significantly higher false negative (FN).

stated_limitations.text: Adding events raises false positives.
stated_limitations.quote: integrating event data reduces the occurrence of missed detection, although it may introduce problems with false positives.

failure_modes: RGB-only methods misinterpret low-light plus heavy-blur scenes, giving many false-positive persons (Figure 8).
OC-SORT performs poorly because large motion displacement makes distant frames uninformative.
Identity preservation is weak: IDF1 at most 22.72 and IDSW increases with event fusion.
future_work: Explore more sophisticated RGB-event fusion methods for pose estimation.
restrictive_assumptions: Custom triplet camera rig with two beam splitters and hardware-synchronized trigger to obtain sharp reference frames.
Low light created deliberately with ND filters and aperture adjustment; blur via 16x exposure.
2D keypoints only (14 joints), no 3D.
Bottom-up pose models and tracking-by-detection evaluated after training on this dataset.

benchmark_gaps.observation: RGB-only 22.7-25.1; best RGB+event (DEKR, proposed fusion) 37.3.
Best MOTA 47.37 (ByteTrack, RGB+event); IDF1 at most 22.72; RGB-only MOTA 33.19.

open_problems_listed: Existing pose and tracking datasets cover only well-lit, blur-free conditions.
Low-light human datasets are small and hard to collect due to privacy and annotation difficulty.
Synthetic blur differs from real blur; real-blur annotation is very hard.
No prior event-based multi-person pose or multi-object tracking dataset.
Better RGB-event fusion methods.
Trade-off between missed detections (RGB) and false positives (events) in tracking.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet track multiple people's poses with stable identities under real low light and heavy motion blur.

papers.title: Pedestrian-Centric 3D Pre-collision Pose and Shape Estimation from Dashcam Perspective
papers.problem_statement: Pose models trained on daily-activity datasets are not robust to pedestrian pre-collision poses, and in-the-wild 3D pose data of collisions are scarce, available only from dashcam or surveillance video.

stated_limitations.text: Small dataset lacking camera and scene metadata.
stated_limitations.quote: the dataset is small in size and lacks real camera parameters, vehicle speed information, global position and direction of pedestrians.

stated_limitations.text: Two-stage design propagates 2D errors.
stated_limitations.quote: the final pose error is largely influenced by the 2D pose estimation results from the first stage.

stated_limitations.text: Not real-time; needs pre-selected boxes.
stated_limitations.quote: Our method is not real-time at present, because our input is Image and pre-selected Bbox sequence of collision pedestrian targets.

stated_limitations.text: No 3D scene layout, so absolute errors are large.
stated_limitations.quote: Because the PVCP dataset contains only pose and shape annotations, there is a lack of spatial arrangement in the 3D scene.

stated_limitations.text: True in-the-wild 3D ground truth is infeasible.
stated_limitations.quote: acquiring ground truth (GT) 3D joint positions in-the-wild is nearly impossible

failure_modes: Missed 2D keypoints from lower-limb occlusion propagate into mesh regression.
Models trained on COCO or 3DPW without PVCP fine-tuning perform poorly on pre-collision poses.
Non-aligned errors remain large (MPVE 257.75 mm) because global position is not recovered.
future_work: Improve one-stage image-to-mesh methods (PARE-like).
Add more modalities to improve accuracy.
Support accident reconstruction, injury assessment and vehicle structural design.
restrictive_assumptions: Pre-selected bounding-box sequences of the colliding pedestrian.
Offline processing of monocular dashcam video.
3D labels are semi-automatic pseudo ground truth from existing estimators corrected with an SMPL annotation tool, not measured 3D.
No camera intrinsics or global trajectory.

benchmark_gaps.observation: PPSENet MPVE 257.75, MPJPE_14j 218.61; one-stage PARE has lower MPJPE_14j (191.97).
VIBE with official weights reaches 849.09 mm, showing poor transfer of generic models.

open_problems_listed: Scarce in-the-wild data of pre-collision poses; dashcam or surveillance the only source.
No real 3D ground truth in the wild.
Missing camera parameters, vehicle speed, global pedestrian position and direction.
Lower-limb occlusion and dynamic backgrounds.
Generic pose datasets do not transfer to emergency poses.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet recover metrically grounded 3D human pose and global position from uncalibrated in-the-wild monocular video of rare dynamic events.

papers.title: Muscles in Time: Learning to Understand Human Motion In-Depth by Simulating Muscle Activations
papers.problem_statement: Ground-truth muscle activation data are scarce because EMG capture is resource intensive and datasets are small; vision models see only surface motion, not the muscles driving it.

stated_limitations.text: Simulated data carry an unavoidable sim-to-real gap.
stated_limitations.quote: MinT is a simulation dataset, and despite careful design of our pipeline and rigorous data analysis, a synthetic-to-real domain gap remains inevitable.

stated_limitations.text: Object interactions mostly excluded for lack of reaction forces.
stated_limitations.quote: the dataset is mostly restricted to motion types limited to foot-ground contact alone; motions with environment contact by other body parts or interactions with external objects were mostly excluded

stated_limitations.text: Included object motions assume weightless objects.
stated_limitations.quote: Since we miss information about object mass, we assume interaction with very small, lightweight objects of negligible weight in these cases.

stated_limitations.text: Discarded non-converging simulations bias category distribution.
stated_limitations.quote: This potentially creates a category distribution shift in comparison to AMASS, since some motion categories might generally be harder to simulate.

stated_limitations.text: Generic musculoskeletal models, not subject-specific.
stated_limitations.quote: providing simulation results for standard models rather than subject-specific human bodies.

failure_modes: Simulations fail to converge on complex movements; long sequences have gaps from failing segments.
Predicted activations underestimate peaks.
Rarely activated small muscles make RMSE misleadingly low and SMAPE high (upper body SMAPE above 100).
future_work: Validate models trained on MinT with real-world experiments.
Use muscle activation data to enhance human motion understanding models.
restrictive_assumptions: Input motion from marker-based mocap (AMASS subsets) converted to SMPL.
Generic validated OpenSim models; height and weight approximated from SMPL shape.
Ground reaction forces estimated, no measured external or object forces.
Manual subject-specific marker adjustments (semi-automatic pipeline).
Offline, compute-intensive simulation.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best transformer PCC 0.54; VQ-VAE 0.40.
Best transformer SMAPE 107.7 and PCC 0.55.

open_problems_listed: Scarcity of real EMG and muscle activation data.
Sim-to-real gap of simulated muscle activations.
Lack of reaction forces for non-foot contact and object interaction.
Unknown object mass in manipulation motions.
Simulation non-convergence and compute cost.
Unequal ethnicity and body-weight representation.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet estimate muscle activations for whole-body motion involving object interaction with unknown external forces.

papers.title: Text to Blind Motion
papers.problem_statement: Existing 3D human motion datasets lack diversity and are biased toward sighted people; no 3D motion dataset includes people with disabilities, so motion models embedded in autonomous systems cannot be assessed on blind pedestrians' distinct, uncertain motion.

stated_limitations.text: Small participant pool; more diverse participants needed to expose further biases.
stated_limitations.quote: The sample size of 11 participants, providing a dataset of 1,005 motion samples after filtering pose tracking failure cases, is representative of in-situ accessibility studies.

stated_limitations.text: Capture hardware is expensive, limiting scale.
stated_limitations.quote: Another limitation is the expensive ($6,500) motion-capture suit, which may hinder larger-scale studies.

stated_limitations.text: In-the-wild motion capture is not solved; IMU suit needs frequent recalibration and manual filtering of tracking failures.
stated_limitations.quote: Nonetheless, we emphasize that motion capture in-the-wild remains an open challenge.

stated_limitations.text: Vision-based 3D keypoint inference was unreliable in their setting; AlphaPose failed frequently.
stated_limitations.quote: vision-based inference of 3D keypoints can be unreliable in our context of multi-actor, dense scenes with frequent occlusion and interaction with objects

stated_limitations.text: Pre-training on a large general dataset gives mixed results because of bias and domain shift.
stated_limitations.quote: in practice, we find this to result in mixed results due to the introduced bias and domain shift. This also highlights a potential direction for future work.

stated_limitations.text: Rare motion scenarios remain challenging for current models.
stated_limitations.quote: Future directions include enhancing model generalizability to handle a broader array of rare motion scenarios, such as complex interactions with obstacles or varying terrain, which remain challenging for current models.

failure_modes: Text-to-motion models trained on Motion-X generate diverse but unrealistic blind motion (high FID, low R-precision).
Pre-training on Motion-X then fine-tuning on BlindWays underperforms training from scratch on arm and mobility-aid joints.
MotionGPT predicts diverse but unrealistic motion in motion-conditioned prediction (ADE 3.01 vs 0.45-0.47 for CVAE-based methods).
DLow trades accuracy for diversity (FDE rises from 0.56 to 0.59).
AlphaPose keypoint detection and lifting failed frequently on dense, occluded urban videos.
IMU suit tracking failures required manual filtering of noisy skeletons.
future_work: Collect data from a more diverse participant pool (heights, backgrounds).
Use lower-cost inertial or vision-based capture for larger studies.
Improve generalization to rare motion scenarios such as complex obstacle interactions and varying terrain.
Resolve bias and domain shift when pre-training on general motion datasets.
restrictive_assumptions: Wearable Xsens IMU suit (18 sensors, one on the mobility aid) with frequent recalibration along each route
Manual inspection to remove tracking-failure skeletons
11 participants on 8 pre-engineered routes in one urban area
Researchers following participants with chest-mounted phone; chest GoPro for egocentric video
Prediction setting of 0.5 s past motion to 9.5 s future

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best model reaches 0.060 vs 0.106 for real data; Motion-X-trained models only 0.041-0.046.
Motion-X-trained models score 11.203 (HumanML3D) and 15.002 (MotionGPT) vs 3.340 when trained on BlindWays.
Motion-X pretrain + BlindWays finetune gives worse arm FDE (0.99/1.07) than BlindWays-only (0.77/0.81).
MotionGPT ADE 3.01 vs about 0.45 for CVAE/DLow/MDN; paper calls this only an initial step.

open_problems_listed: Motion capture in the wild remains an open challenge
No 3D motion dataset includes people with disabilities; motion models do not model pedestrians with disabilities
Vision-based 3D keypoint inference unreliable in dense, occluded, object-interacting scenes
Generalization of motion-language models to rare and diverse human attributes
Pre-training on general datasets introduces bias and domain shift with mixed results
Generalization to rare motion scenarios such as obstacle interactions and varying terrain
Larger and more diverse participant pools
Lower-cost scalable capture to replace expensive mocap suits
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot reliably capture or predict atypical, object-mediated human motion (e.g., cane use) in the wild without expensive wearable mocap.

papers.title: Codec Avatar Studio: Paired Human Captures for Complete, Driveable, and Generalizable Avatars
papers.problem_statement: Building complete, driveable and generalizable photorealistic avatars needs paired captures of the same subject from high-end and lightweight devices, but such paired data is rarely available outside dedicated industrial labs, which has slowed progress.

stated_limitations.text: Release unlikely to support multi-identity relightable head decoders.
stated_limitations.quote: it will likely be hard to create multi-identity relightable head decoders with our release.

stated_limitations.text: Datasets miss the long tail of human expressivity.
stated_limitations.quote: Our datasets also fail to capture the long tail of human expressivity, such as the ability to convey sweat, tiredness, and blood flow.

stated_limitations.text: Goliath-4 has only four subjects.
stated_limitations.quote: However, its sample size is limited to four subjects, restricting the scope of this research.

stated_limitations.text: Raw data size forces lossy compression plus spatial, camera and temporal downsampling for release.
stated_limitations.quote: Compressing images is not enough, since our target release sizes would require compression parameters that would result in too low PSNR for avatar creation.

stated_limitations.text: No assets for full-body phone data.
stated_limitations.quote: no assets are provided for full body phone data in this release.

stated_limitations.text: Clothing complicates body reconstruction.
stated_limitations.quote: This represents a challenge for some reconstruction methods, since body models [32] are often created from subjects in tight-fit clothing.

failure_modes: Headset-to-avatar driving depends on pseudo ground truth; the paper calls obtaining a reliable mapping from headset images to face deformations a key challenge.
Full-resolution data (over 10 TB per dome capture, about 3 PB total) is infeasible for academic labs to store.
future_work: Higher-quality release tiers expected to become usable as storage costs fall.
Mitigations for misuse: authentication protocols, avatar watermarking, interfaces signalling avatar-generated media.
restrictive_assumptions: About 170-camera 2.4 m head dome and about 230-camera 5.5 m full-body dome
Quest Pro headset IR cameras, with an augmented 10-camera headset for ground truth
Person-specific (personalized) avatar models for relightable heads, hands and bodies
Hands captured separately (left and right) in a relightable dome; no object interaction
Released data downsampled to about 80 cameras, 7.5-15 fps, reduced resolution, AVIF compression
open_problems_listed: Paired captures are unavailable to researchers outside industrial labs
Multi-identity relightable head decoders remain hard with the release
Long tail of human expressivity (sweat, tiredness, blood flow) not captured
Converting low-quality capture (phone, full-body) into high-quality heads and hands is limited by four subjects
Clothed full-body reconstruction is hard since body models come from tight-fit clothing
Storage and distribution of petabyte-scale capture data
Reliable pseudo ground truth from headset images to face deformations
Misuse risk: impersonation and disinformation
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet build high-fidelity, generalizable full-body and hand avatars from lightweight sensors without studio-scale paired capture.

papers.title: TAPVid-3D: A Benchmark for Tracking Any Point in 3D
papers.problem_statement: Real-world TAP benchmarks only assess 2D tracking; 3D pose tracking needs known object models, and synthetic 3D tracking benchmarks have a large domain gap, so long-range 3D point tracking from monocular video had no real-world benchmark.

stated_limitations.text: Limited domain coverage and imperfect automatic annotations.
stated_limitations.quote: The three data sources in our benchmark do not cover all possible domains where users may want to infer dynamics, and automatic annotations may be imperfect

stated_limitations.text: Only solid, opaque objects are evaluated.
stated_limitations.quote: we inherit some limitations from TAP and monocular depth: we only evaluate tracking for solid, opaque objects.

stated_limitations.text: Ground-truth noise from source data: ADT misalignment, LIDAR noise, under-constrained Gaussian splats, numerical error.
stated_limitations.quote: small amounts of noise from the underlying dataset sources can cause issues in a small fraction of sequences.

stated_limitations.text: 3D tracking is far worse than 2D tracking for all baselines.
stated_limitations.quote: we find that the 3D tracking performance of our baselines are significantly lower compared to their 2D tracking abilities.

stated_limitations.text: Model-based 3D pose tracking needs known 3D models.
stated_limitations.quote: 3D pose tracking, e.g. for rigid objects [14, 34] and people [12, 49], evaluates precise motion, but requires a known 3D model of each object with articulations.

stated_limitations.text: SfM fails on dynamic content.
stated_limitations.quote: This underperformance is likely because COLMAP fails to reconstruct moving content.

failure_modes: Noisy monocular depth produces noisy 3D tracks even when 2D tracks are accurate.
Depth scale drift over time.
Inconsistent depth scale across space, so one global scale factor cannot fit all tracks.
COLMAP struggles on Panoptic Studio where moving content fills the scene.
ZoeDepth-based methods underperform on outdoor DriveTrack scenes.
TAPIR-3D outputs tracks independently, lacks scale consistency and gets poor 3D-AJ.
Flickering visibility flags in annotations (also seen in Kubric and DriveTrack).
future_work: Integrate elements of 2D tracking, monocular depth and SfM, since each has different strengths.
Use the benchmark to develop models for dynamic scene understanding and surface deformation from monocular video.
restrictive_assumptions: Monocular RGB input with scale ambiguity resolved by rescaling predictions to ground truth (global median or per-trajectory)
Ground truth from multi-sensor sources: Aria Digital Twin replicas, Waymo LIDAR plus box tracks, Panoptic Studio multi-view Gaussian reconstructions
DriveTrack ground truth assumes vehicle rigidity
Operator hands are not modelled in ADT digital replicas and are masked for visibility
Evaluation at 256x256 resolution

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best average 3D-AJ is 9.3 (CoTracker or BootsTAPIR + COLMAP) vs static baseline 4.9, while the same trackers reach 2D-AJ up to 59.1.
ZoeDepth-based methods score 5.0-5.4, near the static baseline 3.9.
COLMAP-based methods score 6.1-8.1 because moving content is not reconstructed.
Best average still only 20.6 (BootsTAPIR + COLMAP).
TAPIR-3D, trained only on synthetic video, averages 3.1, below the static baseline.

open_problems_listed: No real-world benchmark for 3D point tracking prior to this work
Synthetic 3D benchmarks have a significant domain gap
Depth noise, temporal scale drift and spatial scale inconsistency in monocular 3D tracking
SfM pipelines fail on moving content
Monocular depth struggles in complex outdoor scenes
Scale consistency across trajectories
Only solid opaque objects can be evaluated
Domain coverage is incomplete
Automatic annotations can be noisy
Biases inherited from lab participants and six US cities
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet recover metrically consistent long-range 3D point tracks from monocular video, even where 2D tracking is accurate.

papers.title: OctoNet: A Large-Scale Multi-Modal Dataset for Human Activity Understanding Grounded in Motion-Captured 3D Pose Labels
papers.problem_statement: Learning across non-visual sensing modalities (RF, IMU, thermal) is underexplored because large unified multi-modal benchmarks are lacking, hindering multi-modal fusion, cross-modal understanding and sensing foundation models.

stated_limitations.text: Mocap requires standardized garments, which attenuate thermal signals.
stated_limitations.quote: participants were required to wear standardized garments, including a hat, shirt, pants, and shoes that covered their regular clothing.

stated_limitations.text: Uniform attire reduces RGB appearance diversity.
stated_limitations.quote: the uniform attire reduces visual variability in the RGB modality, limiting diversity in appearance-based learning tasks.

stated_limitations.text: Lab-only capture.
stated_limitations.quote: all data in OctoNet were collected in laboratory environments. While this ensures high data quality, it may limit model generalization to real-world environments of varying conditions.

stated_limitations.text: LiDAR not included.
stated_limitations.quote: excludes a common modality, LiDAR, as it is uncommon to employ LiDAR for HAR applications.

stated_limitations.text: Some modalities lack established models.
stated_limitations.quote: several modalities, especially IRAs and ToF sensors, are relatively underexplored, with no well-established models available.

stated_limitations.text: Vision models collapse under scene shift.
stated_limitations.quote: RGB falls from 94.9% to 37.0% (CU) and 12.1% (CS) with Swin-T, indicating reliance on scene-specific cues.

failure_modes: RGB pose error rises to 473.9 mm MPJPE under cross-scene evaluation.

papers.title: InclusiveVidPose: Bridging the Pose Estimation Gap for Individuals with Limb Deficiencies in Video-Based Motion
papers.problem_statement: Existing HPE datasets and methods assume every person has a full set of limbs, so they cannot model missing or altered limbs, cannot predict absent joints, and fail on people with amputations, congenital limb differences or prostheses.

stated_limitations.text: Distinguishing an occluded limb from an absent limb remains ambiguous even with video and multiple annotators, adding label noise.

stated_limitations.section: Appendix F, Discussion and Future Work

stated_limitations.text: Current pose models give unreliable confidence for missing or prosthetic limbs on this data.
stated_limitations.quote: current pose models on our data sometimes give unreliable confidence for missing or prosthetic limbs

stated_limitations.text: Main benchmark is single-frame; multi-frame estimation is left to future extensions.
stated_limitations.quote: We benchmark our InclusiveVidPose dataset on a single-frame pose estimation task.

Video pose models (DCPose, DSTA) hallucinate a complete limb and pull the residual endpoint toward a typical wrist/ankle location; the temporal module then propagates the wrong configuration across frames.
Head AP around 28 due to occlusion, cropping and motion blur, and fewer head labels.
Adding COCO to training hurts small models (YOLOX-Pose-T, RTMPose-T) on people with limb differences.

restrictive_assumptions: 2D keypoints only; no 3D pose or shape.
Fixed 25-keypoint schema (17 COCO plus 8 residual endpoints); no prosthesis-tip joints.
Videos from YouTube and IPC archives; videos are not redistributed (links only).

benchmark_gaps.observation: ArmUp and ArmLow AP is almost zero for DCPose and DSTA; LegUp and LegLow AP in the low to mid teens; mean AP 43.2 (DCPose) and 43.7 (DSTA).
LiCC about 60% for many methods; DEKR and ViPNAS have good COCO AP but low LiCC.
About 28 AP for both video models.

papers.field_cannot_yet: Pose estimators cannot yet represent bodies whose skeleton differs from the fixed template, so residual limbs and prostheses are mislocalized or hallucinated as intact limbs.

No objects; free-hand gestures only.
Wrist joints not modeled.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best sEMG-to-pose 14.7 deg; two-step 16.9 deg.

open_problems_listed: Mapping sEMG to tendon control for dexterous hands.
Occlusion-robust hand tracking for labels.
Sim-to-real for tendon-driven hands.
Hand-object interaction data for EMG-based control.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Wearable hand sensing cannot yet produce validated actuation-level control for hands manipulating objects, because its labels still depend on occlusion-prone mocap and simulation.

papers.title: EgoVerse: An Egocentric Human Dataset for Robot Learning from Around the World
papers.problem_statement: Robot data is expensive to scale. Existing egocentric human datasets are one-off, static, study-specific releases, and effective human-to-robot transfer (embodiment gap, scaling behaviour) remains an open research problem.

stated_limitations.text: The study covers only human-and-robot co-training; other paradigms such as pre-training followed by fine-tuning are left for future work.
stated_limitations.quote: Our study mainly focused on human-and-robot co-training. Future work should conduct broader algorithmic exploration (e.g., pre-train and fine-tune).

stated_limitations.text: Scene and demonstrator diversity findings rest only on offline action-prediction error, not on robot rollouts.
stated_limitations.quote: the scene and demonstrator diversity experiments rely exclusively on offline metrics.

stated_limitations.text: Robot rollouts are still needed to confirm that the diversity effects carry over to robot manipulation.
stated_limitations.quote: additional robot rollouts are necessary to determine whether the observed diversity effects translate to improved generalization in robotic manipulation.

stated_limitations.text: Scaling with diverse human data works only when task- and scene-aligned human-robot data is included in training.
stated_limitations.quote: We find that positive scaling emerges only when such aligned data are included as part of training

stated_limitations.text: Co-training hurt one robot on one task, which the authors attribute to that robot's embodiment forcing a different strategy from the human one.
stated_limitations.quote: we observed a performance decrease in the bag-grocery task for Robot B, whereas Robot A and Robot C saw improvements.

failure_modes: Bag-grocery task on Robot B: performance dropped with human co-training because robot demonstrations used one gripper to prop the bag open, a strategy that differs from the two-handed human strategy.
Neither 8 h of diverse human data nor domain-aligned human data alone produced significant gains in-domain or out-of-domain.
Picking primitives failed in some parts of the workspace (object-in-container, bag-grocery).
Object handover in cup-on-saucer was difficult, especially for Robot C with a dexterous hand.
future_work: Study pre-training on heterogeneous human data followed by targeted fine-tuning on small robot or aligned data.
Exploit unaligned in-the-wild EgoVerse-I data with dense language annotations for language- or goal-conditioned policies.
Analyse how embodiment factors (gripper vs dexterous hand, sensing configuration, control parameterization) interact with types of human data.
Run robot rollouts to validate the offline diversity findings.
restrictive_assumptions: Human action is represented only by 21 3D hand keypoints per hand plus SLAM head pose; these are used as proxies for end-effector motion.
Aligned human-robot data (same task semantics and scene context) is needed to anchor transfer.
Demonstrators were told to keep hands visible, and manual quality control kept only manipulation-dense segments.
Tasks are limited to 'bounded diversity': tasks feasible for typical bimanual mobile manipulators.
Academic data relies on Project Aria glasses and Meta MPS for hand tracking and egomotion.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Performance decreased for Robot B with human co-training, while Robots A and C improved; overall gains were up to 30% elsewhere.
Diversity effects are measured only with offline action-prediction error; the paper says this does not directly measure robot performance.

open_problems_listed: Effective human-robot transfer remains open, with unresolved questions about the embodiment gap and scaling behaviour.
Most human datasets are one-off, static releases that are hard to scale or extend.

Large human activity datasets (Ego4D, HOI4D, EgoExo4D, Epic-Kitchens) lack manipulation-relevant annotations such as precise hand poses or object interactions, and include tasks beyond robot capability.
When pre-training on human data yields transferable structure, and how embodiment-specific design decisions affect transfer, is still an open question.
Methods that use weakly aligned or unaligned human data, grounded through limited aligned supervision, are needed.
Embodiment factors (kinematics, sensing, control) need deeper analysis to guide data selection, curriculum and architectures.
Offline diversity effects still need validation through robot rollouts.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet turn diverse, unaligned egocentric human data into robot policy gains without task- and scene-aligned human-robot anchor data.

papers.title: High Fidelity Capture, Reconstruction, and Transfer of Human Demonstrations for Robot-Assisted Bathing
papers.problem_statement: Collecting, understanding and transferring dynamic, contact-rich human bathing demonstrations is difficult even with modern motion and tactile sensing, and no comprehensive data shows how caregivers actually bathe people.

stated_limitations.text: Standard marker-based fitting (MoSh++) of gloved hands produces contorted fingers and hand-body gaps.
stated_limitations.quote: the process routinely produces serious artifacts such as highly contorted finger poses and major gaps of separation between the hands and body

stated_limitations.text: Closed-loop force control uses summed pressure only, not the per-taxel distribution.
stated_limitations.quote: Our closed-loop strategy, for example, is highly limited by its use of tactile pressure sums rather than the distribution over individual taxels.

stated_limitations.text: The sim-to-real gap is large because of mannequin-vs-SMPL-X and MANO-vs-robot-hand mismatches.
stated_limitations.quote: Our approach's simulation-to-reality gap is substantial.

stated_limitations.text: Compliance of the robot hand and of the reconstructed body and hand is not modelled.
stated_limitations.quote: We also do not account for compliance in the Dexkit hand, reconstructed human body, or reconstructed human hand

stated_limitations.text: The capacitive gloves cannot separate normal from shear force.
stated_limitations.quote: Our data does not differentiate between normal and shear forces.

stated_limitations.text: The system cannot be used on humans; perception is the main bottleneck, and online pose and shape estimation fast enough for live interaction does not exist.
stated_limitations.quote: no existing method achieves fully online human pose and shape estimation while maintaining the sub-frame latency required for live interaction

stated_limitations.text: The method assumes the bathed body is static, which does not hold for a human subject.
stated_limitations.quote: our current assumption of a static body will not extend to a human subject.

stated_limitations.text: Mild-pressure tactile signals fall below sensor sensitivity and are indistinguishable from noise.
stated_limitations.quote: (in multiple cases below the minimum sensitivity of 0.04 N) and thus largely indistinguishable from noise.

stated_limitations.text: Tactile data alone cannot tell which bodies are in contact or why forces change; all three channels together are needed.
stated_limitations.quote: Tactile data alone cannot determine between which bodies contact is happening or why forces change over time.

failure_modes: MoSh++ reconstruction of gloved hands: finger contortion and hand-body gaps, caused by fitting bare-skin hand shape parameters to gloved captures.
Open-loop rollouts applied much higher pressure than humans did, causing mannequin vibration and unsafe conditions.
Targeting a strict absolute pressure caused large arm oscillations.
Closed-loop control deviated from humans in absolute pressure and especially in spatial pressure distribution.
Friction-induced finger curling during wiping could make the controller drive the arm into the mannequin, risking mechanical damage.
Automatic contact-event detection was ambiguous: thumb-palm contacts came from gripping the wipe, and pressure drops could mean either lost contact or lower force.
A flexor-only tendon configuration could not reproduce all needed hand motions.
future_work: Retarget force distributions across different hand geometries and material properties.
Achieve online human pose and shape estimation with sub-frame latency so the robot can react to a moving body.
Add compliance to arm control for safe interaction with humans.
Use sensing modalities (visual, magnetic) that measure shear force.
Add extensor tendons to the soft hand.
Build a whole-body bathing system that learns directly from human demonstrations.
restrictive_assumptions: 20-camera Vicon optical motion capture with 52 body markers and 23 markers per glove.
Tactile gloves with 65 capacitive taxels; all forces are assumed normal to each taxel.
Subjects are able-bodied and seated upright on a stool; markers that block bathing are temporarily removed.
Robot transfer assumes a static mannequin body.
The human demonstration was slowed 20x (120 Hz to 6 Hz) for robot execution.
One-time calibration of hand taxel positions; SMPL-X/MANO shapes are fitted from range-of-motion tests.

benchmark_gaps.metric: contact distance between body contacts and glove taxels (cm)
benchmark_gaps.observation: Ours: median 0.536, mean 0.837, st.dev. 0.842, against MoSh++ at median 1.714 and mean 2.067; the residual error stays below 1 cm on average.

benchmark_gaps.metric: glove pressure (absolute, normalized, median per taxel)
benchmark_gaps.observation: Closed-loop pressure tracks the human signal on a normalized scale but deviates in absolute pressure and spatial distribution; open-loop pressure is significantly higher than the human signal.

open_problems_listed: No comprehensive data exists on how caregivers actually bathe people; existing systems use idealized definitions and coarse metrics.
Point, instantaneous or simple-constraint contact models cannot represent sustained bathing contact; surface- or volume-based contact models are needed.
Low-pressure tactile acquisition needs higher sensor sensitivity.
Patient movement (voluntary and reactive) must be handled; systems must account for constant body repositioning.
Distributed force control is blocked by the mismatch between human and robot hand responses; calibration-based fixes are brittle.
Normal and shear forces must be measured.
Online low-latency human pose and shape estimation is the main perception bottleneck.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet estimate human body pose and shape online, at sub-frame latency, during sustained physical contact, so robots can react to a moving person.

papers.title: A Systematic Study of Data Modalities and Strategies for Co-training Large Behavior Models for Robot Manipulation
papers.problem_statement: How different co-training data modalities and training strategies affect large behavior model performance is poorly understood; prior studies evaluate only subsets of modalities under inconsistent setups.

stated_limitations.text: The impact of vision-language data is not broken down by task type.
stated_limitations.quote: we do not systematically analyze their impact by task taxonomy
stated_limitations.section: V Discussion, Limitations, And Future Work

stated_limitations.text: Human videos are used only through coarse latent actions and language annotations, not fine-grained hand motion.
stated_limitations.quote: we explore only coarse-grained representations for human videos through latent actions and language annotations.

stated_limitations.text: Chain-of-thought exploration is limited to low-level action abstractions present in the co-training data.
stated_limitations.quote: our exploration of CoT is limited to forms naturally arising from our co-training data

stated_limitations.text: Only imitation learning is studied; world models and RL are not explored.
stated_limitations.quote: our study focuses exclusively on imitation learning

stated_limitations.text: The link between backbone vision-language ability and policy generalization is not rigorously characterized.
stated_limitations.quote: further investigation is needed to more rigorously characterize the relationship between backbone visiolinguistic understanding and policy generalization.

stated_limitations.text: No discrete-token variant, including latent actions from human video, gave statistically significant gains.
stated_limitations.quote: Discrete action tokens (including latent actions extracted from videos, FAST tokens, and action tokens learned from VQ-VAE) co-training yield no statistically significant performance improvements in our experiments.

failure_modes: Single-phase co-training with latent actions from human video gave no improvement over the baseline.
Latent-action pre-training helped only when target-robot data was scarce, and the benefit faded as robot data grew; in a data- and compute-rich setting it gave no benefit.
FAST token co-training degraded generalization to unseen tasks.
VQ-VAE token co-training slightly degraded performance under distribution shift.
Training only on robot data eroded the VLM backbone's language ability, leaving it unable to generate language.
Conditioning actions on chain-of-thought gave no benefit in simulation.
Raising the co-training loss weight or data ratio degraded in-distribution performance.
future_work: Extract fine-grained dexterous motions from human video as hand pose estimation improves.
Analyse vision-language data by task category for targeted data curation.
Use richer CoT forms such as history and reflection traces or hierarchical plans.
Study co-training under world modeling and reinforcement learning.
restrictive_assumptions: Human videos have no ground-truth actions, so action reconstruction is omitted for them.
Policies use a pretrained PaliGemma2 VLM backbone and roughly 4,000 hours of robot and human data plus 50M VL samples.
Human video annotations are generated by GPT-5 from frames sampled at 1 s intervals.
A 9:1 robot to co-training data ratio was chosen empirically.

benchmark_gaps.metric: task success under seen/unseen tasks and distribution shift
benchmark_gaps.observation: Latent actions, FAST and VQ-VAE tokens gave no statistically significant improvement; FAST lowered unseen-task success.

benchmark_gaps.dataset: VLM benchmarks (VQA, spatial and multimodal reasoning)
benchmark_gaps.observation: The no-co-training baseline lost all language generation ability and performed poorly across nearly all benchmarks.

open_problems_listed: Fine-grained dexterous motion labels from human video are not yet used as a co-training signal.
Obtaining accurate action labels from human video often needs extra sensing such as VR devices or wearable exoskeletons.
Latent-action approaches have been validated only in low target-robot-data regimes.
Which vision-language task categories drive which policy capabilities is unknown.
The relation between VLM backbone understanding and policy generalization needs rigorous characterization.
Richer CoT formulations for complex decision-making remain to be studied.
Co-training within world modeling or reinforcement learning is an open frontier.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet extract accurate, fine-grained hand action labels from large-scale human video that measurably improve generalist robot policies.

papers.title: Towards Unifying Human Likeness: Evaluating Metrics for Human-Like Motion Retargeting on Bimanual Manipulation Tasks
papers.problem_statement: Many human-likeness metrics exist, but there are no standardized criteria or guidelines for choosing among them. Many were introduced without comprehensive assessment or are evaluated through high-effort user studies, and few address bimanual motion.

stated_limitations.text: The unified metric depends on the generated retargeting dataset, which in turn depends on the chosen metrics and joint mapping.
stated_limitations.quote: the analysis and proposed unified metric is subject to the generated motion retargeting dataset, which itself depends on the design of the individual human-likeness metrics and joint mapping.

stated_limitations.text: Metric and optimizer parameters were set empirically.
stated_limitations.quote: several parameters of the unified human-likeness metric and the utilized optimization approaches were set empirically based on our analysis.

stated_limitations.text: All evaluation is on simulated robots; real-robot evaluation is planned.
stated_limitations.quote: we plan to evaluate the unified human-likeness metric and the different human-like motion retargeting approaches on real robots.

stated_limitations.text: The closed-form joint mapping does not align rotation-axis centres.
stated_limitations.quote: Although this does not perfectly align the centers of the rotation axes, it leads to a one-to-one joint mapping

stated_limitations.text: Metric correlations vary across motions and robots (MAD 0.1 and 0.126).
stated_limitations.quote: the correlation coefficients differ to a certain extent across motions and slightly more across robot models.

stated_limitations.text: Adding several criteria can hurt functional constraint satisfaction.
stated_limitations.quote: Multiple optimization criteria can also have a negative impact, particularly in terms of functional constraints.

stated_limitations.text: Unimanual metrics are applied to bimanual motion by averaging the left- and right-arm values.
stated_limitations.quote: We apply unimanual metrics to our bimanual use case by averaging the result of the unimanual metric for the left and right arm.

failure_modes: The Jacobian-based velocity IK (JV) largely underperforms the optimization IK, which the authors hypothesize is due to many difficult or unreachable end-effector poses, especially on ARMAR-III.
Minimum-jerk cost mostly worsened JV performance.
Human-likeness scores do not improve significantly on ARMAR-III.
Combining several human-likeness criteria can reduce functional scores such as pose tracking.
future_work: Extend the dataset with more humanoid robots and additional metrics to reduce inter-robot variance.
Automatically select and fine-tune metric and optimizer parameters.
Evaluate the unified metric and retargeting approaches on real robots.
restrictive_assumptions: Human motion comes from marker-based capture in the MMM reference model (KIT Bimanual Manipulation Dataset, two subjects for correlation analysis).
The one-to-one joint mapping requires kinematic structures similar to the human arm, and default poses are adjusted perceptually by hand.
Motions are mirrored to compensate for missing left-handed subjects.
Evaluation is in simulation on ARMAR-III, ARMAR-6 and a dual Panda setup.
Robot placement uses reachability maps of the human hand trajectories.

benchmark_gaps.dataset: KIT Bimanual Manipulation Dataset retargeted to 3 robots
benchmark_gaps.metric: mean absolute deviation of Spearman correlation coefficients
benchmark_gaps.observation: MAD across robots 0.126 and across motions 0.1, so metric relationships are not invariant across robots or motions.

open_problems_listed: Guidelines for choosing a human-likeness metric for a given setting are missing.
Several metrics were introduced without comprehensive assessment, or are evaluated by high-effort user studies.
Optimizing a trajectory for one metric biases evaluation with that metric.
Few human-likeness approaches address bimanual manipulation.
Learning-based retargeting still has difficulty explicitly considering task constraints.
Metrics were developed independently, without regard to transferability and compatibility.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field has no validated, robot-independent standard for scoring how human-like a retargeted bimanual robot motion is.

papers.title: TWIN: Two-handed Intelligent Benchmark for Bimanual Manipulation
papers.fulltext_source: https://arxiv.org/html/2407.00278 (PerAct2 arXiv preprint by the same authors; Semantic Scholar ICRA abstract matches; ICRA version itself not accessed)
papers.problem_statement: Real-world bimanual systems exist, but there is a lack of simulated benchmarks with large task diversity for systematically studying bimanual capabilities; real-world tasks suffer from reproducibility and variability issues.

stated_limitations.text: No method reaches a sufficiently high success rate.
stated_limitations.quote: None of the methods is able to achieve a sufficiently high success rate, which can be explained by the complexity of bimanual manipulation.

stated_limitations.text: Discretized-action methods need a sampling-based motion planner to execute.
stated_limitations.quote: methods using discretized actions rely on a sampling-based motion planner for successful execution.

stated_limitations.text: Real-world results are hard to reproduce.
stated_limitations.quote: reproducing them is challenging due to a lack of hardware as well as to object poses and sensor noise.

stated_limitations.text: Simulated cameras are idealized, without noise.
stated_limitations.quote: All cameras are noiseless

stated_limitations.text: Image-based methods confuse the two identical arms.
stated_limitations.quote: both robot arms are the exact same model making it difficult to distinguish between them.

stated_limitations.text: The real-world voxel size was coarsened for training speed at the cost of accuracy.
stated_limitations.quote: to speed up training, but reduces accuracy.

failure_modes: Handover: arms collide due to inadequate spatial awareness or timing errors.
Grasping failures from gripper misalignment.
The arm misses the object entirely in plate and tray pick-up tasks.
Put-item-in-drawer fails on the temporal dependency, for example not opening the drawer.
ACT struggles with high demonstration variance because it predicts joint angles rather than 6-DoF poses.
future_work: Add more state-of-the-art methods to the benchmark.
Extend the benchmark to mobile manipulation.
Develop more sophisticated motion planning strategies for bimanual interaction.
restrictive_assumptions: Simulation with four noiseless RGB-D cameras (front, both shoulders, wrist).
Two identical Franka Panda arms with parallel grippers.
Demonstrations generated automatically via motion planning, 100 per task, single-task training.
Real-world tests use a single Azure Kinect, one kinesthetic demonstration per task, and qualitative evaluation only.

benchmark_gaps.observation: ACT 5.9%, RVT-LF 10.5%, PerAct-LF 17.5%, PerAct2 16.8%.
All methods scored 0 to 3%.
ACT, RVT-LF and PerAct-LF scored 0%; PerAct2 11%.

benchmark_gaps.dataset: TWIN/RLBench2 pick up plate, lift tray, sweep dustpan
benchmark_gaps.observation: Plate at most 4% for any method; PerAct2 1% on tray and 0% on dustpan.

open_problems_listed: There is a lack of simulated bimanual benchmarks with large task diversity.
Real-world bimanual evaluation suffers from reproducibility and variability.
Running two separate agents is insufficient; coordination between arms is crucial.
Bimanual success rates are not sufficiently high for any current method.
More sophisticated motion planning is needed for bimanual scene interaction.
Discretized-action methods depend on sampling-based planners.
Mobile bimanual manipulation is not yet covered.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet learn tightly coordinated bimanual skills such as handovers and joint lifts with reliable success, even in noiseless simulation.

papers.title: HelmetPoser: A Helmet-Mounted IMU Dataset for Data-Driven Estimation of Human Head Motion in Diverse Conditions
papers.problem_statement: Helmet LIO and VIO localization fail under dust, smoke, darkness and low features, while IMUs drift; few datasets capture high-frequency human head motion for data-driven IMU estimation.

stated_limitations.text: IMU-only estimation suffers from accumulating drift.
stated_limitations.quote: IMUs are subject to error accumulation, where small measurement errors gradually accumulate over time, leading to increasing inaccuracies in position and orientation estimates.

stated_limitations.text: Head motion is hard to model with data-driven IMU estimation.
stated_limitations.quote: The motion patterns of the human head are highly non-linear and uncertain [8], complicating the potential of data-driven IMU motion estimation.

stated_limitations.text: Performance drops when models are transferred to a different IMU.
stated_limitations.quote: Although the performance on the VectorNav IMU shows a slight decline compared to the initial sensor

failure_modes: Cross-sensor transfer to the VectorNav IMU reduces final integration-error reduction from about 90-92% to about 53-60%.
Loss rises when training on one motion type and testing on another (for example LSTM trained on walk, tested on run: 0.067).
future_work: The dataset, metrics and baseline are released for future helmet-based localization studies; no specific future work is listed.
restrictive_assumptions: Data is collected only in a VICON-equipped laboratory, which provides ground truth.
Only three motions: walking, running and stair climbing; ten participants, three sessions of about five minutes each.
Ground-truth IMU bias is derived by pre-integration against VICON poses.
A single participant (D) serves as the validation set.

benchmark_gaps.metric: percentage reduction in final integration error
benchmark_gaps.observation: 52.55% to 60.22%, against 90.53% to 92.29% on the training sensor (Livox Mid-360 IMU).

open_problems_listed: LiDAR degrades in dust, smoke, moisture, narrow spaces and feature-poor areas such as tunnels and mines.
Visual sensors fail with low light, motion blur, occlusion or smoke, and worse under rapid, intense motion.
IMU drift makes long-term IMU-only localization problematic.
Data-driven IMU datasets come from vehicles, robots or the body; few capture high-frequency head motion from helmets.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet provide drift-free, sensor-independent head pose from helmet IMUs alone outside the lab when cameras and LiDAR fail.

papers.title: How to Train Your Robots? The Impact of Demonstration Modality on Imitation Learning
papers.problem_statement: Kinesthetic teaching is preferred by users, yet most datasets use VR or spacemouse teleoperation; how demonstration modality affects policy performance, data quality and user experience is insufficiently explored.

stated_limitations.text: Kinesthetic replay fails on contact-force tasks.
stated_limitations.quote: kinesthetic teaching falls short since replaying recorded end-effector poses did not succeed at this task in the first try.

stated_limitations.text: No force sensor is available, so force-induced control error is compensated only after the fact.
stated_limitations.quote: we do not have access to a force sensor and can only account for such control error in hindsight

stated_limitations.text: The compensation heuristic doubles replay time on force tasks.
stated_limitations.quote: This heuristic results in doubling the replay time for tasks that require strong contact forces such as Push Sanitizer.

stated_limitations.text: Non-expert data was excluded from the data-quality analysis.
stated_limitations.quote: Due to high noise and cross-subject variance in non-expert data (6 participants), we discard them for this analysis.

stated_limitations.text: Kinesthetic teaching is too physically demanding for large-scale collection.
stated_limitations.quote: it is not preferred as the way for large-scale data collection due to the physical load.

failure_modes: Push Sanitizer (strong contact force): kinesthetic replay actions are highly jerky and misaligned with the trajectory, and policy success falls.
VR rotation control is unintuitive because users must keep resetting the reference pose.
Participants struggled with Flip Glass through teleoperation, since its trajectory runs near joint limits, giving widely spread trajectories.
future_work: Automatically determine the optimal ratio of data to collect from different modalities.
restrictive_assumptions: A single 7-DoF Franka arm with a Cartesian impedance controller.
Policy training data comes from a single demonstrator to control confounds; diffusion policy is fixed.
Three tabletop tasks; 12 university-student participants.
No force sensing; kinesthetic demonstrations need replay to obtain actions.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Kinesthetic data underperforms the teleoperation modalities, and the task was excluded from the mixed-data scheme because kinesthetic data quality was low.
75% with 100 mixed demonstrations, 5% above the best single-modality model.

open_problems_listed: The relative effects of demonstration modalities on policy performance, data quality and user experience remain insufficiently explored.
Kinesthetic teaching cannot recover actions under contact forces without force profile recording and replay.
Users prefer teleoperation for large-scale data collection despite its lower data quality.
The optimal mix of modalities is unknown and should be determined automatically.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet collect demonstrations that are both clean in contact force and low in effort at scale without force sensing during demonstration.

papers.title: HHI-Assist: A Dataset and Benchmark of Human-Human Interaction in Physical Assistance Scenario
papers.problem_statement: Assistive robots need accurate human motion prediction in physical interaction, which is hard because of the variability of assistive settings and the coupled dynamics between interacting agents; physical HRI data is scarce.

stated_limitations.text: Motions are performed by lab participants and are not validated as ergonomic or clinically safe.
stated_limitations.quote: While the dataset reflects plausible motions used in care scenarios, it does not guarantee that these motions are ergonomically correct or safe for clinical use.

stated_limitations.text: Heavily occluded takes were dropped after manual inspection.
stated_limitations.quote: Data were excluded upon manual inspection when the markers were occluded enough to cause unnatural or infeasible skeleton link overlap behavior

stated_limitations.text: Participants had no caregiving or care-receiving experience requirement.
stated_limitations.quote: Prior experience as a care receiver or caregiver was not required or explicitly considered when recruiting the participants.

stated_limitations.text: Transfer to physical human-robot interaction is not tested.
stated_limitations.quote: We believe this data and the techniques presented in this work are transferable to physical HRI settings and reserve this for future study.

stated_limitations.text: Generalization to unseen tasks degrades.
stated_limitations.quote: improving performance under such distribution shifts remains a direction for future work.

stated_limitations.text: Prediction uses only past pose, with no action class or other modalities.
stated_limitations.quote: we limit our focus to the observation pose sequence alone.

stated_limitations.text: Joint-position prediction does not preserve link lengths.
stated_limitations.quote: joint positions lead to variations in link lengths, with some samples exhibiting significant changes

failure_modes: On an unseen task (Task 3), caregiver MPJPE rises to 89.3 mm on average and 154.8 mm at 1000 ms.
Caregiver motion is harder to predict than care-receiver motion.
Joint-position prediction changes link lengths (mean 7.1 mm, std 14.84 mm); joint-angle prediction keeps link lengths but has higher MPJPE.
Modeling coupled dynamics between agents is challenging in certain scenarios.
future_work: Explore alternative input representations, including other angle parameterizations.
Address sources of uncertainty in the task.
Integrate predictions into receding-horizon controllers or learned policy observations.
Retarget the data to robot kinematics for behaviour cloning, and use it as style data for RL.
Derive assistive-task metrics such as contact sequences, force ranges and kinematic limits.
Transfer to physical HRI settings.
restrictive_assumptions: Marker-based OptiTrack capture with 20 cameras and 50-marker suits; 21-joint skeleton.
Healthy lab participants role-play the caregiver and care-receiver roles.
Only joint positions are released: no video, no contact or force data.
1 s observation predicts 1 s future at 24 fps.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best model (IDD) has 94.0 mm at the longest horizon and 50.4 mm on average.
Caregiver: 89.3 average and 154.8 at 1000 ms; care receiver: 62.5 average and 113.8 at 1000 ms.

open_problems_listed: Physical HRI data is scarce.
Coupled dynamics in physical interaction add complexity to motion prediction.
Assistance scenarios and human dynamics vary widely.
Prediction degrades under distribution shift to unseen tasks.
Angle representations have discontinuities, and position representations violate link lengths.
Using predictions for robot control (MPC, policy observations) is untested.
Metrics for assistive tasks (contact sequences, force ranges, kinematic limits) are still needed.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet predict coupled two-person motion during physical assistance accurately beyond about one second or across unseen assistance tasks.

papers.title: DynOPETs: A Versatile Benchmark for Dynamic Object Pose Estimation and Tracking in Moving Camera Scenarios
papers.problem_statement: Existing real-world object pose datasets assume static conditions (fixed camera or stationary object); annotating moving-camera, moving-object scenes needs manual labeling or expensive mocap, and pseudo-labels fail on symmetric, transparent, reflective or repetitive objects.

stated_limitations.text: After EKF/RTS refinement, FoundationPose pseudo-labels remain poor for symmetric or textureless objects such as bowls.
stated_limitations.quote: for those objects exhibiting significant symmetry or lacking distinctive texture, such as objects within the bowl category, the pose annotation is still not high-quality enough.

stated_limitations.text: The point-tracking relative pose branch drifts over time.
stated_limitations.quote: it is susceptible to cumulative errors, leading to drift in the estimated trajectory over time.

stated_limitations.text: The pipeline still needs manual removal of bad absolute pose estimates.
stated_limitations.quote: The manual effort required by our method is primarily limited to identifying and removing inaccurate absolute pose estimates

stated_limitations.text: SAM6D's built-in segmentation and fixed thresholds do not generalize to the cluttered backgrounds.
stated_limitations.quote: fixed threshold settings that fail to generalize in our dataset's cluttered backgrounds

stated_limitations.text: FoundationPose fails on some sequences and underperforms BundleTrack/BundleSDF on ADD(S)-0.1d.

papers.title: GraspClutter6D: A Large-Scale Real-World Dataset for Robust Perception and Grasping in Cluttered Scenes

open_problems_listed: Robust grasping in dense clutter with unknown poses and varied backgrounds is open.

Foundation segmentation models struggle with instance boundaries in clutter.
Simple approach trajectories fail; need gripper-aware reactive grasping.
Reflective/transparent objects produce depth sensor artifacts.

papers.title: Towards Exploratory and Focused Manipulation with Bimanual Active Perception: A New Problem, Benchmark and Strategy

papers.title: Kaiwu: A Multimodal Manipulation Dataset and Framework for Robot Learning and Human-Robot Interaction
