stated_limitations.text: Some participants left the capture area and occlusions caused missing markers in up to 3% of frames, filled by linear interpolation.
stated_limitations.quote: these issues concerned no more than 3% of the total frames and missing markers were effectively replaced through linear interpolation

stated_limitations.text: Depth sensor field of view is narrower than the cameras; joints outside it are treated as not visible.
stated_limitations.quote: The Field Of View (FOV) of the depth sensors is narrower than the one of the video cameras.

failure_modes: Close-range interaction leaves only part of the body (often one limb) visible to the low-mounted robot cameras.
3D pose from robot sensors has 168 mm average MPJPE, degraded by depth noise at larger distances.
Forecasting from robot-estimated partial poses (HRNet+D+R) yields about 309-333 mm MPJPE vs 43-70 mm with full ground truth.
Faster-moving joints are harder to forecast (Pearson r = 0.79 between joint speed and error).
Fast contacts (kicks, punches) are least predictable; a depth-only baseline reaches 0.49 accuracy on unintended collisions.
future_work: Use the data for further problems such as proxemic behavior and action recognition.
Reconstruct the full 3D skeleton from partial 2D observations.
restrictive_assumptions: Ground truth requires a 6-camera OptiTrack system and a 37-marker suit in a lab capture area.
Single user interacting with the robot at a time; 17 university-student participants; collisions are acted.
Robot future poses are assumed known because the robot plans in advance.
Spot cameras run at roughly 10 FPS with limited overlap between views.

benchmark_gaps.observation: PCK 82.2% in 2D, but 168 mm MPJPE in 3D.
Best HRNet+D+R about 309 mm (400 ms) and 332 mm (1000 ms); GT input EqMotion 43/70 mm.
EqMotion on HRNet+D+R: unintended 0.76 acc, 0.65 sensitivity; kick 0.52 sensitivity; depth baseline 0.49 acc on unintended.

open_problems_listed: 3D human pose estimation when the robot sees users only partially at close range.
Reconstructing the full 3D skeleton from a partial 2D image of the user.
Forecasting from incomplete pose sequences, which existing forecasting approaches cannot process.
Predicting fast, high-energy contacts (kicks, punches) between humans and a mobile robot.
Collision prediction from robot sensors requires approaches beyond simple depth extrapolation.
Further problems enabled by the data: proxemic behavior and action recognition.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet estimate and forecast full 3D human pose accurately from close-range, partial, robot-mounted views.

papers.title: EHoA: A Benchmark for Task-Oriented Hand-Object Action Recognition Via Event Vision
papers.problem_statement: Using event vision to analyze hand-object actions in dynamic environments, which regular CMOS cameras cannot handle, is still lacking in research; EHoA claims to pioneer event-based hand-object action recognition.
restrictive_assumptions: Requires an event-based camera system (asynchronous event streams).
Recognition task is classification of task-oriented hand-object action categories, not 3D tracking or reconstruction.
open_problems_listed: Event-vision analysis of hand-object actions in dynamic environments is still lacking (abstract, per search snippet).
Regular CMOS cameras cannot handle hand-object action analysis in highly dynamic conditions (abstract claim).
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet recognize hand-object actions robustly under fast motion and high dynamic range with conventional frame cameras.

papers.title: A Multi-Modal Hand Imitation Dataset for Dexterous Hand
papers.problem_statement: Existing dexterous imitation datasets predominantly rely on single-modality inputs such as RGB images, which lack the capacity to capture the spatial and temporal dynamics needed for human-like dexterity.
restrictive_assumptions: Human and robot hand poses are aligned in a shared canonical space using neural rendering and kinematic optimization (method requirement per abstract).
Requires synchronized RGB, point cloud and hand kinematic modalities.
open_problems_listed: Single-modality (RGB) dexterous imitation datasets cannot capture spatial and temporal dynamics needed for human-like dexterity (abstract, per search snippet).
Geometrically consistent human-to-robot hand skill transfer requires aligning human and robot hand poses (abstract).
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet transfer human hand demonstrations to dexterous robot hands with geometrically consistent multimodal grounding at scale.

papers.title: Extraction of Robotic Surface Processing Strategies from Human Demonstrations
papers.problem_statement: LfD transfers individual motions rather than whole surface-processing strategies, and no data acquisition system captures contact forces of manually guided, powered sanding tools without disturbing natural human tool use.

stated_limitations.text: Vive motion tracking was interrupted by occlusions and tool vibrations, reducing sampling rate.
stated_limitations.quote: interruptions in the motion tracking occurred due to occlusions and vibrations caused by the sanding tool

stated_limitations.text: A low-cost, robust and portable capture system still needs further hardware work.
stated_limitations.quote: developing a lowcost, robust, and portable system requires to solve further challenges in the hardware design

stated_limitations.text: Optical marker tracking is suggested but not guaranteed to solve vibration problems.
stated_limitations.quote: Nevertheless, it is not guaranteed that optical tracking will overcome the problem introduced by vibrations.

stated_limitations.text: Human strategies are optimized for human anatomy and ergonomics, not robot performance, e.g. box working direction produces many turns.
stated_limitations.quote: Limitations of the presented procedure about extraction of robotic strategies from human demonstrations possibly lie in the human nature of the strategies

stated_limitations.text: Real material removal was not performed; a guide coat substituted because real processing changes the workpiece.
stated_limitations.quote: Full and real surface processing would change the workpiece surface and geometry.

stated_limitations.text: Robot reproduction on the half-cylinder left small unprocessed patches near edges, caused by the finishing disk radius.
stated_limitations.quote: almost full coverage of the halfcylinder could be achieved while small patches remained unprocessed.

failure_modes: Tool vibration and occlusion interrupt Vive tracking; tracker rate varied from 83 to 470 Hz (median 127 Hz).
Kinesthetic teaching alternative would bias demonstrations through robot inertia and kinematic limits.
Human-preferred working direction on the box conflicts with an optimal robot strategy minimizing turns.
Micro patterns (22% of demonstrations) did not increase coverage and increased processing time.
future_work: Evaluate optical passive-marker tracking (OptiTrack, Vicon) to reduce vibration sensitivity.
Investigate more geometric shapes and processing techniques such as edge following and smoothing fine structures.
Consider material properties and realistic material removal in real surface finishing tasks.
restrictive_assumptions: Force/torque sensor placed under a fixed workpiece fixture, so only workpieces mounted on the sensor can be measured.
Workpiece geometry known as a point cloud from a 3D model or depth camera.
Guide-coat removal instead of real sanding; four simple primitive workpieces.
Single customized powered sander with a mounted Vive tracker and damper.
Robot skills defined only for two primitive shapes (plane, half-cylinder) with mean demonstrated normal force.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Highest coverage on the simplest box workpiece; more complex shapes lower (values in figure only).
Near-full coverage, small patches unprocessed near base-plate edges.

open_problems_listed: No known powered sanding tool designs with integrated force sensing; adding an FTS would impair grasp ergonomics.
Force-sensing surface tools mounted on robots bias human demonstrations via inertia and kinematic limits.
Robust, low-cost, portable motion capture under tool vibration and occlusion remains unsolved.
Deciding when to learn strategies from humans versus using pre-programmed expert strategies suited to robot capabilities.
Extending to more shapes and techniques such as edge following and fine-structure smoothing.
Capturing strategies under realistic material removal and material properties.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet capture robust, vibration-tolerant motion and contact force of hand-held powered tool use during real material processing.

papers.title: OpenRoboCare: A Multi-Modal Multi-Task Expert Demonstration Dataset for Robot Caregiving
papers.problem_statement: There is no large-scale, diverse, expert-driven multimodal dataset capturing real-world caregiving routines; prior caregiving datasets are task-specific, often simulated, limited in modalities, and rarely collected from expert caregivers.

stated_limitations.text: The dataset covers only fully passive care recipients; partially mobile individuals are left for future work.
stated_limitations.quote: Another limitation of OpenRoboCare is its focus on fully passive care recipients.

stated_limitations.text: Clothing and slings occluded markers, causing motion-capture tracking failures for manikin pose and caregiver hands.
stated_limitations.quote: occlusions caused by clothing in dressing tasks and slings in transferring tasks often led to tracking failures for both the manikin's pose and the caregiver's hand positions

stated_limitations.text: Occlusion workaround uses triangulation from only three calibrated views.
stated_limitations.quote: While limited to three views, this approach provides a practical and scalable solution for occlusion handling.

stated_limitations.text: Manikins lack agency or resistance and represent only passive full-assistance scenarios.
stated_limitations.quote: While manikins lack partial agency or resistance, they effectively represent passive full-assistance scenarios that are common in OT practice.

stated_limitations.text: Sensors run at different rates due to hardware limits; all modalities are aligned to the 15 Hz RGB-D stream.
stated_limitations.quote: Due to hardware limitations, each sensor operates at a different sampling rate

stated_limitations.text: Off-the-shelf pose estimation performs poorly on caregiving scenes.
stated_limitations.quote: the off-the-shelf YOLOv11 [45] performs poorly, but fine-tuning on even a small subset of our labeled dataset leads to large gains

stated_limitations.text: Long-horizon caregiving procedures are hard to recognize for current models.
stated_limitations.quote: The long task horizons make it difficult for current models to recognize full procedures.

failure_modes: Heavy occlusion from close two-body contact, garments and assistive devices causes pose tracking and estimation failures.
Pretrained 2D pose detector reaches only about 0.02 mAP on bathing, dressing and transfer.
3D pose estimation errors of 119.9-162.7 mm MPJPE.
Video task recognition mislabels caregiving terms (positioning the Hoyer read as foyer) and fails on long procedures.
future_work: Supplement the dataset with partial sensory data that is easier to obtain.
Include partially mobile individuals who actively participate in ADLs.
restrictive_assumptions: Manikins instead of real care recipients (passive, no resistance).
12-camera OptiTrack with marker gloves and hat plus three fixed RealSense D435i cameras in one enclosed room.
Custom tactile skin on manikins; eye-tracking glasses on caregivers.
21 female participants, 19 of them final-year OT students; one trial per task.
Feeding excluded; 15 tasks across 5 ADLs.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Pretrained YOLOv11 0.0244 bathing, 0.0259 dressing, 0.0218 transfer; fine-tuned on 5 OTs still 0.6648 on transfer.
Best RTMOPose3D 119.9 mm; MHFormer 162.7 mm.
Significant gap remains; full long-horizon procedures not recognized.

open_problems_listed: Accurate perception of human state under occlusions in caregiving.
Bimanual and mobile manipulation of human limbs under critical safety constraints.
Long-horizon planning under uncertainty.
Personalization to users' physical function and preferences.
Adaptation in response to human feedback.
Caregiving datasets are task-specific, often simulated, limited in modality, and rarely expert-collected.
Heavy occlusion from close physical interaction and assistive devices makes pose estimation hard.
Distribution shift from general pose datasets: multi-body pose, unusual postures, camera placements that do not minimize occlusion.
Multimodal variability in task plans originating from expert strategies.
Long-horizon task recognition and decomposition; lack of caregiving-domain training data and terminology.
Robots need both delicate (0.1-2 N) and high-force (20-30 N) contact, requiring compliant, backdrivable actuators and wide-range force sensing.
Whole-arm contact requires distributed sensing and compliance along the entire arm.
Extending to partially mobile care recipients who actively participate.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet estimate multi-body human pose under heavy contact occlusion in caregiving or recognize long-horizon caregiving procedures.

papers.title: AgiBot World Colosseo: Large-Scale Manipulation Platform for Scalable and Intelligent Embodied Systems
papers.fulltext_source: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.06669 (arXiv id found via export.arxiv.org API; v4 = IROS camera-ready per change log)
papers.problem_statement: Robot learning datasets are fragmented by heterogeneous hardware and unstandardized collection, and remain constrained to short-horizon tasks in controlled labs, so generalist policies (e.g. from OXE, DROID) generalize weakly to open-world, long-horizon, dexterous tasks.

stated_limitations.text: The VR teleoperation interface limits dexterous-hand demonstrations to a few predefined gestures; a motion-capture system was added to overcome this.
stated_limitations.quote: However, the VR controller restricts the dexterous hand to only a few predefined gestures.

stated_limitations.text: The pre-trained GO-1 has only basic competency and is fine-tuned with task-specific demonstrations before evaluation on new tasks.
stated_limitations.quote: Following the completion of the third-stage pre-training, the pre-trained GO-1 exhibits basic competency in task completion.

stated_limitations.text: Action-labeled robot data remains limited relative to web-scale data, motivating latent actions learned from unlabeled human video.
stated_limitations.quote: the volume of action-labeled robot data remains limited relative to web-scale datasets.

stated_limitations.text: More data alone does not help: unverified demonstrations performed worse than a smaller human-verified set (0.18 completion-score gap).
stated_limitations.quote: being larger in quantity does not necessarily translate to improved performance
stated_limitations.section: V-E How does data quality impact policy learning?

failure_modes: Teleoperators drop objects during collection; such failure-recovery trajectories are about one percent of the dataset and are annotated rather than discarded.
Policies trained on early data showed prolonged pauses at action onset, traced to idle frames and inconsistent transitions in collected demonstrations.
Out-of-distribution scores remain below in-distribution (0.67 vs 0.77 for AgiBot-pretrained RDT; OXE-pretrained 0.38 OOD).
future_work: Community collaboration to build an ecosystem around the open dataset, toolchains and models.
Use failure-recovery data for policy alignment and failure reflection in next-generation robot foundation models.
restrictive_assumptions: Single homogeneous robot embodiment (AgiBot G1, dual 7-DoF arms) across all 100 robots.
Expert human teleoperation (VR or whole-body motion capture) required for every demonstration.
Human-in-the-loop verification and manual annotation of every episode.
Evaluation after task-specific fine-tuning on high-quality demonstrations.
Purpose-built 4,000 square meter collection facility with staged scenes.

benchmark_gaps.dataset: AgiBot World eval tasks (Restock Bag, Table Bussing, Pour Water)
benchmark_gaps.observation: AgiBot-pretrained RDT reaches 0.67 OOD vs 0.77 in-distribution; OXE-pretrained only 0.38 OOD.
Unverified data (482 traj.) yields 0.18 lower score than 528 verified trajectories.
Abstract reports over 60% success on complex tasks, i.e. roughly 40% of complex-task trials still fail.

open_problems_listed: Open-set real-world tasks (fine-grained object interaction, mobile manipulation, collaborative tasks) remain a formidable challenge.
Existing datasets are limited to short-horizon tasks in controlled labs and lack quality assurance.
Limited action-labeled robot data relative to web-scale data.
Generalization across diverse environments and scenarios is beyond current robotic systems.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Train generalist manipulation policies that handle long-horizon, dexterous, open-world tasks without expensive verified teleoperation data and per-task fine-tuning.

papers.title: Challenges for Monocular 6D Object Pose Estimation in Robotics
papers.problem_statement: Prior surveys' broad scope hides open challenges specific to monocular pose estimation for robotics; benchmark-driven pose research diverges from robotic requirements in unstructured open-world environments.

stated_limitations.text: Claims that domain shift is solved hold only for standard datasets with limited variance in shapes, support planes, textures and illumination.
stated_limitations.quote: The presented considerations are only valid for standard datasets, where the variance of the data distribution in terms of, for example, object shapes, support planes, textures and illumination is limited.

stated_limitations.text: No systematic study exists of how specific occlusion patterns and part visibility affect pose accuracy.
stated_limitations.quote: Detailed systematic investigations of the influence of specific occlusion patterns, and the visibility of specific object parts, on the pose estimation accuracy are missing.

stated_limitations.text: Category-level comparison uses inconsistent train-test splits and possibly faulty published results.
stated_limitations.quote: Note that these results are on inconsistent train-test splits.

stated_limitations.text: Multi-object pose estimators still trail single-object estimators trained per object.
stated_limitations.quote: Despite these obvious advantages, the performance trails behind single-object approaches, which train separate pose estimators per object.

stated_limitations.text: Render-and-compare refinement depends on textured 3D models and realistic rendering, which fails for novel and reflective or refractive objects.
stated_limitations.quote: creating a dependence on (textured) 3D object models which is not easily address for, e.g., novel objects.

failure_modes: Monocular category-level pose lags far behind RGB-D on CAMERA25/REAL275, and the gap appears to widen as RGB-only research stagnated.
Novel-object pose methods are limited to opaque objects and runtime grows with the number of templates (minutes).
Metallic (specular) and transparent objects: appearance varies with light and viewpoint; handling them is largely unsolved even at instance level.
Category-level methods interpolate between object origins when an object lies between two categories (e.g. cup vs bowl).
Deep methods lose accuracy when visual symmetries are not considered at training time; symmetries often must be known beforehand.
future_work: Investigate novel pose representations, including keypoint-based symmetry handling.
Formal taxonomies/ontologies for category-level pose estimation, possibly verified LLM/VLM ontologies.
Metrics and formal definitions of pose for deformable and articulated objects.
Scene-level consistency via simulation, reconstruction, inverse rendering or NeRF-like methods.
Realistic benchmarks with natural clutter, backgrounds and material variety.
Template-free, training-free novel-object pose to reduce energy use.
Study strengths and weaknesses of RGB vs depth for transparent objects.
restrictive_assumptions: Most methods and datasets assume rigid objects.
Instance-level methods need a CAD model and per-object retraining.
Novel and category-level methods assume prior information about the object origin.
Standard datasets: opaque, diffuse, hand-sized objects on a single support plane, centered in view, marker-board annotation.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Six of seven core datasets contain only opaque, diffusely reflecting objects; only one includes specular metallic surfaces.
Huge performance gap of RGB-only vs RGB-D approaches, apparently widening.
Little intra-category variation and overlapping categories, limiting tests of category generalization.
Occlusion-specific methods do not outperform general methods; occlusion handling correlates with general accuracy.

open_problems_listed: Domain shift beyond closed-world industrial/household data (underwater, space, medical).
Occlusion handling: systematic analysis of occlusion patterns missing.
Unambiguous yet compact pose representations.
Multi-object training with data imbalance; trails single-object models.
Refinement without depth and without textured models.
Symmetry handling for keypoint-based approaches; symmetries must be known a priori.
Category-level pose: closing the monocular vs RGB-D gap; category taxonomies.
Novel object pose: accuracy, runtime, non-opaque objects, mobile robotics.
Challenging materials: metallic and transparent objects.
Learning beyond supervision (self-supervised, RL).
Uncertainty estimation for downstream robot decisions.
Object ontology for truly unknown objects and part-of relations.
Deformable and articulated objects: no common pose definition or metric.
Scene-level consistency of multi-object pose.
Benchmark realism: clutter, backgrounds, object variation, natural annotation.
Environmental impact of per-object training and template matching.
Relation to generalist manipulation policies that act without explicit poses.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Estimate accurate 6D poses from monocular RGB for unknown, non-rigid, transparent or reflective objects in naturally cluttered scenes without CAD models or per-object training.

papers.title: A Survey on Deep Generative Models for Robot Learning From Multimodal Demonstrations
papers.fulltext_source: https://arxiv.org/html/2408.04380 (arXiv title: Deep Generative Models in Robotics: A Survey on Learning from Multimodal Demonstrations; first author Julen Urain confirmed)
papers.problem_statement: Classical learning-from-demonstration models cannot capture multimodal, high-dimensional demonstration distributions or scale to large datasets; the survey reviews deep generative models and how to generalize them out of distribution.

stated_limitations.text: Survey scope is restricted to offline data and offline supervision, excluding interactively collected data.
stated_limitations.quote: The survey focuses mainly on approaches that consider offline data , i.e., no additional data collected online or interactively, and offline supervision

stated_limitations.text: Current generative policies have not shown strong generalization.
stated_limitations.quote: current generative models have not shown yet powerful generalization capabilities

stated_limitations.text: Density-estimation training objective mismatches task-success evaluation objective.
stated_limitations.quote: This mismatch between the training objective and the evaluation objective can lead to poor performance
stated_limitations.section: I-A Challenges in Learning from Offline Demonstrations

failure_modes: Compounding errors in sequential decisions push the robot into states absent from demonstrations.
With small datasets, policies learn spurious correlations between high-dimensional observations and actions.
Distribution shift between demonstration and deployment contexts causes generalization failures.
Partially observable demonstrations (human uses unobserved cues) yield ambiguous policies.
future_work: Robot policies for long-horizon tasks, e.g. LLM planning grounded in low-level skills.
Learning from video demonstrations (embodiment mismatch, no action labels, environment mismatch).
Learning from synthetic data while addressing the sim-to-real gap.
Learning from online interaction with efficient exploration.
Structured priors for generalization, internet knowledge, and 3D feature fields.
restrictive_assumptions: Offline expert demonstrations with expert action labels.
Teleoperation data, which is costly to collect at scale.
open_problems_listed: Demonstration diversity (multiple modes from different demonstrators).
Heterogeneous action and state spaces across robots and datasets.
Partially observable demonstrations.
Temporal dependencies, compounding error and long-horizon planning.
Mismatch between training (density estimation) and evaluation (task success) objectives.
Distribution shifts and generalization to unseen contexts.
Solving arbitrary long-horizon tasks; grounding language commands in robot actions.
Learning from human video: embodiment mismatch, lack of action data, train-test environment mismatch.
Sim-to-real gap for policies trained on synthetic data.
Efficient exploration when learning online in the deployment environment.
Structured priors, internet knowledge and 3D feature fields for generalization.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Learn policies from offline demonstrations that generalize to novel goals and scenes and solve arbitrary long-horizon tasks.

papers.title: Bi-DexHands: Towards Human-Level Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation
papers.fulltext_source: https://arxiv.org/html/2206.08686 (arXiv version titled 'Towards Human-Level Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation with Reinforcement Learning'; TPAMI version text not read)
papers.problem_statement: Human-level dexterity and bimanual coordination remain open; RL struggles with high-DoF hands, heterogeneous joint cooperation, and generalizing complex skills across tasks in contact-rich settings.

stated_limitations.text: No deformable-object tasks; only articulated rigid bodies are covered.
stated_limitations.quote: the limitation of Bi-DexHands is that it does not support the deformable object manipulation tasks.

stated_limitations.text: Policies use state-based observations unavailable in the real world, which hinders sim-to-real transfer.
stated_limitations.quote: our tasks primarily train with policies with a state-based observation space, which is difficult for sim-to-real transfer because such inputs are not available in the real world.

stated_limitations.text: Isaac Gym cameras render serially, so visual (point cloud) RL runs at about 200 fps vs 30000+ for state input, limiting visual baselines.
stated_limitations.quote: This was a problem with Isaac Gym's poor parallel support for cameras, so we didn't use point clouds or other visual inputs as our baselines

failure_modes: Existing RL algorithms fail in most multi-task and few-shot settings.
SAC fails on almost all tasks, attributed to off-policy learning under massive parallelism and 50+ dimensional actions.
Multi-task PPO performs poorly and ProMP barely beats random policy on MT/ML settings.
Offline RL (IQL) improves only on some datasets due to severe out-of-distribution actions.
Task difficulty for RL increases with the human age the task corresponds to; RL reaches roughly 48-month infant level.
future_work: Learning from human demonstration data.
Soft-body and deformable object simulation with a better physics engine.
Algorithmic advances for meta/multi-task RL to solve all tasks.
Sim-to-real transfer onto real dexterous hands.
restrictive_assumptions: Simulation only (Isaac Gym) with Shadow Hands.
Full privileged state observations.
Rigid and articulated objects only.
Massive parallel sampling (2048 environments) on GPU.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Multi-task PPO does not perform well; ProMP shows tiny improvement over random policy.

benchmark_gaps.dataset: Bi-DexHands offline (Hand Over, Door Open Outward)
benchmark_gaps.observation: IQL improves only on several datasets due to larger out-of-distribution action problem.
SAC does not work on almost all tasks.

open_problems_listed: Cross-task generalization of bimanual dexterous skills under multi-task/meta RL.
Learning from demonstration for bimanual dexterous hands.
Deformable object manipulation and simulation.
Sim-to-real transfer of RL-learned dexterous skills.
RL algorithm design for high-sampling-efficiency regimes.
Offline RL under large state/action spaces and distribution shift.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Learn bimanual dexterous policies that generalize across many tasks from realistic (visual) observations and transfer to real hands.

papers.title: HiSC4D: Human-Centered Interaction and 4D Scene Capture in Large-Scale Space Using Wearable IMUs and LiDAR
papers.problem_statement: Capturing interacting 4D human motions in large real environments from an egocentric view is hard: IMUs drift, external cameras restrict space, RGB methods degrade under dynamic motion or textureless scenes, and prior LiDAR systems cannot capture human-human interaction.

stated_limitations.text: LiDAR vertical field of view causes body truncation and joint occlusion of the second person.
stated_limitations.quote: One limitation of this study is the vertical field of view limitation of the LiDAR, which is 33.2° / 45°.

stated_limitations.text: Low LiDAR resolution prevents reconstruction of human texture.
stated_limitations.quote: due to the low resolution of the LiDAR sensor, our method cannot reconstruct human textures.

stated_limitations.text: Scene-aware optimization is computationally heavy, hindering real-time and large-scale use.
stated_limitations.quote: This complexity can pose challenges in real-time and large-scale applications.

stated_limitations.text: SLAM has limits in extreme situations such as long-duration occlusions.
stated_limitations.quote: there are limitations in extreme situations such as long-duration occlusions.

failure_modes: IMU-only baseline drifts severely and assumes a horizontal walking plane, giving large localization and height errors.
IMU plus LiDAR without joint optimization shows sliding from non-rigid LiDAR-to-root attachment and body-model mismatch, and worse smoothness (ACC).
Second person is intermittently occluded due to head motion and LiDAR FOV; sequences are split into visible segments.
Mapping errors are larger in regions with outdoor trees and untraversed tall buildings.
future_work: Add RGB video to recover geometry detail of the second person.
restrictive_assumptions: Both people wear 17-IMU suits; first person wears a head-mounted LiDAR and backpack.
Rigid LiDAR-to-head transformation.
Calibration at start: A-pose facing a planar marker, second person 5 m ahead, jump-in-place for synchronization.
Offline batch optimization (0.73 h and 2.80 h for one 7725-frame sequence).
Pre-scanned subject body models and only two people per sequence.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Mean 6.5 cm; larger errors near trees and untraversed high-floor buildings.
IMU-only 569.7 mm, IMU+ICP 65.1 mm, reduced a further 47.7% by full optimization.
Optimization takes 0.73 h (first person) and 2.80 h (second person) for 7725 frames.

open_problems_listed: Drift-free motion capture in large capture areas with IMUs.
Capturing human-human interaction from an egocentric view in large scenes with 3D ground truth.
Truncation and occlusion of the second person due to sensor field of view.
Real-time capture with scene-aware optimization.
SLAM robustness under long-duration occlusion.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Capture multi-person interaction and scene in large spaces in real time with fine detail (texture, hands) and robustness to occlusion from wearable sensors alone.

stated_limitations.text: Gains on indoor benchmarks Human3.6M and MPI-INF-3DHP are smaller than on 3DPW, attributed to indoor-outdoor domain gaps.

stated_limitations.text: Annotation captures bone lengths but not full body shape from subject meshes.
stated_limitations.quote: the annotation pipeline may be upgraded to fully capture the body shape besides the bone lengths from the 3D mesh of the subjects.

Models trained on indoor real data do not transfer well to in-the-wild scenes.
CycleGAN-style learned augmentation is not effective for closing the domain gap.
Real data cannot sustain high real-to-synthetic ratios beyond 300K samples.

Study sim2real for parametric human recovery in more depth.
Extend game data to model-free reconstruction and other human tasks.
Capture full body shape in the annotation pipeline.

Single-person monocular RGB human recovery; no hand or object interaction focus.
Mixing with real data still needed (blended training or fine-tuning).

benchmark_gaps.observation: Gains from GTA-Human are smaller than on 3DPW, attributed to indoor-outdoor gap.

open_problems_listed: Scarcity and cost of 3D parametric ground truth in the wild.
Synthetic-to-real domain gap.
Data remains a critical bottleneck for accurate human pose and shape estimation.
Full body shape annotation from synthetic meshes.

papers.title: HOI4D: A 4D Egocentric Dataset for Category-Level Human-Object Interaction
papers.problem_statement: Prior egocentric HOI datasets are instance-level (small pools of objects with known CAD models and sizes) and ignore articulated objects, which blocks perception of interaction with the diversity of everyday objects.

stated_limitations.text: Two-handed manipulation is not covered; the authors consider single-hand manipulation still unsolved and leave hand cooperation for future study.
stated_limitations.quote: The main limitation of HOI4D is that human manipulation tasks with two hands are not covered since the single-hand manipulation tasks remain challenging for current research.

stated_limitations.text: Hand pose annotation by optimization fails on some frames (ambiguous poses, bad initialization) and these frames are corrected manually.
stated_limitations.quote: We manually detect failure frames since the optimization process may fail due to ambiguous hand poses or a bad initialization.

stated_limitations.text: Only 1 of every 10 frames gets manual object pose labels; the rest are propagated, and human 3D pose labels are not fully reliable.
stated_limitations.quote: Labeling object poses in 3D is a challenging task for human annotators while not all annotations are fully reliable.

stated_limitations.text: Scanning large objects with complex topology and materials remains hard for the mesh reconstruction step.
stated_limitations.quote: modeling objects with large size, especially with complex topology and materials remains challenging.

failure_modes: Category-level pose tracking (BundleTrack) drops from 86.5 (5deg5cm) on NOCS to 19.3 on HOI4D bottle, attributed to sensor noise, complex backgrounds, hand occlusion and fast motion.

4D point cloud segmentation methods do much worse on object classes than background because objects are small, move flexibly and are heavily occluded.
Fine-grained action segmentation: Asformer reaches 46.8 accuracy on HOI4D versus 85.6 on 50Salads; models learn action order rather than perceiving the current action.
future_work: Extend to two-handed manipulation and hand cooperation.
More research on category-level object pose tracking in real-world interactive scenarios, via sim-to-real or learning from real data.
Methods that capture object geometry and background geometry simultaneously for 4D segmentation.
Use HOI4D CAD models and poses to bridge simulation and the real world for robot learning and AR.
restrictive_assumptions: Single hand only; no bimanual sequences.
Egocentric head-mounted single RGB-D camera.
Object meshes from scanning or category CAD pipeline; manual keyframe pose labels every 10th frame plus propagation.
16 categories of household objects; 9 participants (abstract says 4).

Scanning large objects with complex topology and materials.
Category-level dexterous robot manipulation from human demonstrations (low success rates).
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet track category-level object pose reliably while a hand is occluding and moving the object, let alone for two cooperating hands.
