stated_limitations.quote: Existing methods show promising results but are still far from tackling these challenges with high precision, as observed in the oracle experiments

stated_limitations.text: Large domain gap between egocentric and fixed views.
stated_limitations.quote: This indicates a significant mismatch and presents a new challenge for studying the domain gap on paired egocentric and third-person actions.

stated_limitations.text: Hand poses carry little object information; joint 3D object and hand pose modelling is left to future work.
stated_limitations.quote: We leave as future work the joint modeling of 3D objects and hand poses for action recognition.

stated_limitations.text: Mistake detection is hard; recall stays low even with ground-truth coarse labels.
stated_limitations.quote: With TSM input features, the recall is currently only around 46.6% and 29.6% once the segment of interest ends.

stated_limitations.text: Long-tail classes perform poorly.
stated_limitations.quote: The low tail performance scores encourage developing few-shot action recognition methods.

failure_modes: Egocentric views 16.2% lower in overall recognition than fixed views.
Side cameras 11-16% lower than best overhead camera.
Unseen toys score lower, especially on objects.
Assembly segmentation worse than disassembly, especially for low-skill participants.
Pose-based recognition object accuracy 10.2% lower than video.
future_work: Joint modeling of 3D objects and hand poses for action recognition.
Few-shot action recognition for tail classes.
Smart assistants that recognize, predict steps and alert on mistakes.
restrictive_assumptions: Desk rig with 8 calibrated static cameras plus 4-camera headset.
3D hand poses from a modified MegATrack egocentric tracker, not mocap ground truth.
No 6D object pose annotations.
Take-apart toy vehicles on a desk.

benchmark_gaps.observation: C2F-TCN reaches 39.2 MoF and 21.3 F1@50.
MS-G3D with context 28.7% action vs 33.8% video; object 36.3%.
TSM mistake recall 46.6%, correction 29.6%; early prediction 35.0% and 26.4%.

open_problems_listed: Fine-grained action recognition from egocentric views.
Action anticipation.
Temporal action segmentation of free-form procedures.
Mistake detection.
Cross-view domain gap.
Long-tail recognition.
Generalization to unseen toys.
Joint 3D object and hand pose modelling.
Domain gap from pretrained video features.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet recognize fine-grained hand-object actions and mistakes in free-form assembly with joint 3D hand and object understanding.

papers.title: A Dataset of Relighted 3D Interacting Hands
papers.problem_statement: Existing two-hand datasets do not achieve both diverse, realistic image appearance and diverse, large-scale accurate 3D ground truth at the same time: lab datasets look monotonous, natural datasets are small with simple poses, composited datasets have inconsistent lighting.

stated_limitations.text: Rendered images are cut at the forearm because the relighting network only takes hand geometry, not a whole body.
stated_limitations.quote: our rendered images have cut at the forearm area. This is because our relighting network only takes a 3D hand geometry, not a whole-body one.

stated_limitations.text: Relighted images sometimes contain artifacts because the relighting network is trained on single-hand data and applied to two-hand data.
stated_limitations.quote: the relighting network is trained on single-hand data and tested on two-hand data, which sometimes results in pose generalization failure.

stated_limitations.text: Natural datasets captured with few cameras (e.g. a single RGB-D camera) cannot provide accurate annotations for complicated interacting hands, so they contain only simple poses.
stated_limitations.quote: As only a few cameras are used, such datasets could not provide accurate annotations for complicated interacting hands.

stated_limitations.text: RANSAC triangulation of multi-view 2D detections (as in InterHand2.6M) gives temporally inconsistent 3D joints and hand collisions.
stated_limitations.quote: We found that their approach suffers from temporally inconsistent results as the triangulation does not take into account the similarity between close frames.

failure_modes: Relighted two-hand images show artifacts when the single-hand-trained relighting network meets unseen two-hand poses.
Training on studio (capture-stage) images alone does not improve accuracy on real natural images (HIC) because appearance is far from real images.
Composited images (and AdaIN harmonization) degrade performance on HIC due to foreground/background light inconsistency and unrealistic skin colors.
Frames with wrong MANO fitting results had to be excluded by manual inspection.
future_work: A better relighting network to remove two-hand artifacts.
Moving the community closer to 3D interacting hands recovery in the wild.
restrictive_assumptions: Ground truth requires a studio with 170 calibrated synchronized cameras and 469 lights.
Hands only, no objects; no hand-object interaction.
Images rendered without forearm/body; downstream systems assumed to use cropped hand images from a separate hand detector.
10 subjects; per-subject relighting networks and per-subject NeuralAnnot fitting.
IntagHand baseline assumes ground-truth hand boxes.

benchmark_gaps.observation: IntagHand 67.11 mm and InterWild 23.59 mm, versus about 19.7-20 mm on InterHand2.6M: large gap on natural images.
InterWild 37.59 mm and IntagHand 52.91 mm before training on Re:InterHand; 20.07 mm after.
InterWild 28.89 mm even after training on the egocentric split.

open_problems_listed: Two-hand analysis is hard due to self-similarity, complicated articulation, small size and inter-hand occlusion, especially from a single image.
True 3D data is not obtainable from a single 2D observation (scale and depth ambiguity).
Lab datasets have monotonous appearance (color, background, illumination).
Natural datasets are limited in diversity and scale and provide only simple poses.
Composited datasets have unrealistic appearance from lighting inconsistency.
Relighting must generalize from single-hand to two-hand poses.
Rendered data lacks forearm and body context.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet obtain accurate 3D ground truth for interacting hands under realistic in-the-wild appearance without a dense multi-camera studio plus synthetic relighting.

papers.title: RenderIH: A Large-scale Synthetic Dataset for 3D Interacting Hand Pose Estimation
papers.problem_statement: Current interacting-hand datasets have simple backgrounds and textures, machine-annotated joints that may be inaccurate, and limited pose diversity; synthetic data must solve both pose validity and image diversity/realism.

stated_limitations.text: Pose-optimization hyperparameters (attraction factors, loss weights) were chosen empirically rather than learned.
stated_limitations.quote: The hyperparameters of pose optimization are chosen on the basis of experimental results, such as factor and in Interhand attraction and weights in the final optimization loss.

stated_limitations.text: Training on RenderIH alone performs worse than training on real IH2.6M; the synthetic data is meant to reduce, not replace, real data.
stated_limitations.quote: the function of our dataset is to largely reduce the number of real data needed for training instead of replacing real data entirely.

stated_limitations.text: Interhand attraction can hurt when hand parts overlap seriously, because anchor pairs conflict and meshes are hard to separate.
stated_limitations.quote: the IH attraction might cause a negative influence when the parts are in serious overlaps

stated_limitations.text: Real IH datasets are annotated by a machine annotator, which may be inaccurate, and are limited in amount.
stated_limitations.quote: with hand joints being annotated by a machine annotator, which may result in inaccuracies, and the diversity of pose distribution is limited.

failure_modes: Synthetic-only training generalizes poorly to real test sets (Tzionas, IH2.6M) compared with real-data training.
Anchor-based attraction fails when hand parts are in serious overlap; hands must first be separated.
7 percent of augmented poses still had notable penetration or exceeded joint limits after optimization and were filtered out.
future_work: Make pose-optimization hyperparameters learnable from data.
Develop 3D interacting-hand pose estimators that do not depend on real data and adapt to various scenes.
Use the dataset for domain adaptation.
restrictive_assumptions: Hands only (MANO/A-MANO), no objects or forearm/body context.
Synthetic rendered monocular RGB; raw poses derived and augmented from InterHand2.6M.
Joint angle limits from a fixed anatomical table; naturalness judged by a discriminator trained on existing datasets.
Rendering cost over 200 hours on 4 A100 GPUs.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Training on RenderIH only gives 22.11/25.8/47.7 versus 11.38/11.1/19.9 for IH2.6M-only training.
RenderIH-only 13.50 mm versus IH2.6M-only 6.76 mm; mixed training 5.79 mm.
Relative root position error remains 14.15 mm even with mixed training.

open_problems_listed: Obtaining real 3D interacting hand annotations is challenging and time-consuming due to severe self-occlusion.
Validity of generated 3D hand poses (interpenetration, anatomical plausibility, naturalness).
Diversity and realism of generated images (backgrounds, lighting, textures).
Close-contact interacting hands are hard to annotate in reality and available close-contact data are limited.
Reducing dependency on real data; synthetic data alone does not yet replace it.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet train interacting-hand pose estimators on synthetic data alone that match real-data training on real images.

papers.title: HandoverSim: A Simulation Framework and Benchmark for Human-to-Robot Object Handovers
papers.problem_statement: Human-to-robot handover research needs a real human in the loop for evaluation, which is expensive and hard to reproduce, and studies use different settings and metrics, preventing cross-study comparison.

stated_limitations.text: The simulated human giver does not adapt to the robot's actions; the authors call this assumption naive.
stated_limitations.quote: Our human's motion is non-adaptive to the robot's actions. This assumption is rather naive

stated_limitations.text: Realistic human hand motion during and after object release is not simulated because such data is lacking.
stated_limitations.quote: We do not simulate realistic human hand motion during object release and post-release due to the lack of such data.

stated_limitations.text: Hand-object collision is disabled because motion-capture noise causes interpenetration; the object is moved by extra actuators rather than physically by the hand.
stated_limitations.quote: Due to the noise in motion capture, the data may contain moderate interpenetration between the hand and object model during grasping. We thus disable the collision detection

stated_limitations.text: Baselines assume perfect perception (ground-truth hand and object states), so reported times exclude perception latency.
stated_limitations.quote: we assume a perfect perception and focus the evaluation solely on planning and control capabilities.

stated_limitations.text: Simulation and real results are offset: real success rates are higher (cooperative users) and real efficiency lower (perception and control latency).
stated_limitations.quote: Despite the correlation, we also see an offset between the performance in real and simulation.
stated_limitations.section: V Experiments, Correlation with Real-World Evaluation

failure_modes: OMG Planner fails mainly by robot-human contact (27.78 percent) since it ignores hand position.
Reactive system of Yang et al. drops objects more often (11.81 percent) due to high accelerations.
GA-DDPG (hold) times out often (25.69 percent) from grasping wrong locations given ambiguous point clouds.
GA-DDPG without hold reaches only 36.81 percent success, contacting the hand or knocking objects while they still move, as it was trained only on static objects.
Two objects (master chef can, wood block) removed due to gripper capacity limits.
future_work: Train handover policies within the benchmark environment (none of the baselines were trained on it).
Realistic simulation of release and post-release human motion once data exists (implied by stated lack of data).
restrictive_assumptions: Human giver motion replayed from DexYCB mocap; single hand (right or left), 20 YCB rigid objects with known meshes.
Giver and robot face each other across a table; giver waits still at the end pose.
Ground-truth hand and object states given to policies; ground-truth segmentation for point-cloud baseline.
Franka Panda parallel-jaw gripper; simple PD controller; rigid-body PyBullet physics, no soft-body hand.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best baseline 64.58 percent (Yang et al.); OMG Planner 62.50 percent; GA-DDPG w/o hold 36.81 percent.

benchmark_gaps.dataset: HandoverSim S1 vs real user study
benchmark_gaps.observation: GA-DDPG 55.00 percent in sim versus 80 percent real; offset attributed to cooperative real users.

benchmark_gaps.dataset: HandoverSim S1 vs real user study
benchmark_gaps.observation: Yang et al. 4.758 s accumulated in sim versus 10.7 s real approach time, sim excludes perception latency.

open_problems_listed: Handover evaluation requires a real human in the loop, which is expensive and hard to reproduce.
Different studies adopt different settings and metrics, making cross-study comparison difficult.
Simulating a realistic human agent and its interaction with the robot during handover.
Contact-rich hand-object interaction needs high-fidelity physics, including soft-body dynamics.
Learning to control a dexterous simulated human hand to manipulate objects is notoriously hard.
Human motion that adapts to the robot is not modelled.
No data exists for human hand motion during release and post-release.
Sim-to-real offset in success rate and timing.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet simulate an adaptive, physically interacting human giver for handovers, so evaluation still relies on replayed non-reactive motion or costly real users.

papers.title: ATTACH Dataset: Annotated Two-Handed Assembly Actions for Human Action Understanding
papers.problem_statement: Existing assembly action datasets are mostly single-label and simplistic, so they do not represent workers performing different simultaneous actions with each hand, which cobots need to understand.

stated_limitations.text: Azure Kinect skeletons represent fingers only very roughly, limiting finger-focused action perception; hand pose estimation is left as future work.
stated_limitations.quote: the estimation of hand poses could provide further information for skeleton-based approaches when trying to perceive actions focused on the fingers, which are only very roughly represented by the Azure Kinect skeletons.

stated_limitations.text: In at least one view the person and action are always partially obscured by furniture parts, making the view split a major challenge.
stated_limitations.quote: in at least one of the views, the person and the action performed are always partially obscured by furniture parts.

stated_limitations.text: Offline detection uses future frames, which is not practical for a cobot that must detect live.
stated_limitations.quote: Since a cobot is supposed to detect actions live and not after a few minutes, such a detection is not practical for our use case.

failure_modes: Cross-view generalization is poor: recognition accuracy on the view split is roughly half that on the person split.
GCN skeleton methods generalize across views worse than the CNN method (VA-CNN).
Swin-based detection degrades at large clip lengths, possibly due to small fixed-size feature vectors.
Online detection is marginally worse than offline.
future_work: Hand pose estimation to supply finger-level information for skeleton-based action understanding.
Further action understanding tasks using the high-resolution recordings.
restrictive_assumptions: Three static calibrated Azure Kinect cameras around a single worktable; ArUco cube calibration.
Single worker per recording, IKEA cabinet assembly only.
Body skeletons from the Azure Kinect body tracking SDK, without finger detail.
No 3D object poses or hand-object geometry annotated; only action labels.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best 33.2 percent (VA-CNN) and 30.4 percent (Swin) versus 57.4 percent on person split.
Best 29.5 percent offline person split; only 10.7-11.3 percent on view split.

open_problems_listed: Recognizing simultaneous, overlapping fine-grained actions of both hands during assembly.
Generalization across camera viewpoints (mobile cobot sees new perspectives); view split is a major challenge.
Background-independent action understanding, since training data for the target environment often cannot be recorded.
Online, low-latency action detection on embedded hardware for cobots.
Finger-level action perception, as body skeletons only roughly represent fingers.
Large variance in action duration (0.2 s to minutes) and execution across skill levels.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet recognize overlapping two-handed assembly actions robustly across unseen viewpoints, nor capture finger-level detail from body-tracking skeletons.

papers.title: Ego-Exo4D: Understanding Skilled Human Activity from First- and Third-Person Perspectives
papers.problem_statement: Existing ego-exo datasets are few, small, lack synchronization, or are too staged, so moving fluidly between first- and third-person perspectives to understand skilled activity is out of reach.

stated_limitations.text: Exo camera placement is hard to optimize; the action is often occluded by the person in most static exo cameras, affecting annotation.
stated_limitations.quote: Often, the action is occluded by the person in the majority of the exo camera due to the standard and static positioning of these cameras.

stated_limitations.text: Data are long-tailed due to natural activity durations (9x more cooking than soccer), which may challenge model training.
stated_limitations.quote: the data is long-tailed due to the natural durations of activities.

stated_limitations.text: Only 70 percent of captures achieved frame-accurate automatic sync; the rest were manually synced with lower accuracy.
stated_limitations.quote: In practice, 70% of recorded captures yielded frame-accurate sync through our automated pipeline.

stated_limitations.text: Real-world capture with five or fewer cameras brings more occlusion and limited hand view and resolution from distant cameras.
stated_limitations.quote: This introduces challenges like increased occlusions from body and objects along with limited view and resolution of hands from distant cameras.

stated_limitations.text: Lower body pose and temporal consistency need further refinement.
stated_limitations.quote: further refinement is possible, especially in lower body pose estimation and to ensure temporal consistency in predictions.

failure_modes: Ego-to-exo correspondence fails on heavily occluded, very small objects in exo views.
Exo-to-ego translation baselines estimate object visibility at chance level (about 50 percent).
Hand pose errors are largest for thumb and fingertips, which are more often occluded.
Hand pose error increases as fewer views see a joint (PA-MPJPE 14.01 mm at 3 views vs 10.02 mm at 6).
Late fusion of ego and exo views does not improve proficiency estimation.
Future keystep prediction gains are limited.
future_work: Study detailed hand pose including hand-object interactions together with full body pose in real-world recordings.
Compare actor and observer reflections using narrations and expert commentary.
Better view-invariant learning and use of exo views for ego keystep recognition.
Personalized skill feedback and life-long skill monitoring.
General 3D vision uses: environment reconstruction, camera relocalization.
restrictive_assumptions: Single-person skilled activities only.
Aria glasses plus 4-5 static exocentric GoPros, synchronized with QR-code timers.
Hand pose evaluation restricted to joints visible in at least 3 cameras.
Ego pose benchmark excludes exo video and other modalities at test time.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best baseline POTTER 30.57 MPJPE / 11.14 PA-MPJPE (manual GT); THOR-net 51.24 MPJPE.
Best test MPJPE 18.51 cm (location-based); EgoEgo 26.38 cm.
pix2pix-mask 56.2 percent and GNT-mask 50.0 percent, near random guess.
Best test accuracy 41.53 percent (VI Encoder).
ActionFormer absolute mAP fairly low; task described as very challenging.

open_problems_listed: Ego-exo object correspondence under extreme viewpoint change, heavy occlusion and many small objects.
Exo-to-ego translation: predicting object location, shape and visibility in the ego view.
View-invariant learning and harnessing exo views for ego keystep recognition.
Energy-efficient multimodal online keystep recognition.
Procedure understanding, especially future keystep prediction.
Skill proficiency estimation (demonstrator and demonstration level), including effective ego-exo fusion.
Ego body pose from monocular ego video or IMU, especially lower body and temporal consistency.
Ego hand pose under occlusion, out-of-view hands and subtle skilled motion.
Joint hand pose, hand-object interaction and full body pose in real-world recordings.
Optimizing exo camera placement to avoid self-occlusion.
Long-tailed activity distribution and differing skill challenge across domains.
Robust time synchronization across heterogeneous cameras.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet estimate hand and body pose robustly from egocentric or sparse real-world views under occlusion, nor relate objects reliably across ego and exo views.

papers.title: Towards Human-Level Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation with Reinforcement Learning
papers.problem_statement: Achieving human-level dexterity with two hands is hard due to high degrees of freedom and required cooperation among heterogeneous agents; existing RL lacks a benchmark for bimanual dexterous skills.

stated_limitations.text: The benchmark does not support deformable object manipulation; tasks only cover articulated rigid bodies.
stated_limitations.quote: the limitation of Bi-DexHands is that it does not support the deformable object manipulation tasks.

stated_limitations.text: Policies use state-based observations unavailable in the real world, hindering sim-to-real transfer.
stated_limitations.quote: our tasks primarily train with policies with a state-based observation space, which is difficult for sim-to-real transfer because such inputs are not available in the real world.

stated_limitations.text: Multi-task and meta RL largely fail across tasks.
stated_limitations.quote: existing RL algorithms fail to work in most of the multi-task and the few-shot learning settings

stated_limitations.text: Point-cloud visual input is very slow in Isaac Gym (200+ fps vs 30000+ for state), limiting environments to 256, so visual baselines were not used.
stated_limitations.quote: the point cloud RL has only 200+ fps, and the full state can reach 30000+.

failure_modes: SAC fails on almost all tasks (attributed to massive parallelism favouring on-policy RL and entropy instability in 50+ action dimensions).
Multi-task PPO and ProMP barely exceed random policy on MT/ML settings.
Point-cloud input underperforms full-state input.
IQL improves only on some offline datasets due to severe out-of-distribution actions.
RL difficulty rises with tasks matched to older human ages; RL reaches about 48-month infant level.
future_work: Learning from human demonstration data.
Soft-body and deformable object simulation.
Algorithmic advances in meta/multi-task RL to solve all tasks.
Sim-to-real transfer to real dexterous hands.
Visual-input RL for sim-to-real.
restrictive_assumptions: Simulation only (Isaac Gym) with two Shadow Hands.
Full ground-truth state observations.
Rigid and articulated objects only.
Requires thousands of parallel environments for sample efficiency.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Multi-task PPO 8.9 versus per-task ground truth 32.5.
ProMP 0.02/0.36 versus ground truth 33.7/26.1; random 0.27 on test.

open_problems_listed: Multi-task and meta RL generalization across bimanual dexterous tasks.
Learning from demonstration for dexterous bimanual manipulation.
Simulation of soft bodies and deformable objects.
Sim-to-real transfer of learned dexterous skills.
Visual (point cloud or image) observations at high simulation throughput.
Off-policy RL instability with high-dimensional action spaces and massive parallelism.
Offline RL under severe distribution shift in large state/action spaces.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet learn generalizable bimanual dexterous skills from realistic (visual) observations that transfer from simulation to real hands.

papers.title: ADL4D: Towards A Contextually Rich Dataset for 4D Activities of Daily Living
papers.problem_statement: Existing 4D hand-object interaction datasets are limited to one subject interacting with one object, lacking the spatial and temporal context of multi-object, multi-subject activities, which restricts generalization of learned HOI methods.

stated_limitations.text: Keypoints from aggregated 2D estimators are triangulated with SVD; learnable triangulation or epipolar transformers could improve results.
stated_limitations.quote: The results can still be improved by using a learnable triangulation approach

stated_limitations.text: Deep-learning annotation methods generalize poorly across datasets early in data collection and need similar training data.
stated_limitations.quote: in the early stages of data collection, the deep-learning-based methods have a bad cross-dataset generalization

stated_limitations.text: Dynamic Matching needs a hand detected in at least 3 views and often failed to isolate all hands in early annotation due to weak detectors.
stated_limitations.quote: our initial batches of data annotation are often unable to isolate all hands of users, primarily due to insufficient detections caused by lower detector performance.

stated_limitations.text: A fixed clustering threshold fails when hand speed varies, e.g. two hands close together moving slowly versus sudden motion.
stated_limitations.quote: a fixed threshold may however fail to annotate all frames for a full sequence.

stated_limitations.text: Search criteria are inconsistent across datasets and must be tuned per multi-camera system.
stated_limitations.quote: the search criteria hyper-parameters like cluster size threshold should be tuned for every multi-camera system separately.

failure_modes: Plain Dynamic Matching leaves 2005 of 6815 frames unannotated on ADL4D with 18.30 mm MPJPE.
Even the best configuration skips 226 frames on ADL4D.
When search fails to find a valid cluster, the last successful cluster is reused.
Rolling-shutter colour imagers on D435 produce blurry frames under normal indoor light; spotlights were needed.
Cross-dataset hand mesh recovery errors exceed 33 mm.
future_work: Learnable triangulation or epipolar transformers to refine keypoints.
Use hand-level action labels for action-to-motion generative HOI models beyond pick-up, grasp and handover.
restrictive_assumptions: 8 calibrated RealSense D435 RGB-D cameras plus 8 OptiTrack mocap cameras with markers on objects.
12 pre-scanned rigid object meshes with markers.
Hands tracked marker-free but need detection in at least 2-3 views.
Extra spotlights required to avoid motion blur; 20 fps synchronized capture.
Software synchronization; up to two subjects.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Within-dataset about 12-14 mm but cross-dataset 33.34-54.76 mm.
Best 55.04 percent accuracy and F1@50 33.78 with pose features; I3D 32.77 and 7.12.
Best tracking mode still skips 226 frames and has 5.94 mm MPJPE versus manual labels.

open_problems_listed: Existing 4D HOI datasets limited to one subject and one object, restricting generalization.
Maintaining consistent 3D hand tracking over long activity sequences.
Marker-free annotation methods rely on 60-90 fps, short sequences and at most two hands.
Very large camera rigs add cost, synchronization and hardware burden.
Hands are visually similar with fine articulation, weakening trajectory continuity.
Marker-based hand capture biases detectors toward markers.
Multi-view annotation systems are prone to failure with multiple actively moving objects.
Generative action-based HOI animation limited to pick-up, grasp or handover.
Bad cross-dataset generalization of learned annotators and HMR models.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet automatically and completely annotate 3D hands of multiple people handling multiple objects over long sequences without mocap for objects and manual intervention.

papers.title: HardMo: A Large-Scale Hardcase Dataset for Motion Capture
papers.problem_statement: Monocular human mesh recovery methods perform well on benchmarks but are vulnerable to unusual poses such as dance and martial arts, due to a data domain gap; failures concentrate in hand-wrist and foot-ankle misalignment.

stated_limitations.text: The work only addresses hand and foot misalignment; other challenges such as self-occlusion remain.
stated_limitations.quote: This paper only focuses on the misalignment of feet and hands. Apart from such hardcases, there still exist some other significant challenges, such as self-occlusion

stated_limitations.text: Automatic SMPL annotations from 4DHumans fail on extreme hand and foot postures and require mining and refinement.
stated_limitations.quote: SMPL annotations failed to meet our requirement for quality in some cases. We empirically find that the failures mainly derive from extreme hand and foot posture.

stated_limitations.text: Hand hardcase handling targets wrist rotation only, not precise finger postures.
stated_limitations.quote: we do not consider the precise finger postures.

stated_limitations.text: Optimization-based label correction (SMPLify, EFT) damages other parts and can produce implausible poses.
stated_limitations.quote: these methods damage the annotation precision of other parts and may lead to implausible poses.

failure_modes: Existing methods (ProHMR, 4DHumans) recover hands and feet near T-pose in dance and martial arts.
ProHMR reaches 113.8 mm MPJPE on HardMo.
Pseudo-labels in existing datasets (Human3.6M, AIST++) show hands and feet near rest/T-pose.
future_work: Address self-occlusion and other hard cases.
Encourage mocap research centered on practical real-world settings.
restrictive_assumptions: Pseudo 3D labels from 4DHumans plus RTM-pose keypoints and learned refinement, not marker or multi-view mocap; test labels are optimized pseudo labels.
SMPL body model without articulated fingers or face.
Single-person monocular internet video of dance and martial arts.
Samples filtered by keypoint confidence thresholds (0.5, 0.65).

benchmark_gaps.observation: ProHMR 113.8 mm and HMR (InstaVariety) 61.1 mm versus HardMo-HMR 36.0 mm.
ProHMR 213.6 mm and 4DHumans-b 88.1 mm versus HardMo-HMR 34.9 mm.

open_problems_listed: Domain gap between standard mocap datasets and unusual real-world motions.
Limited diversity of hand and foot postures in synthetic datasets.
Incorrect hand and foot SMPL annotations in real datasets.
Common keypoint formats lack hand and foot keypoints.
Self-occlusion in hard poses.
Marker or markerless capture of skilled dance and martial arts is prohibitively expensive.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet recover correct hand-wrist and foot-ankle articulation in unusual poses from monocular video without targeted pseudo-labelled hardcase data.

papers.title: WorldPose: A World Cup Dataset for Global 3D Human Pose Estimation
papers.problem_statement: Existing pose datasets are mostly single-person or lab-bound multi-person; none cover large groups moving over open outdoor areas with moving cameras, so global relative positions over long trajectories cannot be evaluated.

stated_limitations.text: Annotation pipeline depends on 2D detection quality and static camera layout.
stated_limitations.quote: A limitation of our method is its reliance on the quality of the 2D detections and the arrangement of the static cameras

stated_limitations.text: Costly manual correction was needed for poorly covered or blurry players.
stated_limitations.quote: expensive manual interventions were required when a player was not adequately covered or when the image was blurry

stated_limitations.text: Only male matches, so gender representation is unequal.
stated_limitations.quote: Another limitation is that the data focuses on male events, resulting in an unequal gender representation among the participants.

stated_limitations.text: Fitting SMPL to triangulated 3D joints lacks a pose prior and can yield unrealistic poses with low reprojection error.
stated_limitations.quote: the resulting poses lack prior knowledge of feasible 3D poses, which can lead to the reconstruction of unrealistic poses which happen to have low reprojection errors.

stated_limitations.text: Commercial broadcast calibration normally needs a pre-game scan that was unavailable, so 3D poses were used as extra constraints.
stated_limitations.quote: the software requires a pre-game scan by the camera operator, which is not available to us.

stated_limitations.text: Pipeline accuracy against Vicon is about 8 cm G-MPJPE and 6.6 cm PA-MPJPE, measured only in the penalty box with 6 players.
stated_limitations.quote: We observe that the system was able to achieve a very low 6.6 cm error w.r.t. PA-MPJPE and 8.0 cm error w.r.t. G-MPJPE

failure_modes: GLAMR places players on a tilted plane when the camera principal axis is not parallel to the floor, and only uses the trajectory of player id 0, misplacing distant players.
SLAHMR motion-chunk optimization diverges when players are far apart, under fast camera motion and large focal length; fails on up to half of chunks for some sequences even with GT cameras.
DROID-SLAM camera estimates fail on the nearly textureless pitch with highly dynamic audience background.
Global methods get relative positions between players wrong even with a shared ground plane.
SLAHMR produces overly smooth motion, missing fast movements, and shows mesh gaps between non-overlapping chunks; 40 minutes per 100 frames with 4 subjects.
GLAMR and SLAHMR have worse PA-MPJPE than their own initializers (HybrIK, 4DHuman).
future_work: Expand the dataset beyond male events when data access allows.
Initialize and regularize SMPL fits using 2D-based estimators on zoomed broadcast footage.
Methods that handle large movement areas, inter-person relative placement, and unreliable SLAM cameras (textureless background, changing focal length).
restrictive_assumptions: Ground truth requires a calibrated multi-view static stadium camera system (VAR-style infrastructure).
Thorough manual review and correction of 2D detections and associations.
Soccer field markings and planar-field prior for calibration.
Broadcast camera calibration relies on commercial software plus triangulated player poses.
Validation against Vicon only in a small sub-area (penalty box) at night.

benchmark_gaps.observation: GLAMR 18888.9, SLAHMR 8334.1, SLAHMR with GT cameras 5837.2; per-person alignment still 3749.7 to 4699.5.
GLAMR 53.3, SLAHMR 17.6, SLAHMR with GT cameras 10.7.
SLAHMR 163.9 and GLAMR 85.2 are worse than their initializers 4DHuman 116.5 and HybrIK 78.8.

open_problems_listed: Global methods struggle when the area of movement expands.
Determining relative positions between multiple people, even with a shared ground plane.
Degraded performance when SLAM camera poses are unreliable due to texture-less backgrounds or changing focal length.
Marker-based capture is impractical over vast areas; body-worn sensors drift under dynamic motion.
Calibrating fast-moving broadcast cameras with few distinctive pitch features.
Low player resolution, fast motion and frequent occlusion degrade SOTA 2D detectors.
Unequal gender representation in the dataset.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Monocular global pose methods cannot yet recover accurate world-frame trajectories and relative positions of many people over large areas from a moving, zooming camera.

papers.title: Systematic Comparison of Projection Methods for Monocular 3D Human Pose Estimation on Fisheye Images
papers.problem_statement: Fisheye undistortion methods have not been systematically evaluated for absolute 3D human pose estimation from monocular fisheye images when poses span a wide field of view, e.g. close-up robot viewpoints.

stated_limitations.text: All experiments use ground-truth bounding boxes; a real detector would be needed in deployment.
stated_limitations.quote: To ensure detector-independent results, all experiments are conducted using GT bounding boxes. In real-world usage, they would be provided by a person detector.

stated_limitations.text: Method requires known intrinsics of the physical fisheye camera.
stated_limitations.quote: Its intrinsics are required input for our method.

stated_limitations.text: No projection is best for relative pose estimation overall.
stated_limitations.quote: For relative pose estimation, no single best practice emerges.

stated_limitations.text: Pinhole projection is weakest for absolute pose regardless of FOV.
stated_limitations.quote: PH remains the weakest model for absolute pose estimation

stated_limitations.text: Ground truth is pseudo-GT from multi-view triangulation of 2D detector outputs, not marker-based.
stated_limitations.quote: It includes accurate 3D pseudo-ground truth obtained through multi-view triangulation from time-synchronized cameras.

stated_limitations.text: Skeleton format differs from training data; a linear mapping had to be trained on a held-out FISHnCHIPS subset.
stated_limitations.quote: We thus need to apply a mapping between training skeleton formats and our skeleton format.

failure_modes: Pinhole reprojection error rises rapidly for poses covering more than about 120 degrees FOV (close-up subjects under 1 m); MPJPE grows from about 115 mm at 50 deg MPJA to over 250 mm at 150 deg.
Central cylindrical projection underperforms due to its limited 180 degree vertical FOV across camera orientations.
Reprojecting a fisheye image to pinhole format causes significant information loss.
future_work: No explicit future work stated beyond the bounding-box heuristic for choosing projection; paper offers insights for fisheye HPE in human-robot interaction.
restrictive_assumptions: Calibrated fisheye intrinsics (double sphere model) must be known.
Ground-truth bounding boxes instead of a detector.
Single-frame, non-temporal MeTRAbs trained only on pinhole data.
Indoor household scenes only, 7 subjects, 3 setups, data downsampled to 5 Hz.
Pseudo-GT from 10-camera triangulation including Kinects.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best absolute error still about 204-205 mm (EC 204.4, DS 205.2); PH 219.4.
Best only 45.5% (DS, EF); PH 41.5%.
Relative MPJPE exceeds 250 mm at 150 degree MPJA; hybrid heuristic improves MPJPE by only 2 mm.

open_problems_listed: No systematic comparison of fisheye handling methods for 3D HPE existed.
Upward-facing (robot-height) fisheye views have not been addressed in any study.
Existing fisheye HPE datasets focus on egocentric AR/VR or downward surveillance; horizontal third-person datasets are not public.
Pinhole projection becomes infeasible for subjects close to the camera.
No single best projection for relative pose; choice depends on FOV covered by the person.
Research on 3D HPE using fisheye images is limited.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Monocular 3D pose estimators cannot yet deliver accurate absolute 3D pose for people very close to a wide-FOV robot camera without known intrinsics and hand-chosen projections.

papers.title: Benchmarking 3D Human Pose Estimation Models Under Occlusions
papers.problem_statement: 2D-to-3D lifting models are evaluated on controlled Human3.6M with clean or randomly masked inputs, which does not reflect real-world occlusions; their robustness to realistic occlusion-induced 2D noise is unknown.

stated_limitations.text: All lifting models degrade under occlusion; diffusion models underperform.
stated_limitations.quote: all models exhibit notable performance degradation under occlusion, with diffusion-based models underperforming despite their stochastic nature.

stated_limitations.text: No model is robust across the whole occlusion range.
stated_limitations.quote: no model was able to maintain consistent performance across the full occlusion spectrum

stated_limitations.text: Occlusion-aware DTF is robust under severe noise but worse on clean input.
stated_limitations.quote: Occlusion-aware models such as DTF showed improved robustness under severe occlusion but underperformed on clean inputs.

stated_limitations.text: Distal, high-DoF joints are error-prone even when visible.
stated_limitations.quote: keypoints with higher degrees of freedom, such as wrists and feet, are consistently more error-prone, even when not occluded.

stated_limitations.text: Diffusion lifters are too slow for real time.
stated_limitations.quote: these models are computationally expensive, requiring iterative sampling during inference, which further limits their practicality in real-time.

stated_limitations.text: Current models are not ready for real-world deployment.
stated_limitations.quote: Despite advances in 3D HPE, our results show that current models are not yet robust enough for real-world environments.

stated_limitations.text: Only one dataset with keypoint-level occlusion labels exists, so the benchmark relies on synthetic BlendMimic3D.
stated_limitations.quote: To the best of our knowledge, BlendMimic3D is the only 3D HPE dataset that provides explicit, frame-level and keypoint-level occlusion labels.

failure_modes: Original DTF collapses to about 302 mm MPJPE when occlusions last longer than its 81-frame interpolation window, leaving joints zeroed.
T3D-CNN fails to generalize beyond the fixed number of masked keypoints it was trained with; errors exceed 1000 mm in some test configurations.
Diffusion denoisers conditioned on corrupted 2D input propagate occlusion noise through all sampling steps.
Errors rise at subject-camera distances below about 2.5 m, underrepresented in Human3.6M training.
Wrists, feet, nose and head show the highest MPJPE under occlusion.
future_work: Uncertainty-aware or visibility-conditioned denoising and sampling less dependent on corrupted inputs.
Hybrid architectures combining frequency-domain smoothing with confidence-aware fusion.
Explicit per-joint modeling such as local corrective branches or keypoint-reliability modules.
Occlusion-aware models that generalize across viewing conditions and skeleton formats while keeping clean-input accuracy.
Longer temporal windows or learned occlusion-aware 2D reconstruction instead of interpolation; training with mixtures of occlusion patterns.
restrictive_assumptions: Occlusion simulated as zero-mean Gaussian noise added to ground-truth 2D keypoints using ground-truth occlusion labels.
Evaluation on synthetic BlendMimic3D only (test subject S2).
All models trained on Human3.6M and not retrained.
Single-person 2D-to-3D lifting only; no image-based or multi-view methods.

benchmark_gaps.observation: MixSTE rises from 69.46 (GT 2D) to 175.21 at sigma 0.05; DiffuPose reaches 223.32; FinePose 183.86.
Original DTF-GT outputs 301.91 mm at all noise levels; DTF variant best at sigma 0.05 with 95.70 but 93.37 at low noise versus 69.46 best clean.

open_problems_listed: Lifting models lack explicit occlusion modeling; existing training strategies are insufficient for real-world occlusions.
Diffusion-based lifters need alternative conditioning, uncertainty-aware denoisers or hybrid formulations.
Interpolation-based occlusion handling fails for prolonged realistic occlusions.
Masking-trained models do not generalize across occlusion counts and patterns.
Distal joints (wrists, feet) are inherently hard even when visible.
Camera-related distribution shift (close distances, unseen viewpoints) harms generalization.
Evaluation inconsistencies: hip keypoint normalization and skeleton format mismatches.
Standard benchmarks (Human3.6M, MPI-INF-3DHP) and global metrics do not reflect real-world complexity.
Diffusion models are computationally expensive for real-time use.
papers.field_cannot_yet: 3D pose lifters cannot yet keep accurate wrist and other distal-joint estimates under realistic, prolonged occlusion while also staying accurate on clean input.

papers.title: Validation of Human Pose Estimation and Human Mesh Recovery for Extracting Clinically Relevant Motion Data from Videos
papers.problem_statement: Markerless motion capture methods are rarely validated against sports-biomechanics gold standards (optical MoCap, IMUs) for clinically relevant kinematics, so their suitability for clinical decision-making is unclear.

stated_limitations.text: Markerless errors remain high relative to IMU and MoCap.
stated_limitations.quote: While the error of these technologies are still high when compared to both the IMU and MoCap, which are the current state-of-the-art

stated_limitations.text: Only simple 1D knee metrics were validated; complex biomechanics metrics need further study.
stated_limitations.quote: Further studies will be required to compare the tools when measuring more complex metrics from the field of sports biomechanics rather than these simpler 1D metrics.

stated_limitations.text: MoCap and IMUs remain preferred for maximum accuracy due to higher frequency and accuracy.
stated_limitations.quote: the gold standard to use for maximum accuracy is still MoCap and the IMUs due to both their higher recording frequencies and higher measurement accuracies.

stated_limitations.text: Modalities could not be hardware-synchronized; curves were aligned manually.
stated_limitations.quote: we manually shifted the time-series curves along the x-axis.

stated_limitations.text: Data quality still needs improvement; claim limited to low-speed clinical actions.
stated_limitations.quote: Overall, while there is still room for improvement when it comes to the quality of the data produced

failure_modes: MediaPipe knee angles start and end roughly 15 degrees below IMU and MoCap in squat-to-box; peak knee angle lower in sit-to-stand.
VIBE-based range of motion deviates from the other modalities.
Normal loose clothing gives wider spread in range of motion than tight MoCap clothing.
Self-occlusion causes incorrect landmarks or jitter; clothing and lighting affect predictions (cited from prior work).
future_work: Validate on more complex sports-biomechanics metrics beyond 1D knee biomarkers.
Further experiments on the effect of clothing on predicted pose.
Force-plate data collected but left for future studies.
restrictive_assumptions: 10 healthy adult participants without knee conditions.
Low-speed, well-defined actions (sit-to-stand, squat-to-box) chosen for consistent peaks.
Two fixed tripod cameras at 30 Hz, frontal and sagittal views.
Knee flexion only; IMU treated as reference in Bland-Altman analysis.
Manual temporal alignment of modalities.

benchmark_gaps.observation: MediaPipe offset of roughly 15 degrees at start and end of squat-to-box; VIBE range of motion deviates from other modalities.

open_problems_listed: Self-occlusion leads to incorrect landmark estimation or frame-to-frame jitter.
Clothing choice affects predicted pose and needs further testing.
Lighting affects pose accuracy.
Few studies validate markerless methods against biomechanics gold standards for clinical use.
Markerless capture lacks the recording frequency to detect small pathology-relevant changes.
Synchronizing heterogeneous capture modalities is difficult due to hardware limitations.
Complex sports-biomechanics metrics remain unvalidated.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Off-the-shelf monocular markerless capture cannot yet match marker or IMU accuracy and frequency for fine, clinically meaningful joint kinematics beyond simple low-speed 1D metrics.

papers.title: A Dataset and Evaluation for Complex 4D Markerless Human Motion Capture
papers.problem_statement: Benchmark success does not transfer to real videos because datasets are controlled, mostly single-person with limited occlusion; none combine synchronized multi-view RGB-D, marker-based ground truth and interactions of more than two people.

stated_limitations.text: Dataset captured with only three male actors.
stated_limitations.quote: The dataset was collected using three male actors and comprises 52 distinct action sequences

stated_limitations.text: D455 depth accuracy limits capture volume and activity design.
stated_limitations.quote: Therefore, camera placement and activity design were constrained and adjusted accordingly.

stated_limitations.text: Evaluated baselines are frame-based and ignore interaction and time.
stated_limitations.quote: all evaluated approaches operate on single frames without explicitly modeling multi-person interactions or temporal consistency.

stated_limitations.text: Marker tracking suffers dropout in tight multi-person interactions; extra marker clusters were added.
stated_limitations.quote: Capturing tightly coupled multi-person activities and interactions presents tracking challenges due to severe occlusions and marker dropout.

failure_modes: SPIN and HMR2.0 fail when inter-person occlusion corrupts 2D keypoints; SPIN refinement cannot recover plausible bodies.
PARE part-attention loses its advantage when torso and pelvis are occluded by body overlap.
Frame-based methods cannot maintain identity assignments and coherent trajectories when bodies overlap or exchange positions.
Depth variation as subjects move toward or away from cameras creates ambiguity.
future_work: Interaction-aware reconstruction.
Temporal reasoning for identity-consistent motion modeling.
Multi-view geometry-aware learning that better exploits RGB-D observations.
restrictive_assumptions: Professional 44-camera Vicon studio and 56-marker MoCap suits for ground truth.
Six hardware-synced RealSense D455 at 720p, 15 fps, within about 3 m optimal depth range.
Evaluation uses PA-MPJPE only with off-the-shelf weights, no fine-tuning.
Ground truth retargeted to SMPL 24-joint via Maya IK.

benchmark_gaps.observation: SPIN, PARE, HMR2.0, PersPose rise from about 39-82 on 3DPW to 151-180 on HUM4D; PersPose best.

open_problems_listed: Lack of interaction-aware modeling for multi-person scenes.
Insufficient robustness to severe occlusion and body overlap.
Limited exploitation of multi-view and temporal cues.
Standard datasets (Human3.6M, CMU Panoptic, HUMAN4D) are approaching saturation.
No dataset combines synchronized multi-view RGB-D, marker-based ground truth and interactions of more than two people.
Hardware-level sync across RGB-D sensors is often missing; small misalignments cause artifacts.
Generalization of HMR in tightly coupled social interactions remains unclear.
Identity switching and rapid position exchanges between similarly dressed people.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Markerless capture cannot yet reconstruct closely interacting, mutually occluding people with stable identities; errors roughly double to triple outside standard benchmarks.

papers.title: EMDB: The Electromagnetic Database of Global 3D Human Pose and Shape in the Wild
papers.problem_statement: Global (world-frame) human pose estimation from moving monocular cameras has little work because no comprehensive in-the-wild dataset gives accurate 3D pose, shape and global body and camera trajectories.

stated_limitations.text: No multi-person sequences because multiple EM systems interfere.
stated_limitations.quote: EMDB does not contain multi-person sequences, because using multiple EM systems requires non-trivial changes to avoid cross-talk and interference between sensors.

stated_limitations.text: No foot sensors since metal in floors disturbs EM readings.
stated_limitations.quote: Furthermore, there are no sensors on the feet as indoor floors often contain metal beams that would disturb the readings.

stated_limitations.text: Camera trajectory quality bounded by ARKit.
stated_limitations.quote: the quality of our camera trajectories is upper-bounded by the quality of Apple’s AR toolkit.

stated_limitations.text: In-the-wild global trajectories drift: 23.4 cm over 81 m indoors, 73.0 cm over 112 m outdoors.
stated_limitations.quote: For an indoor sequence of 81 meters, this error is 23.4 cm

failure_modes: Baseline monocular methods fail to capture lower-arm rotations, which MPJPE does not reveal.
GLAMR global predictions drift significantly from ground truth (G-MPJPE 3193 mm).
Monocular methods show high jitter, high angular errors over 23 degrees and high standard deviations even with GT boxes.
Good MPJPE-PA does not translate to visually pleasing results.
future_work: Use EMDB to improve monocular local and global pose estimation.
restrictive_assumptions: Up to 12 body-worn wireless EM sensors with source on the lower back.
Per-subject minimal-clothing scan in a multi-view volumetric studio and calibration sequence for skin-to-sensor offsets.
Hand-held iPhone RGB-D with ARKit poses; clap-based synchronization.
Single person; baselines given ground-truth bounding boxes; fully occluded frames excluded.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best method HybrIK exceeds 65 mm despite GT bounding boxes.
All methods exceed 23 degrees mean angular error.
GLAMR 3193 mm, G-MVE 3203 mm.

open_problems_listed: Little work on global pose estimation due to lack of in-the-wild datasets with global trajectories.
Camera-relative weak-perspective settings are too restrictive for moving-camera applications.
Static multi-camera systems restrict outdoor use; egocentric systems have self-occlusion or fixed volumes.
IMU drift and lack of positional measurements constrain pose diversity and accuracy (3DPW).
Multi-person EM capture needs handling of cross-talk.
MPJPE-PA is forgiving; angular error, jitter and standard deviation are neglected.
Monocular RGB methods have ample room for improvement in pose and global trajectory.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Monocular methods cannot yet recover drift-free world-frame human trajectories and accurate limb rotations from a moving hand-held camera in the wild.

papers.title: BEDLAM: A Synthetic Dataset of Bodies Exhibiting Detailed Lifelike Animated Motion
papers.problem_statement: HPS progress entangles architecture and training data; prior synthetic datasets were too small, unrealistic or lacked realistic clothing, so synthetic data alone had not sufficed for real-image accuracy.

stated_limitations.text: Licensing blocks use of many high-quality commercial assets.
stated_limitations.quote: There are many high-quality commercial assets that we did not use in this project because their licences restrict their use in neural network training.

stated_limitations.text: Motions are random, uncorrelated with clothing and scene, and lack interactions.
stated_limitations.quote: Additionally, people interact with each other and with objects in the world. Methods are needed to automatically synthesize such interactions realistically [99].

stated_limitations.text: Few sitting, lying, complex sports poses.
stated_limitations.quote: the current dataset has relatively few sitting, lying, and complex sports poses, which are problematic for cloth simulation.

stated_limitations.text: Hands interacting with objects largely missing.
stated_limitations.quote: There is very little mocap data with the full body and hands and even less with hands interacting with objects.

stated_limitations.text: No facial motion and no evaluation datasets for body plus face.
stated_limitations.quote: Here we ignored facial motion; there are currently no datasets that evaluate full body and facial motion.

stated_limitations.text: Hair lacks physics and diversity; hair cards cause artifacts.
stated_limitations.quote: BEDLAM lacks hair physics, long hairstyles, and hair color diversity.

stated_limitations.text: Cloth simulation fails for high-BMI bodies.
stated_limitations.quote: Note that draping high-BMI models in clothing is challenging because the mesh self-intersects, causing failures of the cloth simulation.

stated_limitations.text: Bodies are barefoot; textures lack realistic reflectance.
stated_limitations.quote: BEDLAM bodies are barefoot.

stated_limitations.text: Accuracy still depends on real-image backbone pre-training.
stated_limitations.quote: We find that HPS accuracy depends on backbone pre-training.

failure_modes: Training backbones from scratch on BEDLAM gives worse results than COCO-pretrained backbones.
Hair-card rendering produces ghosting at fast motion and low frame rates; hue shifts and black hair under ray-traced HDRI shadows.
High-BMI cloth simulation and motion retargeting fail frequently.
future_work: More open-source assets; correlated motions, clothing and scenes; realistic human-human and human-object interactions.
Strand-based hair, uniform body-shape distribution including children and atypical bodies, better skin textures, shoes.
Methods estimating humans in world coordinates and exploiting temporal information and action semantics.
Support for SMPL, GHUM and SUPR body models.
restrictive_assumptions: Motions randomly sampled from AMASS with GRAB hand motions pasted on; no object contact.
Mostly static cameras with randomized extrinsics.
Multiple people placed to avoid collision rather than interact.
Evaluation of single-frame regressors (HMR, CLIFF).

benchmark_gaps.observation: Table numbers not extracted; paper states methods trained on BEDLAM do not estimate world coordinates or use temporal information.

open_problems_listed: Licence restrictions on commercial assets impede research; more open-source assets needed.
Synthesizing realistic human-human and human-object interactions automatically.
Correlating motions with clothing and scenes.
Few sitting, lying and sports poses due to cloth simulation difficulty.
Hair physics, long hair and hair color diversity.
Body-shape diversity: children, scoliosis, amputees; high-BMI draping and retargeting.
Realistic skin textures and reflectance.
Shoes that change posture and gait.
Very little mocap with full body plus hands interacting with objects.
No datasets evaluating full body and facial motion.
Estimating humans in world coordinates; exploiting temporal information and action semantics.
Removing dependence on real-image backbone pre-training.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Synthetic human data cannot yet realistically render people interacting with objects or each other, especially hands manipulating objects.

papers.title: BEDLAM2.0: Synthetic humans and cameras in motion
papers.problem_statement: Estimating human motion in world coordinates under both human and camera motion is limited by lack of video data with ground-truth human and camera movement; BEDLAM had limited focal lengths and camera motions.

stated_limitations.text: Only human-ground interaction; no objects.
stated_limitations.quote: A key limitation of B1 and B2 is that they only support people interacting with the ground and not with other objects.

stated_limitations.text: Realistic synthetic human-object and human-human interaction remains open.
stated_limitations.quote: Generating realistic synthetic sequences of general human-object and human-human interaction remains an open research problem but is clearly the next step for the field.

stated_limitations.text: Non-foot body-scene contacts may be inaccurate (e.g. hands in cartwheels).
stated_limitations.quote: other than foot-ground contact, other body-scene contacts may not be accurate

stated_limitations.text: Motions not semantically meaningful in scene or relative to other people.
stated_limitations.quote: the motions in B2 are not semantically meaningful in the context of the scene or the motions of other humans in the scene.

stated_limitations.text: Visual domain gap to real video remains.
stated_limitations.quote: And, of course, there is a still a visual domain gap between B2 and real videos.

stated_limitations.text: No facial motion or audio.
stated_limitations.quote: An important direction for future work is to add facial motions and audio, which are completely lacking in B1 and B2.

stated_limitations.text: Removing unsupported motions (sitting, stairs) hurts accuracy on such scenes.
stated_limitations.quote: This actually reduces accuracy on scenarios like stair climbing in EMDB relative to B1.

failure_modes: Training on B2 alone underperforms B1 on EMDB motions absent from B2, such as stair climbing.
Training CameraHMR on B1 plus B2 gives no clear advantage over B2 alone.
future_work: Synthetic human-object and human-human interaction with contact.
Facial motion and audio for human-human communication.
Children, amputees, atypical morphologies, impaired movement, assistive devices.
Use for 4D point tracking, non-rigid SfM, depth, optical flow, dynamic scene reconstruction.
restrictive_assumptions: Motions exclude actions depending on external objects (sitting) or non-ground support (stairs).
Hand motions randomly sampled from ARCTIC and attached to AMASS bodies, not coordinated with objects.
Only flat-soled shoes.
3D environments cannot be redistributed.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best is PromptHMR trained on B1+B2 at 193.7; GVHMR on B2 284.4.
GVHMR on B2 alone 113.7, slightly worse than on B1 112.4.

open_problems_listed: General human-object and human-human interaction synthesis is open.
Body-scene contact beyond feet is inaccurate.
Motions lack semantic meaning relative to scene and other people.
No children, amputees or atypical morphologies; no impaired motion or assistive devices.
Visual domain gap to real videos.
Facial motion and audio absent.
Lack of ground-truth sequences limits 4D point tracking, non-rigid SfM, depth, flow and dynamic reconstruction.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Synthetic training data cannot yet supply realistic human-object contact and manipulation, so world-frame methods are trained without object interaction.

papers.title: SLOPER4D: A Scene-Aware Dataset for Global 4D Human Pose Estimation in Urban Environments
papers.problem_statement: Optical systems are unstable outdoors and lack global translation, RGB-D has limited range and fails outdoors, IMUs drift; prior human-scene capture decouples pose and scene, so no urban-scale multi-modal global HPE dataset with scene constraints exists.

stated_limitations.text: Single-person capture only, although multiple people appear in the data.
stated_limitations.quote: SLOPER4D is limited to single-person capture though it perceives multiple-person data.

stated_limitations.text: Camera and LiDAR are not synchronized online, so frame drops cause tedious offline work.
stated_limitations.quote: the camera and LiDAR are not synchronized online, causing tedious offline work if the camera loses frames even with a low time offset

stated_limitations.text: Camera texture is not used for color or texture reconstruction of scenes and humans.
stated_limitations.quote: texture information from the camera is not fully exploited for color and texture reconstruction of scenes and humans.

failure_modes: GLAMR global HPE fails worst on the high-pace, largest-area running scene: ATE RMSE 29.48 m and G-MPJPE 32329.3 mm on Running001.
Models trained on another LiDAR dataset only give the largest errors on SLOPER4D, indicating a domain gap between LiDAR sensors.
Pre-trained VIBE generalizes better to 3DPW than to SLOPER4D's camera modality.
future_work: An online camera-LiDAR synchronization algorithm.
Extend capture to multiple persons.
More research on global HPE in real-world interactive scenarios.
restrictive_assumptions: Subject wears a full IMU mocap suit while a second operator carries the head-mounted LiDAR plus camera.
Offline joint optimization with LiDAR SLAM, IMU poses and scene constraints to build ground truth.
Offline camera-LiDAR synchronization and per-frame calibration fine-tuning.
Single tracked subject per sequence.

benchmark_gaps.observation: 29.48 m ATE and 32329.3 mm G-MPJPE; global trajectories of high-dynamic activity remain far from solved.
264.6 mm MPJPE and PA-MPJPE 118.5 mm on dynamic football training.
Best case 86.3 mm on daily walking; still G-MPJPE 4407.0 mm.

open_problems_listed: Single-person limitation; multi-person urban capture is open.
Online synchronization of camera and LiDAR.
Exploiting camera texture for colored and textured reconstruction of scenes and humans.
Global human pose estimation in large outdoor scenes with high-dynamic activities.
Domain gap between different LiDAR sensors for LiDAR-based HPE.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet estimate globally accurate human trajectories and poses for fast, large-area activities from a moving monocular or LiDAR viewpoint.

papers.title: HSC4D: Human-Centered 4D Scene Capture in Large-Scale Indoor-Outdoor Space Using Wearable IMUs and LiDAR
papers.problem_statement: IMU mocap drifts over long captures, external cameras confine capture space, and camera-based self-localization (HPS) needs pre-built maps; no method captures human motion plus large scene from wearable sensors only.

stated_limitations.text: Depends on LiDAR SLAM for initial localization, so fails where LiDAR mapping fails.
stated_limitations.quote: it is limited when LiDAR mapping fails, such as crowded places, narrow areas, etc.

stated_limitations.text: Activities that occlude the body-mounted LiDAR are excluded.
stated_limitations.quote: some activities are limited in our system, such as sitting in a chair with a backrest, standing back against a wall.

stated_limitations.text: Hand-crafted optimization losses; rock climbing does not always work.
stated_limitations.quote: the optimization loss terms in our pipeline are hand-created. Some cases like rock climbing do not always work.

failure_modes: LiDAR SLAM fails in crowded places and narrow areas.
Large LiDAR occlusion by backrests or walls.
Rock climbing sequences do not always converge with hand-crafted losses.
Localization error grows linearly with distance travelled for all methods including HSC4D.
LiDAR alone increases local pose errors (foot contact) due to body jitter.
future_work: A more general loss term or a deep learning framework that uses semantic information.
restrictive_assumptions: Subject wears 17 Noitom IMUs plus body-mounted 64-beam LiDAR and mini-computer.
Body shape parameter assumed constant per recording.
A-pose start for coordinate calibration; offline synchronization and calibration.
Offline graph-based and joint optimization.
Static scene map from LiDAR SLAM.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Error increases linearly with distance for all methods; HSC4D improves 25.4% over LiDAR-only baseline but does not remove growth.

open_problems_listed: Robust capture when LiDAR mapping fails (crowded or narrow spaces).
Capture of activities that occlude the body-worn LiDAR.
Replacing hand-crafted losses for difficult motions such as climbing.
