papers.title: Scene-aware Egocentric 3D Human Pose Estimation
papers.problem_statement: Single head-mounted fisheye egocentric pose methods still produce body-environment penetration or body floating under self-occlusion and distortion, and no egocentric dataset carries scene geometry labels to train scene-aware estimation.

stated_limitations.text: Pose accuracy is bounded by the estimated scene depth, especially behind the body where the scene is occluded.
stated_limitations.quote: The accuracy of voxel-based pose estimation network is constrained by the accuracy of estimated depth, especially where the scene is occluded by the human body.

stated_limitations.text: The method works per single frame; temporal extension is left for future work.
stated_limitations.quote: In future, this method could be extended to estimate physically-plausible egocentric motion from a temporal sequence.

stated_limitations.text: The EgoPW-Scene training set is smaller than EgoPW because SfM reconstruction fails on some sequences.
stated_limitations.quote: The number of frames in the EgoPW-Scene dataset is less than EgoPW dataset since SfM fails on some sequences.

stated_limitations.text: Existing egocentric datasets lack camera pose and scene geometry, so human-scene interaction cannot be evaluated on them.
stated_limitations.quote: Evaluating human-scene interaction requires precise annotations for camera pose and scene geometry. However, such information is not available in existing datasets for egocentric human pose estimation.

failure_modes: Predicted depth that still includes the human body or has the body masked out degrades MPJPE (167.3 and 135.7 mm vs 118.5 mm).
Without the inpainting network, depth estimation shows artifacts in the body region (Abs-Rel 0.383 vs 0.107).
An optimization baseline with contact term fails when the initial pose is inaccurate, forcing non-contact joints into contact.
future_work: Extend to temporally consistent, physically plausible egocentric motion from sequences.
Use temporal information to obtain a full view of the surrounding environment behind the body.
restrictive_assumptions: Single head-mounted downward-facing fisheye camera
Real test set needs multi-view SfM scene scan and a calibration board rigidly attached to the egocentric camera for ground truth
Method is fine-tuned on the training split of the new test dataset before evaluation
Real-data scene labels come from SfM with scale recovered from known objects (laptops, chairs)
Static scene; no object manipulation modelled

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best result is still 118.5 / 92.75 mm; with ground-truth depth it drops only to 109.9 / 88.8 mm.
Prior methods Mo2Cap2, xR-egopose, EgoPW score 200.3, 241.3, 189.6 mm.

open_problems_listed: Recovering scene depth behind the body for egocentric views
Lack of egocentric datasets with scene geometry and camera pose labels
Temporal egocentric motion with physical plausibility
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet produce accurate, physically plausible egocentric full-body pose from one head-worn camera when the body occludes the scene it interacts with.

papers.title: EgoSim: An Egocentric Multi-view Simulator and Real Dataset for Body-worn Cameras during Motion and Activity
papers.problem_statement: Egocentric research focuses on head-mounted cameras that suffer self-occlusion, poor lower-body resolution and little environment context; no simulator or dataset exists for multiple body-worn cameras with realistic motion artifacts.

stated_limitations.text: Simulated avatars are animated independently from AMASS, so interactions with other humans or objects are not modelled.
stated_limitations.quote: These animations, while physically plausible, do not account for interactions with other humans or objects, limiting the study of such interactions.

stated_limitations.text: Only four scenes are simulated, limiting generalisation.
stated_limitations.quote: Additionally, our system currently features only four scenes, which can be extended to improve the generalization.

stated_limitations.text: A sim-to-real rendering gap remains.
stated_limitations.quote: improvements in graphics and neural rendering methods [ 100 ] are expected to reduce the simulation-to-real gap further.

stated_limitations.text: Global root position and orientation remain weak, with cumulative drift on long sequences.
stated_limitations.quote: there is still room for improvement in the global position and orientation estimation of the root, especially for long sequences, where cumulative errors in root position become more pronounced.

stated_limitations.text: Experiments use RGB only.
stated_limitations.quote: Moreover, our current experiments only utilize RGB data.

failure_modes: Direct sim-to-real and training on real data alone both fail to reach accurate pose (global MPJPE 0.77 m and 1.23 m).
Largest errors occur on fast-moving limbs; model sometimes hallucinates arm movement.
Root translation errors accumulate because the model predicts frame-to-frame relative transforms and lacks SLAM or SfM grounding.
Cross-scene transfer raises PA-MPJPE from about 0.04 m to 0.14-0.15 m, with arms badly predicted.
Cross-participant evaluation lags, indicating insufficient subject diversity.
Predictions are under-active: lower jerk than ground truth, not capturing full speed of motion.
future_work: Integrate low-drift camera localization (SLAM or SfM) for stable global translation and orientation.
Use MultiEgoView for inertial-based pose estimation, depth estimation and semantic scene classification.
Add human-human and human-object interactions and more scenes to the simulator.
Use better graphics or neural rendering to reduce the sim-to-real gap.
restrictive_assumptions: Six body-worn cameras at head, pelvis, wrists and knees
Real data captured in one university courtyard that was also scanned for simulation
Ground truth from Xsens IMU suit, synchronised by a clap
Pretraining on 119 h synthetic data required before fine-tuning on real data
Offline 5-second clips at 10 fps and 224x224

benchmark_gaps.observation: Even best fine-tuned model has 0.33 m global MPJPE and 0.31 m root translation error versus 0.044 m PA-MPJPE.
Training on scenes (1)(2) and testing on (3)(4) gives 0.148 vs 0.041 in-scene.
0.060 m and 16.6 deg versus 0.044 m and 10.2 deg on random split.

open_problems_listed: Simulated interactions between humans and with objects
More and more diverse scenes for generalisation
Sim-to-real rendering gap
Drift-free global root position and orientation over long sequences
Using non-RGB modalities: inertial-based pose, depth estimation, semantic scene classification
Cross-participant generalisation needing more subject diversity
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet estimate drift-free global body pose from body-worn cameras, nor simulate body-worn views of people interacting with objects.

papers.title: SynBody: Synthetic Dataset with Layered Human Models for 3D Human Perception and Modeling
papers.problem_statement: Real human datasets are hard to scale, and scan-based synthetic datasets are limited in subjects, carry fitting errors in 3D annotations, and cannot provide separate body and clothing annotations.

stated_limitations.text: Asset balance for body shapes and clothing is not guaranteed, risking bias.
stated_limitations.quote: other elements, such as body shapes and clothing, might not be as balanced, posing a potential for bias in the resultant human models.

stated_limitations.text: SMPL annotations cannot be derived directly from SMPL-XL and must be refit.
stated_limitations.quote: Although SMPL-XL naturally provides accurate SMPL-X annotations, SMPL cannot be derived directly. Thus, we need to refit the SMPL parameters.

stated_limitations.text: Loose garments and diverse motions remain challenging for human NeRF methods.
stated_limitations.quote: the diverse motions and appearances, as well as loose garments in SynBody, pose further challenges in the field of neural rendering of 3D humans.

stated_limitations.text: Contact labels for human-scene interaction are not yet included.
stated_limitations.quote: the high controllability of the synthetic dataset offers ample opportunities for further improvements, such as the incorporation of contact labels for human-scene interaction.

failure_modes: SURREAL-style rendering without cloth geometry or hair leads to significant performance degradation (Table 5).
Human NeRF methods are sensitive to the accuracy of estimated SMPL.
future_work: Methods that predict body and cloth simultaneously using layered annotations.
Adding contact labels for human-scene interaction.
restrictive_assumptions: Synthetic monocular RGB only; used as complement to real data, not alone
Motions retargeted from AMASS without object interaction
Procedural clothing attached to SMPL-X surface

benchmark_gaps.observation: Even with SynBody, PARE remains at 169.93 mm MPJPE and HMR at 199.51 mm.
Generalizable NHP reaches only 22.46 on novel identity versus 25-29 for person-specific views.

open_problems_listed: Joint prediction of body and clothing
Contact labels for human-scene interaction
Neural rendering of loose garments and diverse motions
Dataset asset balance and bias in body shapes and clothing
Accurate SMPL-X annotations for real images are difficult to obtain
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet obtain accurate layered body, clothing and contact annotations for real images at scale.

papers.title: Putting People in their Place: Monocular Regression of 3D People in Depth
papers.problem_statement: Multi-person mesh regressors reason in the image plane, struggle with occlusion, diverse body size and monocular depth ambiguity; existing 3D multi-person datasets lack height and age diversity to train or evaluate depth reasoning.

stated_limitations.text: Not trained for diverse weights, gender or ethnicity.
stated_limitations.quote: it is not trained to capture diverse weights, gender, ethnicity, etc.

stated_limitations.text: Assumes a constant focal length.
stated_limitations.quote: BEV also assumes a constant focal length.

stated_limitations.text: Not designed for large crowds.
stated_limitations.quote: BEV is not trained or designed to deal with large "crowds" (e.g. 100's of people).

stated_limitations.text: No modelling of contact between people; mesh intersections and missed contact occur.
stated_limitations.quote: Without modeling the contact between multiple people, BEV may miss obvious contact and cannot avoid mesh intersections.

stated_limitations.text: Fails with heavy occlusion and dense small subjects.
stated_limitations.quote: BEV is unable to handle occlusions with few visible parts and dense small-scale subjects in crowds.

stated_limitations.text: Weak depth/age labels are inconsistent across annotators and needed trained offline labellers.
stated_limitations.quote: we observe that people's judgments for such weak labels vary greatly. It is hard to obtain consistent weak labels through online platforms (e.g. AMT).

failure_modes: Missed contact and interpenetrating meshes between people in contact.
Fails on people with few visible parts.
Fails on dense, small-scale subjects in crowds.
Depth ambiguity for infants and children when height priors are wrong.
future_work: Use BEV as a foundation for exploring complex multi-person relationships in 3D.
restrictive_assumptions: Standard camera without radial distortion and fixed field of view (constant focal length)
Single RGB image
Relative depth layers and age groups as weak labels rather than metric depth
Moderate numbers of people, not crowds of hundreds

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best method reaches 68.27 overall and only 60.77 for babies, so about a third of depth relations are still wrong.
Prior methods score 41.6-57.5 overall and 30-39 for babies.

open_problems_listed: Lack of multi-person in-the-wild data with accurate 3D translation annotations
Depth-height ambiguity across ages
Modelling contact between multiple people
Heavy occlusion and dense crowds
Diversity in weight, gender, ethnicity
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet recover metric depth and contact-consistent 3D meshes for many overlapping people from one image without camera intrinsics.

papers.title: TRACE: 5D Temporal Regression of Avatars with Dynamic Cameras in 3D Environments
papers.problem_statement: Current HPS methods cannot reliably estimate moving humans in global coordinates, especially when the camera also moves, entangling human and camera motion; in-the-wild training data with global trajectories is lacking.

stated_limitations.text: DynaCam videos only approximate real dynamic-camera videos because camera motion is simulated by crops and panorama projection.
stated_limitations.quote: The videos generated with our process only approximate real DC-videos shot in the wild since they lack perspective effects.

stated_limitations.text: Camera motion is not explicitly estimated; only implied by a world motion map.
stated_limitations.quote: We do not explicitly estimate the camera motion. Instead, we use a world motion map to represent the global trajectory in world coordinates, which implies the camera motion.

stated_limitations.text: Corrected 3DPW results are worse than reported; an evaluation bug in a widely used PA-MPJPE function was found.
stated_limitations.quote: The computation of the per-frame PA-MPJPE was performed incorrectly in a widely used PA-MPJPE evaluation function.

stated_limitations.text: Metric accuracy in world coordinates is left as future work.
stated_limitations.quote: Future work should look at explicitly estimating the camera, using training data like BEDLAM [ 6 ] , which contains complex human motion, 3D scenes, and camera motions.

failure_modes: On 3DPW, corrected PA-MPJPE 50.8 mm is worse than all compared single-frame baselines (42.7-47.9 mm).
SLAM baselines fail with moving people; synthetic camera motions may also disadvantage them.
DynaCam pseudo-ground truth needs manual filtering of fitting failures.
future_work: Explicitly estimate the camera.
Train with data like BEDLAM containing complex motion, 3D scenes and camera motion.
Combine camera and human motion to recover metric world-coordinate motion.
restrictive_assumptions: Monocular RGB video
Training camera motion simulated from static or panoramic videos
DynaCam ground truth is pseudo-labels from 2D pose fitting plus PnP
Global trajectory evaluated after similarity alignment, not metric
GPU memory limits clips to 10 frames in training

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best ATE is 0.334 m (translating) and 0.475 m (rotating) even after similarity alignment.
Corrected TRACE 50.8 mm versus 42.7 mm for D&D and 43.0 mm for CLIFF.
Best HOTA is only 65.3.

open_problems_listed: Disentangling human and camera motion in dynamic-camera videos
Lack of in-the-wild training data with global trajectories and camera poses
Tracking through long occlusions in multi-person video
Metric-scale world-coordinate human motion
Evaluation-code bugs in widely used PA-MPJPE functions
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet recover metric-accurate world-coordinate human trajectories from moving monocular cameras with real camera-motion ground truth.

papers.title: Benchmarking 3D Pose and Shape Estimation Beyond Algorithms
papers.problem_statement: Human mesh recovery research focuses on algorithms while datasets, backbones and training strategies are rarely studied, producing suboptimal baselines and unfair comparisons across methods trained with different data mixes.

stated_limitations.text: Benchmarks are mainly run on HMR only.
stated_limitations.quote: Due to the large amount of experiments, we mainly perform the benchmarks on HMR, which is an important milestone work with straightforward architecture.

stated_limitations.text: Dataset selection and partitions are chosen manually using prior knowledge.
stated_limitations.quote: Currently we need to use prior knowledge to manually select the datasets and their partitions.

stated_limitations.text: Findings are empirical and not yet explained.
stated_limitations.quote: It is worth conducting deeper investigations to interpret and explain those findings, and obtain the optimal strategy.

stated_limitations.text: Pseudo-annotated test sets contain visible SMPL errors.
stated_limitations.quote: we found errors in our visualisation of the SMPL annotations, raising the concern if datasets with pseudo-annotations are suitable to be used as test benchmarks.

failure_modes: Error rises sharply when noisy SMPL samples exceed about 50 percent, and much more when keypoints are also noisy.
Replacing body-part pose parameters (e.g. hands, feet) with noise increases error by a large margin.
Adding more datasets (Mix 10) can harm accuracy.
H36M performance does not correlate with other test sets.
future_work: Extend benchmarks to more pose and mesh algorithms.
Automate dataset selection and partitions, for example with AutoML, reinforcement learning or Bayesian optimization.
Interpret and explain the empirical findings.
restrictive_assumptions: Monocular RGB single-person crops
3DPW-test as main benchmark
SMPL body model only

benchmark_gaps.observation: Saturation noted: benchmark is in 50+ mm range; best here 47.3 mm.
3DPW is the only large-scale real outdoor dataset with accurate SMPL ground truth.

open_problems_listed: Automatic selection of training datasets and their contributions
Fair comparison requires fixed dataset combination, backbone and initialisation
Need test sets with accurate mocap or simulation SMPL ground truth and large diversity
Suitability of pseudo-annotated datasets as test benchmarks
H36M not indicative of generalisation
Effect of augmentation depends on training-set characteristics
Explaining why the findings hold
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet fairly compare mesh-recovery algorithms because data mixes and noisy pseudo-labels dominate results and accurate diverse test sets are scarce.

papers.title: Recovering 3D Human Mesh from Monocular Images: A Survey
papers.problem_statement: Monocular human mesh recovery remains challenging due to 2D-to-3D ambiguity, flexible bodies, complex environment interactions and insufficient in-the-wild 3D annotations.

stated_limitations.text: Synthetic data lack realism; mocap data are confined to constrained settings.
stated_limitations.quote: The MoCap data is generally limited to constrained environments and lacks the diversity of subjects and actions.

stated_limitations.text: Benchmark comparisons are inconsistent across configurations.
stated_limitations.quote: However, the deployment and evaluation standards for comparison are not fully consistent.

stated_limitations.text: Whole-body recovery error rises sharply with hands and face.
stated_limitations.quote: this task is very challenging as the reconstruction error becomes much higher when taking face and hands into consideration.

stated_limitations.text: Interaction methods depend on pre-defined contact vertices, limiting generalization.
stated_limitations.quote: depend on pre-defined candidate contact vertices or pairs to constrain interaction, which limits the generalization to diverse scenes.

failure_modes: Ground penetration, foot skating and body leaning in reconstructions.
Severe jitter in frames with heavy occlusion or complex context.
Interpenetration with 3D scenes when scene is ignored.
EFT pseudo-labels may overfit when the body is partially invisible.
future_work: Robust recovery under heavy occlusion and multi-hypothesis outputs.
Stable reconstruction from videos without jitter.
Scene-constrained reconstruction beyond flat floors.
Unsupervised or self-supervised mesh recovery.
Grouped person reconstruction with tracking and re-identification.
Whole-body recovery with hands and face.
Detailed clothed shape reconstruction.
restrictive_assumptions: Scope limited to monocular RGB images and videos
Parametric body models SMPL/SMPL-X represent minimally clothed bodies
Scene-aware methods typically assume flat floors or pre-scanned static scenes

benchmark_gaps.observation: Errors become much higher when face and hands are included.

open_problems_listed: Robustness under heavy occlusions; multiple plausible reconstructions or pose distributions
Long-term motion jitter in video reconstruction
Reconstruction with scene constraints beyond flat floors
Learning beyond full supervision with unlabeled data
Grouped person reconstruction over space and time
Whole-body mesh recovery with scarce whole-body data and hand occlusion, blur, interaction
Detailed clothed shape beyond parametric models; over-smoothed and not robust to novel poses
Lack of realism in synthetic data and limited diversity in mocap data
Inconsistent evaluation standards across methods
Interaction methods relying on pre-defined contacts
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet reconstruct robust, jitter-free, scene-consistent whole-body meshes with hands under heavy occlusion from monocular input.

papers.title: Deep Learning for 3D Human Pose Estimation and Mesh Recovery: A Survey
papers.problem_statement: 3D pose estimation and mesh recovery still face multi-person scenarios, self-occlusion and detailed body reconstruction; prior reviews cover these tasks, implicit methods and future challenges only partially.

stated_limitations.text: Top-down methods depend on detection; bottom-up methods struggle with small figures.
stated_limitations.quote: Top-down methods depend heavily on human detection and are susceptible to detection inaccuracies, often leading to unreliable pose estimations in environments with multiple people.

stated_limitations.text: Explicit models lack detail; implicit models lack stability.
stated_limitations.quote: Explicit models excel in robustly reconstructing human mesh but often fall short in capturing intricate details

stated_limitations.text: Object interaction reconstruction faces pose initialisation and sparse SfM observation problems.
stated_limitations.quote: challenges such as pose initialization and sparse observation of objects in Structure from Motion are encountered

failure_modes: Top-down pipelines fail on detection errors in multi-person scenes.
Bottom-up methods miss smaller-scale figures.
Implicit and NeRF/Gaussian methods lack robustness in pose estimation.
future_work: Real-time processing on edge and ARM devices.
Handling crowding and occlusion.
Large models for 3D human tasks.
Detailed reconstruction bridging robust pose and surface detail.
Reconstruction with environment and objects.
Controllable and animatable avatars.

Mostly RGB monocular and multi-view inputs

Controllability and animatability of avatars

papers.title: Deep Learning-Based Human Pose Estimation: A Survey
papers.problem_statement: Despite high performance of deep learning HPE, challenges remain from insufficient training data, depth ambiguity and occlusion; prior surveys omitted multi-view and non-RGB-sensor 3D HPE and gave short discussion of challenges and future directions.

stated_limitations.text: Survey states 3D HPE ground truth depends on mocap, so datasets are constrained and methods degrade in the wild.
stated_limitations.quote: High-quality 3D ground truth pose annotations depend on motion capture systems that cannot be easily deployed in a random environment.

stated_limitations.text: Performance of 3D HPE drops in crowded scenes due to mutual occlusion and low resolution per person.
stated_limitations.quote: The performance of current 3D HPE methods drops considerably in crowded scenarios due to severe mutual occlusion and possibly low-resolution content of each person.

stated_limitations.text: Depth and other sensors alleviate ambiguity but need special hardware and are not cost-effective.
stated_limitations.quote: these approaches are usually not cost-effective and require special-purpose hardware.

stated_limitations.text: Most methods ignore human interaction with 3D scenes.
stated_limitations.quote: Most existing methods ignore human interaction with 3D scenes.

failure_modes: Top-down person detectors fail to separate boundaries of largely overlapped bodies under heavy occlusion; bottom-up keypoint association degrades in occluded scenes
Poor performance on rare poses (e.g. falling) due to data imbalance
Performance degrades on in-the-wild data when trained on constrained mocap datasets; synthetic data suffers sim-to-real gap
3D HPE from video is not smooth or continuous
Inaccurate estimation on low-resolution input when trained on high-resolution data
Vulnerable to imperceptible adversarial noise

Body models with fewer parameters while preserving mesh quality; use BMI or silhouette for shape
Exploit human-scene interaction and physical constraints
Frame-level metrics for temporal consistency and motion smoothness
Resolution-aware HPE networks, e.g. via contrastive learning
Defence against adversarial attacks
Neural architecture search for per-body-part and efficient architectures, including multi-objective NAS
restrictive_assumptions: Most surveyed 3D methods train on mocap-annotated lab datasets with selected common motions
Monocular RGB 3D HPE inherits depth ambiguity; multi-view methods require viewpoint association and calibrated setups

benchmark_gaps.observation: Survey states 3D HPE for in-the-wild data with unusual poses and occlusions is still a challenge; SOTA performance degrades off constrained datasets.

papers.title: OmniPose6D: Towards Short-Term Object Pose Tracking in Dynamic Scenes from Monocular RGB
papers.problem_statement: Object pose tracking relies on CAD models, category priors, registration or depth; RGB-only monocular methods are scarce and limited in dynamic scenes, and real datasets lack large-scale precise ground truth for dynamic object tracking.

stated_limitations.text: Robust tracking in dynamic settings remains challenging, with representative failure cases shown.
stated_limitations.quote: Our proposed tracking method outperforms existing ones, yet achieving robust tracking in dynamic settings remains a challenging endeavor.

stated_limitations.text: Pipeline runs offline and keypoint selection needs further work.

stated_limitations.quote: However, our pipeline still builds upon existing successes in segmentation, keypoint tracking, and bundle adjustment modules.

stated_limitations.text: Reliance on local feature matching causes failure on textureless objects.
stated_limitations.quote: Our method may fail when applied to textureless objects.

stated_limitations.text: Extreme scale change between scan video and test sequence is hard to handle.
stated_limitations.quote: our method still has difficulty to handle extreme change of scales between images in the video scan and the testing sequences.

stated_limitations.text: A known 2D bounding box is assumed at localization time.
stated_limitations.quote: During the localization phase, we assume the 2D bounding box of the object is known

failure_modes: Textureless objects lacking repeatable keypoints.
Extreme scale differences between reference scan and query images.
PVNet baseline drops drastically without large-scale synthetic CAD-rendered pretraining.
restrictive_assumptions: A pose-annotated video scan of each object is available to build a sparse SfM model.
Known 2D object bounding box from an external detector.
Static rigid objects; reference poses from ARKit plus manual 3D box and bundle adjustment.
Monocular RGB, textured objects.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Large objects 0.471, medium 0.629, small 0.405.

open_problems_listed: High-quality CAD models of everyday objects are often inaccessible.

Visual localization pipelines take seconds per frame and cannot track moving objects in real time.
Obtaining masks for instance-level training requires time-consuming dense reconstruction.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet estimate CAD-free object pose for textureless objects or under extreme scale change from a casual video scan.

papers.title: Gen6D: Generalizable Model-Free 6-DoF Object Pose Estimation from RGB Images
papers.problem_statement: Existing generalizable pose estimators need high-quality object models or extra depth maps or masks at test time, limiting applicability; Gen6D targets unseen objects from RGB using only some posed reference images.

stated_limitations.text: Generalization relies on learned image matching, so performance drops with limited training data.
stated_limitations.quote: Gen6D requires enough diverse training data to learn general image matching for accurate pose estimation and it performs worse with limited training data.

stated_limitations.text: Not designed for occlusion; accuracy may degrade under severe occlusion.
stated_limitations.quote: Gen6D is not specially designed to handle occlusions and the performance may degenerate when severe occlusions exist.

stated_limitations.text: Without training on the object, depth (translation along the viewing ray) is poorly estimated for small, far objects, so it trails instance-specific methods trained on real data on LINEMOD.
stated_limitations.quote: Without training on the object, Gen6D cannot perceive such subtle scale changes, which results in worse performance.

stated_limitations.text: Poses from viewpoints not covered by the reference images cannot be predicted accurately.
stated_limitations.quote: When only a part of viewpoints are available like Fig. 14 (b), Gen6D is not able to accurately predict object poses on images captured from uncovered region.

failure_modes: Severe occlusion of the object (stated as not handled).
Query viewpoints outside the reference-image coverage: Prj-5 drops from 82.64 (even coverage) to 35.56 (half-space coverage) on GenMOP.

Small, distant objects where 1-2 pixel scale error causes large depth offset (LINEMOD).
Viewpoint selection degrades when no reference image is near the query viewpoint.
restrictive_assumptions: Requires a set of posed reference images of the object (poses from COLMAP plus manual keypoint alignment in GenMOP).

Rigid object; single object per query detection.

Static per-frame estimation; no temporal tracking or hand-object interaction modeled.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Average 50.39; PlugEN only 19.63 and Scissors 32.76, below instance-specific PVNet on Piggy and Scissors.

papers.title: OpenEgo: A Large-Scale Multimodal Egocentric Dataset for Dexterous Manipulation
papers.problem_statement: Egocentric corpora lack either fine-grained temporally localized action descriptions or dexterous hand annotations; no single large-scale egocentric dataset has unified hand joints plus intention-aligned language.

stated_limitations.text: Hand joints missing in some frames due to occlusion or absent labels.
stated_limitations.quote: Hand joints are missing in some frames due to occlusions or absent labels; visibility masks reflect this.

stated_limitations.text: Language annotations auto-generated and only partially verified; temporal drift possible.
stated_limitations.quote: Language annotations are automatically generated and only partially verified; temporal drift can occur for long or ambiguous actions.

stated_limitations.text: For sources without dexterous labels, 3D joint quality depends on landmark estimator and depth.
stated_limitations.quote: For sources lacking dexterous labels, 3D joint quality depends on the landmark estimator and depth sensing.

stated_limitations.text: Experiments use only 0.1% of the data and one architecture.
stated_limitations.quote: Experiments train on only 0.1% of OpenEgo with a single architecture; results should not be interpreted as upper bounds.

failure_modes: Hand-trajectory prediction error grows with horizon: AED 0.0491 at 0.5 s to 0.1045 at 4.0 s; DTW grows from 0.39 to 6.80 due to accumulated timing offsets.
CaptainCook4D hand joints come from 2D landmark detection back-projected with depth, so quality depends on detector and depth.
future_work: Release all resources at openegocentric.com (no further future work stated).
restrictive_assumptions: Aggregates six existing datasets; inherits their sensing and annotation quality
Hand poses expressed in camera frame only; no object pose annotations
Training on a 0.1% subset due to compute limits

benchmark_gaps.metric: AED / FED / DTW (3D hand trajectory, 15 fps)
benchmark_gaps.observation: At 4.0 s horizon AED 0.1045, FED 0.1076, DTW 6.7975; errors rise steadily with horizon.

open_problems_listed: Missing hand joints under occlusion
Unverified automatically generated language annotations with temporal drift
3D joint quality for sources without native dexterous labels
Lack of upper-bound results at full data scale or with other architectures
Privacy and surveillance misuse risk of egocentric video
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field lacks a fully verified, occlusion-complete, unified egocentric hand-pose and language corpus, and long-horizon dexterous hand-trajectory prediction remains inaccurate.

papers.title: DexCanvas: Bridging Human Demonstrations and Robot Learning for Dexterous Manipulation
papers.problem_statement: Existing human manipulation data either lacks scale and systematic coverage, suffers vision-based self-occlusion and noisy 3D pose, or (mocap) captures only geometry without the contact forces needed for dexterous control.

stated_limitations.text: Coverage restricted to basic geometric objects and fundamental primitives.
stated_limitations.quote: Our current coverage is limited to basic geometric objects and fundamental manipulation primitives.

stated_limitations.text: Per-object-manipulation RL policy training does not scale.
stated_limitations.quote: Our per-object-manipulation policy training faces obvious scalability challenges.

stated_limitations.text: Only human hand data released; no robot retargeting yet.
stated_limitations.quote: The dataset currently releases only human hand data

stated_limitations.text: RGB-D streams unexplored; language annotations minimal.
stated_limitations.quote: RGB-D streams are included but unexplored.

stated_limitations.text: Cross-dataset and downstream experiments not yet provided.
stated_limitations.quote: Additional experiments demonstrating cross-dataset applicability and downstream task evaluation will be available in future versions.

stated_limitations.text: Force estimation from observation alone is under-constrained.
stated_limitations.quote: force estimation from observation alone is under-constrained, requiring either physical sensors that disrupt natural behavior or physics simulation that can enforce consistency between motion and forces

failure_modes: RL reproduction success only 80.15% under nominal conditions (termination when positional error exceeds 5 cm).
Success drops to 62.54% when initial object pose is perturbed by up to 20% of object size.
Unusable segments with long marker occlusions or broken marker constellations are removed; brief occlusions interpolated.
future_work: Extend from simple geometries to YCB and real-world assets, and to in-hand reorientation and free-form multi-primitive scenarios
Unified MANO control model conditioned on object and task encodings
Physics-aware retargeting to robot hands using force annotations
Use RGB-D for visuomotor learning and rendering/world-model synthesis; richer language annotations
Cross-dataset applicability and downstream task evaluation
restrictive_assumptions: Room-scale optical mocap with 22 infrared cameras and reflective markers on hand and objects
Right hand only (14 markers on right hand)
Objects 3D-printed from CAD models with carved marker mounts (known object geometry)
Forces derived from physics simulation (IsaacGym), exact only up to simulation accuracy, not measured
Per-participant hand calibration sequences

benchmark_gaps.observation: 80.15% nominal; 62.54% with 20% object-size pose perturbation.

open_problems_listed: Scaling beyond basic geometric objects and primitives to real-world assets and composed skills
Unified policy replacing thousands of per-object policies
Cross-morphology retargeting preserving contact dynamics
Exploiting RGB-D for perception; minimal language annotation
Force estimation from vision is under-constrained; sensors alter contact mechanics; distributed whole-hand contact capture infeasible
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot obtain physically grounded hand-object contact forces at scale from vision alone, without markers, CAD objects and per-sequence simulation policies.

papers.title: World In Your Hands: A Large-Scale and Open-Source Ecosystem for Learning Human-Centric Manipulation in the Wild
papers.problem_statement: Existing egocentric manipulation datasets have limited scenario diversity, inadequate vision-language-action alignment (calibration, accurate 3D hand/wrist motion, masks, task language) and insufficient policy-level evaluation.

stated_limitations.text: No tactile sensing; limited embodiment and category coverage in policy evaluation.
stated_limitations.quote: WIYH currently focuses on visual, geometric, language, and motion annotations; future extensions could incorporate full-hand tactile sensing and broader policy evaluations across more robot embodiments

stated_limitations.text: In-the-wild data lacks motion-capture ground truth; quality is checked by reprojection consistency only.
stated_limitations.quote: for large-scale in-the-wild data where motion-capture ground truth is unavailable, we use reprojection-based consistency checks

stated_limitations.text: Unverified ego data gives little gain; noisy labels offset scale.
stated_limitations.quote: noisy ego-centric action labels and unreliable action-language alignment can offset the benefits of ego-centric scale

failure_modes: Unverified variant WIYH* provides little overall gain over no pretraining in RoboCasa.
Robot-only training in cluttered multi-object scenes: 0.0% (200 clips) and 8.0% (500 clips) success.
VLMs struggle with spatial referring across height levels or different depths (e.g., 'beneath'); completion verification only slightly above random.
Untextured video generation baselines show object fragmentation and physically implausible hand-object interactions.
future_work: Incorporate full-hand tactile sensing
Broader policy evaluations across more robot embodiments and manipulation categories
restrictive_assumptions: Custom wearable Oracle Suite: chest-mounted multi-camera module, Manus data gloves with IMUs and fisheye cameras, backpack compute
Gloved hands (glove appearance differs from bare hands)
Wrist accuracy (<5 mm) validated only in a mocap room; offline SfM refinement
Atomic segmentation needs human verification

benchmark_gaps.observation: Spatial referring remains difficult for all VLMs; completion verification only slightly above 50% random.
Single-object with 200 robot clips plus 800 ego clips reaches only 23.3%.
With pretraining 70% average; unseen bottle 3/6.

open_problems_listed: Limited scenario diversity in lab-collected datasets
Missing aligned supervision (calibration, accurate 3D hand/wrist motion, masks, task language)
Insufficient policy-level evaluation of egocentric datasets
Annotation quality control: unverified labels erase the benefit of scale
No tactile sensing
Fine-grained embodied spatial understanding and progress modeling in VLMs
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet obtain verified, accurate 3D hand action labels from in-the-wild egocentric capture without instrumented gloves, mocap validation and manual review.

papers.title: Open-AoE: An Open Egocentric Manipulation Dataset and Toolchain for Embodied Learning
papers.problem_statement: High-quality egocentric data depends on specialized head-mounted or AR/VR hardware, while passive video lacks hand motion, camera trajectory and action boundaries; processing pipelines remain fragmented rather than unified infrastructure.

stated_limitations.text: Distribution statistics computed from a 100-hour sample; diversity benefit unvalidated.
stated_limitations.quote: The downstream benefit of camera-domain diversity remains a training hypothesis that should be validated through controlled ablations.
stated_limitations.section: 3.6 Data Distribution Analysis (Scope and claim boundary)

stated_limitations.text: Annotation-consistency comparison is not a controlled accuracy benchmark.
stated_limitations.quote: these results should be interpreted as a cross-dataset audit of image-annotation support under a shared evaluator rather than as a fully controlled benchmark of annotation accuracy

failure_modes: Recordings with residual third-person views, hand truncation or excessive occlusion are screened out.
Severe camera shake and torso motion require re-tuned robust kernels in DROID-W.
Segment-wise reconstructions suffer scale drift and coordinate mismatch, requiring global bundle adjustment.
Model hallucinations in atomic-action labels require human-in-the-loop correction.
Parts with low hand-reconstruction valid-frame ratio or high IK failure rate are discarded.
future_work: Community contributions of new scenes, reconstruction and retargeting methods, training adapters and evaluation results
Controlled ablations to validate the downstream benefit of camera-domain diversity
restrictive_assumptions: Monocular consumer smartphone RGB; hand poses estimated (HaWoR, MANO), not measured
Metric scale from SLAM; no depth sensor
No released object pose annotation; object 6-DoF must come from downstream tools
Both hands must remain clearly visible
open_problems_listed: Fragmented dataset-specific processing pipelines lacking unified infrastructure
Specialized capture hardware limits accessibility
Passive video lacks hand motion, camera trajectory, action boundaries and physical structure
Unvalidated benefit of camera-domain diversity
No controlled benchmark of annotation accuracy across datasets
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet verify the accuracy of hand and camera annotations recovered at scale from commodity monocular smartphone video.

papers.title: HumanNet: Scaling Human-centric Video Learning to One Million Hours
papers.problem_statement: Physical-interaction models train on collections orders of magnitude smaller than vision-language corpora, narrow and tied to specific robots; existing human-video corpora are limited in duration, fragmented or narrowly optimized.

stated_limitations.text: Embodiment gap remains despite scale.
stated_limitations.quote: human behavior is not robot behavior. Even at one-million-hour scale, a human-centered corpus does not eliminate the embodiment gap

stated_limitations.text: Scale introduces label, boundary, metadata and quality noise; automated annotations carry errors.
stated_limitations.quote: Caption labels, pose estimates, and motion annotations help with coverage but introduce their own errors.

stated_limitations.text: Coverage is uneven and biased.
stated_limitations.quote: one-million-hour scale can create an illusion of universality where significant blind spots remain

stated_limitations.text: Privacy and safety issues from bystanders, interiors and documents.
stated_limitations.quote: human-centric video raises serious privacy and safety issues

stated_limitations.text: No new human-to-robot transfer experiments reported.
stated_limitations.quote: This paper does not report new transfer experiments

failure_modes: Clips are designated robot-ready only when retargeting error is below 15 mm and valid-frame coverage exceeds 60%; others lack reliable retargeting.
Monocular SLAM camera trajectory only for first-person clips meeting stability and parallax requirements.
Clips with severe motion blur, heavy occlusion or static framing are discarded.
future_work: Transparent reporting of annotation confidence and subset quality
Release with license review, redaction, restricted-content filtering and access controls
restrictive_assumptions: Internet and self-collected monocular RGB video; 3D hand/body pose estimated, not measured
Validation only by VLA validation loss, not task success

benchmark_gaps.dataset: LingBot-VLA post-training, five held-out task groups
benchmark_gaps.observation: 1,000 h egocentric pretraining only matches or slightly surpasses 100 h real-robot data; does not match the 20,000 h robot baseline.

open_problems_listed: Embodiment gap between human and robot control spaces
Noise from ambiguous labels, inconsistent task boundaries, missing metadata, viewpoint imbalance and variable quality
Errors in automated captions, pose estimates and motion annotations
Uneven coverage and geographic, socioeconomic and body-type bias
Privacy, safety and licensing of human-centric video
Dual-use and surveillance risk
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet convert internet-scale human video into reliable, accurately annotated robot supervision that closes the embodiment gap.

papers.title: EgoLive: A Large-Scale Egocentric Dataset from Real-World Human Tasks
papers.problem_statement: Robot datasets suffer restricted environmental diversity and poor extensibility; teleoperation and UMI collection have limited scalability and real-world deployability.

stated_limitations.text: Depth error grows with distance; low error claimed only within typical human operation range.
stated_limitations.quote: our depth reconstruction approach can achieve low mean errors within the typical human operation range

failure_modes: Stereo depth mean error rises from about 3 mm at 500 mm to 18.0 mm at 3500 mm (calibration room).
3D hand keypoint accuracy validated only by qualitative alignment with stereo point clouds, not quantitative ground truth.
Predicted captions omit or alter steps compared with ground truth (Table 3 examples).
future_work: Sustain continuous growth in scale and coverage; support human-to-robot alignment and humanoid policy learning
restrictive_assumptions: Custom head-mounted stereo RGB device with IMU (JoyEgoCam)
Hand pose from HaMeR monocular estimation refined by stereo optimization (no ground truth)
No object pose annotation; objects get masks only
Depth from learned stereo (FoundationStereo)

benchmark_gaps.observation: 3.06 mm at 500 mm but 13-18 mm beyond 1700 mm; under 80% of points within the tightest threshold beyond 900 mm.

open_problems_listed: Restricted environmental diversity of existing robot datasets
Poor extensibility of teleoperation and UMI collection
Gap between human behavior and robot action
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field lacks quantitatively validated 3D hand and object annotation for in-the-wild egocentric capture at scale.

papers.title: SABER: A Scalable Action-Based Embodied Dataset for Real-World VLA Adaptation
papers.problem_statement: Retail environments are absent from general robot pretraining distributions and teleoperated in-store demonstrations are prohibitively expensive, so general VLAs such as GR00T N1.6 achieve near-zero retail success.

stated_limitations.text: Evaluation in simulation only.
stated_limitations.quote: All evaluations are in simulation; real-robot deployment remains future work.

stated_limitations.text: Body-pose stream is small.
stated_limitations.quote: The body pose retarget stream is substantially smaller (1.2K) than the other streams

stated_limitations.text: Stream-type conditioning is one design choice; alternatives untested.
stated_limitations.quote: The stream-type conditioning approach is one design choice

stated_limitations.text: Frozen vision encoder limits domain-specific perception.
stated_limitations.quote: the frozen vision encoder limits the acquisition of domain-specific perceptual representations

stated_limitations.text: No per-stream ablation.
stated_limitations.quote: Per-stream ablation results would quantify this empirically and are a promising direction for future analysis.

failure_modes: Non-fridge tasks remain low: mean 13.8% success after SABER post-training.
Board-to-board Nestle task stays at 2% success; Duff unchanged at 10%.
Precise gripper finger shaping around small packaging is the dominant failure on board and basket tasks.
Robot downward extension is the primary failure on floor-pick tasks.
Robot-native anchor data was needed to stabilize early training.
future_work: Complete the full multimodal evaluation suite
Expand the body-pose retarget stream
Validate on physical retail robots and additional VLA backbones
Train the full model end-to-end including the vision encoder
Replace COSMOS-Reason backbone with a retail-specialized VLM (PRISM)
Explore separate action heads or hierarchical architectures; per-stream ablations
restrictive_assumptions: Hand landmarks require frame-by-frame manual correction by trained annotators
Whole-body SMPL needs a fixed 360-degree exocentric camera and manual correction
Evaluation only in RoboBenchMart simulation
Robot-native anchor data needed

benchmark_gaps.observation: SABER-MM mean 29.3%; non-fridge mean 13.8%; Nestle 2%, Duff 10%, Vanish 11%.
Mean 0.146 after post-training.

open_problems_listed: Domain-specific data gap for retail deployment
Real-robot validation absent
Small whole-body pose stream
Gradient conflict and negative transfer between streams
Frozen vision encoder limits domain perception
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet convert human retail demonstrations into robot policies that reliably succeed at precise grasps of small packaged items, even in simulation.

papers.title: HuRo: Robotizing Human Videos for Scalable VLA Pretraining
papers.problem_statement: Joint observation-action robotization of human video has mostly been shown in task-matched settings; it is open whether heterogeneous human videos can serve as a scalable source of jointly robot-aligned observation-action data for VLA pretraining.

stated_limitations.text: Robotized observation fidelity is bounded by reconstruction and visual conversion quality; the robot overlay ignores occlusion with scene geometry and leaves inpainting/rendering artifacts.
stated_limitations.quote: our current robot overlay does not explicitly model occlusion between the rendered robot and scene geometry, and residual inpainting or rendering artifacts may introduce visual inconsistencies.

stated_limitations.text: The effect of robotization fidelity on downstream policy learning is not characterized.
stated_limitations.quote: How different levels of robotization fidelity affect downstream policy learning remains unexplored

stated_limitations.text: No force or tactile signals are captured, only visual and kinematic action supervision.
stated_limitations.quote: the HuRo dataset provides visual and kinematic action supervision but does not capture force or tactile signals for contact-rich manipulation.

stated_limitations.text: Kinematic retargeting models neither self-collision nor physical contact; only 55.2% of audited trajectories were free of non-grasp self-contact, so outputs are not executable demonstrations.
stated_limitations.quote: our kinematic retargeting does not model self-collision or physical contact. In a five-source audit, only 55.2% of trajectories had no detected non-grasp self-contact

failure_modes: Retargeted trajectories contain non-grasp self-contact in about 45% of audited trajectories (no self-collision term in IK).
Only 62.5% of audited trajectories had no URDF joint-limit violation before post-hoc clamping.
Camera-robot alignment has a high-error tail with large viewpoint or robot-placement inconsistency (Fig. 10).
Policies pretrained on small subsets show unstable grasps, off-center contacts, slipping and stacking failures under shifted placement and checkered tablecloth.
Low manipulation-segment yield from in-the-wild video: 17.3% of EPIC-Kitchens and 6.9% of Ego4D frames retained.
future_work: Systematically characterize how robotization fidelity affects downstream policy learning.
Augment robotized human videos with inferred contact or force cues.
Jointly pretrain with sensor-rich robot datasets.
restrictive_assumptions: Monocular egocentric RGB; metric scale recovered from MoGe-2 monocular depth, camera from masked DROID-SLAM.
3D hand pose from HaWoR (MANO) estimates; median root-relative 21-keypoint error 20.4 mm vs EgoDex annotations.
Retargeting is kinematic only (fingertip and structure cues), no object pose or physics.
Background behind the human arm is unobserved and must be inpainted.
Actions derived as next retargeted state (a_t = s_{t+1}); trajectories used as pretraining supervision, not executable demos.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Even with full HuRo pretraining, OOD completion is 72.2% (from 34.9% without), versus 80.3% overall completion.
Median root-relative 21-keypoint hand error 20.4 mm; camera ATE median 4.47 mm.
Only 55.2% of trajectories free of non-grasp self-contact.

open_problems_listed: Robotized observation fidelity limited by reconstruction and visual conversion (no robot-scene occlusion modelling, inpainting artifacts).
Unknown relationship between robotization fidelity and downstream policy learning.
No force/tactile supervision for contact-rich manipulation from human video.
Kinematic retargeting without self-collision or physical contact modelling yields non-executable trajectories.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Convert in-the-wild human video into physically valid, contact-aware, occlusion-consistent robot demonstrations rather than kinematic pretraining hints.

papers.title: RoboEdit: Turning Human Manipulation Videos into Scalable Robot Experience
papers.problem_statement: Robot interaction data is costly and embodiment-specific; translating human videos into physically plausible target-robot videos while preserving scene context, interaction dynamics and temporal consistency across embodiments remains challenging.

stated_limitations.text: Monocular hand reconstruction (HaMeR) has depth and scale ambiguity that misplaces hands in 3D, causing missed contacts, penetration or instability after retargeting; depth correction is needed.
stated_limitations.quote: Monocular HaMeR estimates often suffer from depth and scale ambiguities, such that even an image-aligned hand can be misplaced in 3D space, leading to missed contacts, object penetration, or instability

stated_limitations.text: Without depth regularization and physics refinement the retargeted robot hand is displaced or has floating/penetrating fingers.
stated_limitations.quote: Without depth regularization, monocular depth and scale errors propagate to retargeting and displace the robot hand in the scene.

stated_limitations.text: Background SSIM is slightly lower because robot and human hands differ in spatial extent near the edit-mask boundary.
stated_limitations.quote: Its slightly lower BG SSIM reflects the differing spatial extent of robot and human hands

failure_modes: Kinematic matching alone produces floating or penetrating fingers.
Monocular depth/scale errors displace the robot hand in the composited scene.
Decoded robot-hand states have about 42 mm wrist, 43 mm fingertip and 23 degree rotation error in camera space.
Trajectory-reproduction success in simulation only 71% (Panda) and 62% (XHand); real-robot tasks reach at least 50% over 10 trials.
restrictive_assumptions: Rigid object mesh reconstructed by TRELLIS and 6D-tracked by FoundationPose (model-based tracking of a reconstructed template).
Camera intrinsics, extrinsics and depth from VGGT on monocular RGB.
Source videos from lab HOI datasets (DexYCB, HOT3D, H2O, GigaHands, TACO).
Contacts defined by fingertip-to-surface distance thresholds consistent across frames.
Slow offline curation: about 20 minutes per clip for ADC and 8 minutes for Trans inference on an H100.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Full model wrist 42.03 mm, fingertip 43.26 mm, rotation 23.28 degrees.
71% with Panda gripper and 62% with XHand.

open_problems_listed: Faithfully transforming human videos into robot interaction videos while preserving scene context, interaction dynamics and temporal consistency across embodiments.
Depth and scale ambiguity of monocular hand reconstruction harming contact geometry.
Penetration, floating contacts and temporal jitter in reconstructed hand-object interactions.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Recover metrically accurate, contact-consistent 3D hand-object interaction from monocular video without heavy depth and physics correction.

papers.title: Human-Centric Transferable Tactile Pre-Training for Dexterous Robotic Manipulation
papers.problem_statement: Tactile datasets are small and narrow in contact coverage due to hardware and collection limits, and tactile VLA models rely on dynamics-agnostic post-training; human demonstration datasets overlook the tactile modality.

stated_limitations.text: Existing tactile datasets remain small and narrow in contact coverage because of hardware and collection systems.
stated_limitations.quote: limited by hardware and data collection systems, existing datasets with tactility remain small in scale and narrow in contact coverage.

stated_limitations.text: Standard VLA policies ignore tactile information, degrading performance in contact-intensive tasks.
stated_limitations.quote: the learned policies remain predominantly driven by visual cues and systematically ignore tactile information, leading to degraded performance in contact-intensive scenarios.

stated_limitations.text: Simulation benchmarks have no tactile modality, so a proprioceptive proxy replaces tactile input there.
stated_limitations.quote: Since these benchmarks do not have tactile modalities inherently

failure_modes: PlugIn tasks with visual defects remain mostly unsolved: 20% (gripper) and 10% (DexBotic) in-distribution success.
Bimanual VaseWiping OOD drops to 80% while single-hand reaches 100%.
On LIBERO-plus camera and robot perturbations TTP scores 48.9 and 49.5, below some baselines.
restrictive_assumptions: HOI-Tac tactile labels are binary per-vertex contact from hand-object mesh distance thresholding, not measured force.
DeskTask-Tac requires three calibrated RealSense cameras plus tactile glove, and for the AprilTag pipeline a MoCap glove and scene AprilTags.
Tactile from simulation InternData-Tac is projected onto a shared MANO surface.
Unified 351-D tactile space on MANO UV assumed across embodiments.

benchmark_gaps.observation: In-distribution 20% and 10%; OOD 20% and 20%; all baselines 0%.
TTP 48.9%, below OpenVLA-OFT 56.4% and pi0-Fast 65.1%.
TTP average 55.1%; Pick and Place only 35%.

open_problems_listed: Scarcity of large-scale tactile data with broad contact coverage.
Tactile sensors on robot hands are non-unified in hardware integration.
Teleoperation for contact-rich tasks is labor-intensive and hard to scale.
Human demonstration datasets largely omit tactile modality.
Pre-train/post-train distribution mismatch in tactile VLA training.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Obtain measured, scalable full-hand contact force for natural human manipulation without gloves, MoCap or mesh-distance proxies.

papers.title: Human Universal Grasping
papers.problem_statement: Multi-fingered robots lack human-level grasp generality because diverse real-world grasp data is missing; synthetic grasps suffer sim-to-real gaps and per-hand retraining, teleoperation cannot cover the open world.

stated_limitations.text: Trained on right-hand grasps only with fixed MANO shape; left-handed, bimanual and hand-specific morphology are not modeled.
stated_limitations.quote: The model is trained on right-hand grasps only, with the MANO shape held fixed at a canonical value, so left-handed or bimanual grasping and hand-specific morphology are not modeled.

stated_limitations.text: Retargeting fails when robot hand cannot reach a feasible analog of the MANO pose.
stated_limitations.quote: The human-to-robot retargeting can fail when the target robot hand cannot reach a feasible analog of the predicted MANO pose.

stated_limitations.text: Open-loop execution without visual feedback fails on objects that shift or articulate.
stated_limitations.quote: Real-world rollouts run open-loop, with no closed-loop visual feedback during contact or lift, which can cause failures on objects that shift or articulate during the trajectory.

stated_limitations.text: Hand tracking degrades under occlusion, making grasp labels too loose or tight.
stated_limitations.quote: When the hand is occluded during the grasp, Aria Gen 2 hand tracking degrades, so the grasp label can be too loose or too tight.

stated_limitations.text: Accuracy drops on very small objects (224x224 input) and on large or far objects rare in egocentric data.
stated_limitations.quote: Accuracy drops on very small objects, limited by the 224x224 input resolution, and on large or far objects, which are rare in egocentric data

stated_limitations.text: Only one grasp predicted per trial; evaluation indoor only.
stated_limitations.quote: Our evaluation is indoor only.

failure_modes: Objects too large for the hand to wrap (football, wipe dispenser) and irregular or articulated objects (nail clipper, headphones) are hardest open-loop.
PC-only variant grasps wrong part (pineapple leaves, brush bristles) and snaps to nearby larger object when depth is unreliable on small targets.
RGB-only variant rarely reaches the object (test SR 29.7%).
Human-grasp oracle itself reaches only 90-94% due to hand-tracking error, asset inaccuracy, open-loop execution.
future_work: Generate many grasp candidates and select the best.
Normalize grasp translation around the 3D query point for large or far objects.
Closed-loop visual feedback (implied by stated open-loop limitation).
restrictive_assumptions: Stereo RGB-D input with a user-specified query point on the object.
Static scene: grasp propagated back to no-hand frames using Aria SLAM camera poses.
Right-hand, single-hand grasps, canonical MANO shape.
Grasp only (pre-grasp, grasp, lift); no post-grasp manipulation.
Aria Gen 2 hand tracking provides 21 landmarks used as labels.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Full model 73.0% vs human-grasp oracle 94.0%, a ~20-point gap.
66.7% tabletop and 62.0% in-the-wild.
Neither SR nor FC error saturates at 1M frames; model still data-bound.

open_problems_listed: Bimanual and left-hand grasping not modeled.
Hand-specific morphology not modeled.
Retargeting infeasibility across robot hands.
Open-loop execution failures on shifting or articulated objects.
Grasp label noise when the hand is occluded.
Small, large and far objects poorly handled.
Outdoor evaluation absent.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Learn bimanual, closed-loop, occlusion-robust grasp-and-manipulate behaviour from egocentric human capture at scale.

papers.title: EgoTactile: Learning Grasp Pressure for Everyday Objects from Egocentric Video
papers.problem_statement: Vision-based pressure estimation relies on planar surfaces or fingertip-only contacts and fails to generalize to full-hand grasps on 3D objects; synchronized full-hand pressure data for 3D objects is scarce.

stated_limitations.text: Main supervised split is in a controlled environment; broader real-world coverage remains future work.
stated_limitations.quote: its main supervised split is collected in a controlled environment. Although our realistic-scene evaluation shows encouraging robustness, broader real-world coverage remains an important future direction.

stated_limitations.text: Bare-hand subset gives weakly paired supervision, not exact force labels for the visible hand.
stated_limitations.quote: The bare-hand subset also provides weakly paired supervision rather than exact force labels for the visible hand.

stated_limitations.text: RGB-conditioned models fail on rare interaction patterns without explicit hand pose and object 6D pose.
stated_limitations.quote: current RGB-conditioned models remain limited when detailed hand pose and object 6D pose are not explicitly modeled.

stated_limitations.text: Diffusion model slower than discriminative baselines.
stated_limitations.quote: EgoPressureDiff is still slower than discriminative baselines

failure_modes: False negatives at grasp initiation and hallucinated lingering pressure at release due to egocentric self-occlusion of the hand-object gap.
Temporal flickering of pressure across adjacent frames from stochastic diffusion sampling.
Unseen interaction patterns (palm press, palm support, hook lift, toss-and-catch) drop C-IoU from 56.3 to 31.8.
In-the-wild scenes drop C-IoU from 56.3 to 49.6 and raise CoP error 3.1 to 5.4.
Base model runs at 2.8 FPS (25-step).
future_work: Explicit geometric conditioning (hand pose, object 6D pose).
Adaptation to robot hands for scalable imitation learning.
Stronger temporal consistency constraints or consistency distillation.
restrictive_assumptions: Green-screen controlled capture for the main split.
Tactile glove with 162 taxels on the grasping hand (visible in gloved split).
Single grasping hand per clip; 12 participants, 63 objects.
Object and subject metadata (weight, stiffness, fill state) supplied as text conditioning.
