Models worst on VQA inputs longer than 1 minute.
future_work: More holistic perception of egocentric videos.
restrictive_assumptions: Project Aria glasses with MPS SLAM and gaze.
Digital twins manually curated in Blender from SLAM point clouds.
Object 3D locations from masks lifted with monocular metric depth aligned to sparse SLAM points; 3D boxes, not 6D object poses.
Validation-only dataset in 9 kitchens.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Gemini Pro: 3D perception 32.5, object motion 20.8, gaze 28.7; human 93.8, 92.7, 75.0.
SAM2 27.0, Cutie 34.6, static 6.6.
Best 51 verb, 37 noun, 24 action.

open_problems_listed: Fine-grained to hour-long video understanding remains out of reach for foundational and specialised models.
3D perception and object itinerary reasoning relative to fixtures.
Gaze-based anticipation of next object movement.
Long-term segmentation of manipulated objects under occlusion and out-of-view.
Robustness of audio recognition to new scenes and devices.
Long-video (over 1 minute) and multi-video question answering.
Recognising fine-grained actions in unscripted in-the-wild settings.
papers.field_cannot_yet: Track manipulated objects over long egocentric videos and reason about their 3D motion; object VOS J&F is 27 to 35 and VLM object-motion accuracy 20.8 percent.

papers.title: Robot Learning from Human Videos: A Survey
papers.problem_statement: Robot data is hard to scale; human videos are abundant but the field lacks a taxonomy centred on how information flows from human videos to robot execution, a cross-comparison of transfer pathways, and an organised view of video sources.

stated_limitations.text: Nearly all learning-from-human-video methods assume one human demonstrator and one robot; collaborative, multi-agent tasks are not supported.
stated_limitations.quote: almost all existing LfHV methods are developed under a single-agent assumption

stated_limitations.text: Even with RGB-D or metric depth, vision-only human video remains vulnerable to occlusion and ambiguous interaction states.
stated_limitations.quote: the observed spatial structures are limited in the vision modality, which are still vulnerable to occlusions and ambiguous interaction states

stated_limitations.text: Action-near methods fail by mis-grounding: extracted trajectories or contact cues look plausible in video but violate robot kinematics, control or contact dynamics.
stated_limitations.quote: Methods close to actions usually fail through mis-grounding

stated_limitations.text: Current pipelines depend on curated or aggressively filtered data, discarding low-quality, occluded or blurred videos and long-tail interactions.
stated_limitations.quote: the current pipelines either rely on relatively curated datasets or aggressively filter noisy web data before training

stated_limitations.text: Benchmarking is fragmented across robots, tasks and video sources, and most methods cannot be benchmarked in simulation alone.
stated_limitations.quote: most LfHV cannot be easily benchmarked in simulation alone

stated_limitations.text: Affordance extraction is limited to visually observable geometric traces (contact regions, hand trajectories, object poses, flow) without function or physical constraints.
stated_limitations.quote: Current affordance-based LfHV methods mainly extract visually observable cues, such as contact regions, hand trajectories, object poses, and motion flow.

stated_limitations.text: Human-video world models emphasise visual similarity and do not impose physical constraints, producing physically invalid rollouts in contact-rich, long-horizon tasks.
stated_limitations.quote: still neglect to impose strict physical constraints on the modeled dynamics

stated_limitations.text: Human videos are used as a fixed offline corpus with no mechanism to absorb new videos after initial training.
stated_limitations.quote: most existing LfHV pipelines still lack a systematic mechanism for incorporating newly available human videos after the initial training stage
stated_limitations.section: 5.3 Continual Learning with Human Video Data

failure_modes: Task-level transfer fails through under-grounding: the robot understands the task but cannot execute it precisely.
Action-level transfer (trajectories, contact cues, latent actions) fails through mis-grounding when cues violate robot kinematics, control frequency, collision constraints or contact dynamics.
Observation-level alignment fails through false visual equivalence: aligned images or embeddings do not imply aligned actions.
Vision-only HOI cues degrade under occlusion and ambiguous interaction states, and for material-dependent interactions.
Multi-agent settings require resolving agent correspondence, disentangling overlapping motions, and tracking contacts across agents and shared objects, which current pipelines do not do.
future_work: Physically grounded world models learned from human video that anticipate long-horizon interaction states.
Physics-aware functional affordances encoding function, manipulated part, interaction mode and physical constraints, including articulated objects.
Continual learning that absorbs new human videos with quality-aware filtering and continual evaluation.
Multi-agent interaction modelling (handovers, joint transport, collaborative assembly) and suitable datasets.
Adding audio, gaze and tactile (including pseudo-tactile) signals to human video.
Learning from low-quality web video via uncertainty-aware supervision and robust pseudo-labelling.
Standardised benchmarks, possibly using 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstructions of capture scenes.
Egocentric data ecosystems with standardised protocols and 3D hand and head pose annotations.
restrictive_assumptions: Most methods assume a single human demonstrator and a single robot.
Most rely on curated or filtered video rather than raw in-the-wild footage.
Affordance pipelines assume hand, object pose and contact cues are visually observable from the camera view.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Methods are evaluated on different robots, tasks and human video sources, so which transfer choices cause better performance remains unclear.

open_problems_listed: Physically grounded world models that capture long-horizon causal dependencies and physical consistency.
Physics-aware functional affordance extraction beyond geometric HOI traces.
Continual learning with newly available human video data.
Multi-agent interaction: agent correspondence, overlapping motions, cross-agent contact tracking, and coupled feasible action spaces.
Multimodal signals (audio, gaze, tactile) accompanying human videos, and their integration despite differing rates and noise.
Use of low-quality human videos (blur, occlusion, camera shake, failed executions, passive observation).
Standardized benchmarking, including evaluation not reducible to simulation.
Egocentric data ecosystems with shared protocols, annotations and access interfaces.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet extract physically grounded, robot-executable interaction signals (contacts, object motion, multi-agent coordination) reliably from occluded, unconstrained human video.

papers.title: Data Pyramid for Embodied Manipulation: A Survey
papers.problem_statement: Embodied data sources differ in scalability, robot alignment and physical fidelity, but their roles, trade-offs and integration have not been systematically organised at the category level or analysed from a data-centric view.

stated_limitations.text: Egocentric human data is not equivalent to robot experience and suffers from occlusion, blur, camera motion and device-dependent viewpoints.
stated_limitations.quote: First-person recordings suffer from partial observability, hand-object occlusion, rapid camera motion, motion blur, and device-dependent viewpoints.

stated_limitations.text: Wearable head and hand tracking is not mature for large-scale deployment; gloves, tactile sensors and EMG need fitting, calibration and synchronisation.
stated_limitations.quote: Head and hand tracking remain sensitive to occlusion, motion blur, drift, and limited field of view
stated_limitations.section: 8.3 Scalable Data Collection Across Pyramid Layers

stated_limitations.text: Instrumented capture trades accuracy under occlusion against calibration effort and participant burden.
stated_limitations.quote: Instrumented capture generally yields more continuous and accurate 3D motion under visual occlusion, but increases calibration effort and participant burden

stated_limitations.text: Object pose labels in HOI datasets can be ambiguous under occlusion and object symmetry.
stated_limitations.quote: although occlusion and object symmetry can make pose recovery ambiguous.

stated_limitations.text: UMI-style data quality depends on pose tracking and synchronisation that degrade in hard visual conditions.
stated_limitations.quote: Its quality also relies on accurate pose tracking and sensor synchronization, which may degrade under occlusion, rapid motion, or visually challenging environments

stated_limitations.text: Tactile sensing is not a standard modality in robot datasets, leaving a missing contact layer.
stated_limitations.quote: tactile sensing is still not systematically incorporated as a standard modality
stated_limitations.section: 8.1 Tactile Data for Contact-Rich Robot Learning

stated_limitations.text: Failure and recovery data are scarce and poorly organised; binary success labels are insufficient.
stated_limitations.quote: failure data remains limited in scale and lacks systematic organization.
stated_limitations.section: 8.2 Failure Data and Recovery-Centric Robot Learning

stated_limitations.text: Retargeted human hand motions can look plausible yet fail on real robot hands.
stated_limitations.quote: retargeted motions that appear geometrically plausible may still violate robot-specific constraints or fail to produce stable contacts on real hardware.
stated_limitations.section: 8.5 Egocentric Priors for Dexterous Hand Policy Learning

stated_limitations.text: Optimal data mixtures across pyramid layers are unknown and compute-matched ablations are limited.
stated_limitations.quote: However, the most effective data composition remains an open problem.

failure_modes: Headset inside-out tracking (EgoDex, HoloAssist) can fail under fast motion, occlusion or limited field of view.
IMU-based tracking accumulates drift; magnetic fingertip sensors are distorted by nearby metal.
Model-based pose pseudo-labels inherit errors from occlusion, motion blur and domain shift.
Camera and scene geometry labels are sensitive to calibration drift, motion blur and coordinate-frame choice.
Embodiment-aware inpainting produces interactions that are not physically grounded.
End-effector poses defined in different frames give conflicting supervision across datasets.
future_work: Large-scale, standardised tactile datasets integrated with long-horizon trajectories.
Failure-centric datasets with pre-failure context, onset, causes, state changes and recovery actions.
Lighter, wireless, modular wearables with automatic cross-device calibration and on-device hand-object reconstruction.
Recording coordinate conventions, calibration parameters and controller modes as first-class metadata.
Treating egocentric data as structured interaction priors (contact sequences, grasp choices) rather than precise action labels.
Architecture-aware, stage-dependent data recipes with compute-matched ablations.
restrictive_assumptions: Dense geometric and multimodal egocentric supervision requires extra hardware, calibration, synchronisation and reconstruction.
Optical mocap ground truth (e.g. HOT3D) requires markers and a controlled calibrated workspace.
Object pose annotation often relies on CAD-model registration.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Skill-constrained generation produced many trajectories whose action keypoints concentrate in a small region, indicating repetition despite scale.

open_problems_listed: Building large-scale tactile datasets for contact-rich learning.
Collecting and structuring failure and recovery data.
Scalable data collection across pyramid layers, including mature wearable sensing with automatic calibration and on-device hand-object reconstruction.
Cross-embodiment state-action alignment with consistent geometric semantics.
Leveraging egocentric priors for dexterous hand policy learning across the kinematic, morphological and physical gap.
Principled data recipes for mixing data sources.
Data quality assessment, multimodal and action-space standardisation, human-to-robot and sim-to-real transfer (conclusion list).
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet capture accurate, calibrated hand-object geometry and contact at scale from wearable or egocentric sensing without heavy calibration and participant burden.

papers.title: Vision-Language-Action in Robotics: A Survey of Datasets, Benchmarks, and Data Engines
papers.problem_statement: VLA progress is shaped by datasets, benchmarks and data engines, yet these lack a systematic, data-centric categorisation needed to understand current limitations.

stated_limitations.text: Datasets trade fidelity against scale; aggregated corpora gain volume at the cost of interface consistency.
stated_limitations.quote: current dataset development strategies have not resolved the fundamental tension between fidelity and cost

stated_limitations.text: Contact-rich behaviours with force or tactile signals are underrepresented.
stated_limitations.quote: Contact-rich behaviors requiring force or tactile feedback remain underrepresented because collecting such signals in real environments is costly and hardware-dependent.

stated_limitations.text: Video-to-data engines inherit perception errors from grounding, pose and depth estimation.
stated_limitations.quote: Failures in grounding, pose estimation, and depth reconstruction introduce systematic noise that propagates into policy learning

stated_limitations.text: Video-to-data engines still struggle with reconstruction noise and action error.
stated_limitations.quote: these data engines still face challenges in reducing reconstruction noise and acquiring minimal action errors.

stated_limitations.text: Generation scales faster than grounding and verification.
stated_limitations.quote: data generation scales faster than physical grounding, verification, and embodiment alignment.

stated_limitations.text: Benchmarks report overall success without diagnosing whether failures come from planning, memory, composition or recovery.
stated_limitations.quote: current benchmarks lack structured frameworks for assessing reasoning ability in VLA systems

failure_modes: Long-horizon chained instructions: CALVIN success drops sharply for five sequential instructions.
Multi-step logical tasks fail systematically (VLABench).
Performance degrades under combined perturbations (THE COLOSSEUM); single-axis robustness does not extrapolate.
Trajectory reuse (MimicGen family) assumes known subtask structure; visual augmentation cannot create new physics; LLM-driven generation remains simulation-bound.
Lab-based teleoperation limits scene diversity; hardware engines face calibration and embodiment constraints.
future_work: Reconstruct real scenes in simulation with high geometric and physical fidelity and generate trajectories there.
Build benchmarks on top of high-fidelity data engines so training and testing match deployment.
Integrate 3D sensing pipelines with robot platforms to build accurate scene models.
Unified engines combining physics constraints, temporally coherent reconstruction and embodiment-aware reasoning.
restrictive_assumptions: Video-to-data engines assume reliable hand pose, object mesh and 6D pose and depth reconstruction from video.
Trajectory-reuse generators assume known subtask structure.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Success drops to 0.08 percent for five sequential instructions, as cited by the survey.
Substantial degradation under combined perturbations (no number given).
Systematic failures reported (no number given).

open_problems_listed: Fidelity-cost trade-off in datasets; interface consistency vs scale.
Underrepresentation of force and tactile, contact-rich data.
Grounding semantics into physically valid closed-loop control.
Benchmarks that diagnose temporal and compositional reasoning, memory, and recovery.
Evaluation under compounded variability across perception, embodiment and semantics, and cross-embodiment transfer.
Grounding reliability of data engines: perception noise, physical plausibility, feasibility checks, calibration, reward specification.
Limited temporal context, compute cost and sim-to-real discrepancy of interactive world models.
Bridging the sim-to-real fidelity gap via high-fidelity real-scene reconstruction in simulation.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet turn human or robot video into physically valid, low-error action labels, because pose and depth reconstruction errors propagate into policies.

papers.title: Robots Need More than VLA and World Models
papers.problem_statement: Scaling VLAs is incomplete: the core bottleneck is the absence of mechanisms that convert abundant unstructured behaviour (human motion, video, simulation) into grounded robot supervision with actions, task semantics and rewards.

stated_limitations.text: Robot-native supervision does not scale because most real-world behaviour lacks robot action labels.
stated_limitations.quote: most of the physical behaviour available in the world does not arrive with explicit robot actions.

stated_limitations.text: Learning from passive video does not solve grounding; latent actions, progress signals and representations still miss contact dynamics and force constraints.
stated_limitations.quote: weak physical supervision does not remove the need for grounding; it relocates it.
stated_limitations.section: 2.2 Learning from Weakly Grounded Physical Observations

stated_limitations.text: Multimodal streams (video, mocap, tactile, logs) are asynchronous; aligning them to physical events is itself unsolved.
stated_limitations.quote: temporal alignment is not a preprocessing detail. It is, in fact, part of the embodied autolabelling problem.
stated_limitations.section: 3.1 Physical Data Engines and Embodied Autolabelling

stated_limitations.text: Inferring events, contacts and object states from episodes that carry only partial supervision is an open question.
stated_limitations.quote: when most episodes provide only partial supervision
stated_limitations.section: 3.1 Physical Data Engines and Embodied Autolabelling

stated_limitations.text: Pose-matching retargeting is insufficient; the effect on the object must be preserved.
stated_limitations.quote: This formulation makes clear why pose matching is insufficient.

stated_limitations.text: Object-centric world models depend on reliable perception and tracking; 3D representations struggle with contact and force.
stated_limitations.quote: Object-centric models expose entities and relations but require reliable perception and tracking.

stated_limitations.text: Without component-level credit assignment, deployment failures cannot be routed to the faulty component.
stated_limitations.quote: Otherwise, the system may know that a rollout failed but not what should change.

failure_modes: Purely learned predictors produce futures where objects interpenetrate, contacts occur without force, or rigid objects deform.
3D representations (point clouds, meshes, neural fields, Gaussian splats) may struggle with contact, force and material response.
Mechanics-based models are brittle when the environment is unknown or deformable.
future_work: Physical data engines performing embodied autolabelling: temporal alignment, event segmentation, object-state estimation, contact inference, phase recognition, latent actions, outcome prediction.
Wearable sensing suits as labelling instruments for contacts, task phases and object state changes.
Task-preserving retargeting that preserves contact and object-state transitions, not pose.
Hybrid physics-grounded world models combining 3D scene, object-centric structure, physics constraints and residual dynamics.
Task-conditioned reward grounding and self-improving deployment loops with component-level credit assignment.
restrictive_assumptions: Current robot learning assumes observations, actions, task labels, rewards and success metrics are specified in advance.
Object-centric world models assume reliable perception and tracking of objects.
open_problems_listed: Physical data engines and embodied autolabelling from heterogeneous, asynchronous, partially labelled episodes.
Temporal alignment of video, motion capture, tactile and robot logs to a common event timeline.
Joint inference of coupled labels: task phase, contact, object state, action and reward.
Task-preserving retargeting across embodiments (moving from pose to contact to object-state to intent preservation).
Choice of world-model representation for consequence prediction (pixel, object-centric, 3D, mechanics, hybrid).
Task-conditioned reward grounding distinguishing progress, failure, recovery and success.
Self-improving deployment loops with component-level credit assignment.
New evaluation questions: can a system infer contacts, object-state changes and task phases from human behaviour?
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet automatically infer aligned contact events, object-state changes and task phases from multimodal human demonstrations as robot-usable supervision.

papers.title: TULIP: Multi-camera 3D Precision Assessment of Parkinson's Disease
papers.problem_statement: PD symptom scoring (UPDRS) is coarse and subjective, and there are no benchmark video datasets; prior video work is single-camera, covers one or two activities, and 3D data needed markers.

stated_limitations.text: The cohort is small relative to the heterogeneity of PD.
stated_limitations.quote: our cohort is still relatively small, especially considering the hetereogeneity of PD.

stated_limitations.text: Low demographic diversity may limit generalisation.
stated_limitations.quote: TULIP also contains relatively little demographic diversity, which could hinder generalization to more representative patient populations.

stated_limitations.text: Baselines use only finger tapping and gait, not all 25 recorded activities.
stated_limitations.quote: our baseline TULIP analyses did not incorporate data from all of the activities we recorded.

stated_limitations.text: Capture used a large room unlike a typical clinical exam space.
stated_limitations.quote: TULIP was also collected in a large room that does not reflect the constraints of a typical clinical exam environment

stated_limitations.text: A deep pose-sequence classifier underperformed, attributed to small dataset size.
stated_limitations.quote: The poor performance of the ResNet50 pose sequence classifier could stem from the relatively small size of the TULIP dataset.

failure_modes: Models using 2D features performed poorly compared with 3D features for both finger tapping and gait.
All approaches performed worse on gait than on finger tapping, attributed to natural gait heterogeneity.
Gait PD/healthy classification was slightly worse than a previously published Random Forest approach.
Clinician agreement was very low on kinetic tremor (ICC 0.1 right hand, 0.4 left hand), limiting label reliability.
Keypoints can be occluded in specific viewpoints (Figure 5).
future_work: Adapt the paradigm and acquisition hardware to smaller clinical spaces.
Add more and more diverse subjects and activities closer to daily living.
Unsupervised analysis to find PD signatures independent of UPDRS.
Networks fit directly to 3D pose time series.
Extend to movement disorders beyond PD.
restrictive_assumptions: Six synchronised (GPIO-triggered), calibrated cameras at 80 fps in a 6.3 x 3 m hexagonal capture space.
Intrinsics and extrinsics fit before and after each session.
Off-the-shelf MediaPipe and MMPose without fine-tuning, triangulated by DLT with outlier interpolation and smoothing.
Hand-crafted features and small-sample leave-one-subject-out evaluation.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Best model (MLP, 3D features) reached 0.69 F1, commensurate only with the least accurate clinician rater.
Best model (Random Forest, 3D features) reached 0.72 F1; 2D features underperformed.
21 mm for finger tapping and 56 mm for gait (reprojection 22 and 16 px).
Kinetic tremor right hand ICC 0.1 and left hand 0.4.

open_problems_listed: Small cohort relative to PD heterogeneity.
Low demographic diversity.
Baselines covering only two of 25 activities.
Recording in a large room rather than a typical clinical space; need for hardware adapted to small rooms.
Need for activities aligned with daily living and for unsupervised PD signatures beyond UPDRS.
Inter-rater variability of UPDRS component scores.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet obtain precise markerless 3D hand and body kinematics in compact clinical rooms without a large multi-camera calibrated capture space.

papers.title: Care-PD: A Multi-Site Anonymized Clinical Dataset for Parkinson's Disease Gait Assessment
papers.problem_statement: Objective PD gait assessment is limited by the absence of large, diverse, clinically annotated motion datasets; existing ones are small, single-site, unstandardised, and models perform poorly under real-world variability.

stated_limitations.text: Severe gait impairment (UPDRS-gait 3) is underrepresented.
stated_limitations.quote: the dataset remains imbalanced with respect to severe gait impairment (UPDRS-gait score 3), which is both clinically rare and difficult to capture due to mobility constraints.

stated_limitations.text: Monocular RGB mesh recovery (WHAM) adds depth and distal-joint error.
stated_limitations.quote: monocular errors in depth and distal-joint estimation may still affect downstream tasks.

stated_limitations.text: Mixing UPDRS and MDS-UPDRS rubrics and per-session labels adds label noise.
stated_limitations.quote: introduce additional label variability

stated_limitations.text: No outdoor or in-home data.
stated_limitations.quote: all data are recorded in clinical corridors or labs; outdoor and in-home walking are absent.

stated_limitations.text: Fine-grained symptom estimation is not addressed.
stated_limitations.quote: more fine-grained symptom estimation (e.g., stride irregularity, freezing episodes) is left for future work.

stated_limitations.text: Mostly short single-task walks; little multi-visit temporal context.
stated_limitations.quote: Most datasets in Care-PD consist of single-task, short-segment gait walks

stated_limitations.text: Encoders collapse under cross-site distribution shift.
stated_limitations.quote: their accuracy collapses under distribution shifts

failure_modes: Cross-dataset transfer reduces F1 by 0.2 to 0.4 due to distribution shift.
Scarcity of severe (class 3) samples is a major failure mode in cross-site tests.
Zero-shot models pretrained on generic motion (H3.6M) over-predict class 0 and fail on severe classes.
Performance drops on smaller cohorts (T-SDU-PD) and further on 3DGait.
Handcrafted gait features underperform in most cross-dataset settings.
Ceiling-mounted cameras skew recovered 3D walks, needing slope correction.
future_work: Domain-aware training and test-time adaptation to avoid site-specific bias.
Generative or semi-synthetic augmentation to balance severe cases.
Add IMU and other wearable modalities.
Richer labels: stride-level events, patient-reported outcomes.
Longitudinal temporal modelling using the longitudinal cohorts.
Identity-preserving photorealistic video synthesis for end-to-end video-to-clinic benchmarking.
restrictive_assumptions: Only textureless SMPL meshes are released; no video frames, so video-based methods cannot be benchmarked end-to-end.
RGB cohorts depend on monocular WHAM mesh recovery and manual verification of the target person.
Only clean walking segments retained; non-walking behaviour removed.
Lab or clinical corridor recording only.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Transfer to unseen datasets typically reduces F1 by 0.2 to 0.4; best in-site up to 0.73 on PD-GaM.
Zero-shot MotionAGFormer 60.7 mm vs 7.5 mm after Care-PD fine-tuning; MoMask 22.5 mm vs 8.7 mm.
Mean 39 mm error for monocular WHAM meshes.
Including class 3 lowers scores by 5 to 10 pp for models trained on cohorts without class 3.

open_problems_listed: Imbalance and scarcity of severe gait impairment (UPDRS-gait 3).
Noise from monocular RGB reconstruction (depth and distal joints).
Lack of wearable sensor modalities.
Label variability from UPDRS vs MDS-UPDRS rubrics and per-session labels; high inter-rater variability of gait score.
Absence of outdoor and in-home walking.
Fine-grained symptom estimation (stride irregularity, freezing episodes).
Temporal context across visits and activities; most data are short single-task walks.
Cross-site generalisation and domain adaptation.
Demographic imbalance (underrepresentation of women in severe FoG cohorts).
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet produce clinical motion models that generalise across sites and capture setups, especially for rare severe cases, from monocular reconstructions.

papers.title: Markerless Motion Capture in Routine Clinical Upper Limb Assessments: Validity and Insights Beyond Ordinal Scoring
papers.problem_statement: ARAT ordinal scoring is subjective, insensitive (floor and ceiling effects) and non-specific; marker-based mocap is incompatible with clinical routine, and whether markerless kinematics from routine sessions are valid and informative is untested.

stated_limitations.text: Longitudinal evidence comes from two case studies only.
stated_limitations.quote: The longitudinal evidence rests on two case studies, motivating but not establishing the coupled finding at the cohort level

stated_limitations.text: The minimal clinically important difference is borrowed, not estimated for this measure.
stated_limitations.quote: The MCID adopted here is an approximation translated from consensus recommendations

stated_limitations.text: No inter-rater reliability data for the ARAT reference scores.
stated_limitations.quote: ARAT scores were also assigned by treating therapists without parallel inter-rater reliability data

stated_limitations.text: Hand-crafted metrics assigned to one domain across all tasks break down for some tasks (e.g. Water Pouring).
stated_limitations.quote: This is not an accuracy limitation but a representational one

stated_limitations.text: The three-camera clinical setup lacks reliable finger kinematics and has more occlusion than a five-camera lab setup.
stated_limitations.quote: returning to a five-camera configuration, as used in laboratory validation, would support reliable finger kinematics and reduce occlusion-driven artefacts

failure_modes: Reprojection error 12.5 px, above the 5-10 px laboratory standard, attributed to three cameras and more frequent occlusion in clinic.
Score 0 trials showed slightly higher reprojection error (13.9 px median).
Water Pouring had the lowest Tier 1 discrimination (AUC 0.75) because the domain assignment did not fit the task.
Grip task lacked finger kinematics, causing longitudinal mismatch for patient P10.
Discrimination attenuated at the subjective Score 2 vs 3 boundary (AUC 0.70-0.84).
future_work: Prospective cohort study with structured assessment schedules.
Estimate movement-specific MCID and reliability bounds in a larger cohort.
Score movement by deviation from an able-bodied reference rather than pre-chosen scalars.
Feed full biomechanical trajectories to movement foundation models.
Five-camera setup for finger kinematics, or single-camera reconstruction for lower deployment barrier.
restrictive_assumptions: Three synchronised calibrated webcams (1280x720, 60 Hz) placed around the assessment table.
Therapist marks trial start and stop on a tablet in real time.
Upper-limb body kinematics only; no reliable finger or object tracking.
Score 3 used as a proxy for normal motor performance instead of measured able-bodied references.

benchmark_gaps.observation: 12.5 +/- 3.0 px, above the 5-10 px lab standard.
0.70-0.84; compensation-only AUC 0.59-0.68.
0.75, the lowest of seven task groups.

open_problems_listed: Cohort-level longitudinal validation (only two case studies).
Measure-specific MCID and reliability bounds.
Quantifying clinician subjectivity in reference scores.
Task-specific domain assignment of kinematic metrics.
Population-scale able-bodied and patient reference data.
Finger kinematics and occlusion in clinical camera setups.
papers.field_cannot_yet: The field cannot yet capture reliable finger and hand-object kinematics during routine clinical grasp tasks with a minimal, ad-hoc camera setup.

papers.title: Monocular Markerless Motion Capture Enables Quantitative Assessment of Upper Extremity Reachable Workspace
papers.problem_statement: Marker-based and multi-camera markerless systems are hard to deploy routinely; monocular markerless capture with biomechanical modelling has not been validated on specific clinical assessments beyond gait.

stated_limitations.text: Cohort of healthy adults only; validity in patients unknown.
stated_limitations.quote: the generalization of these findings is limited by the homogeneity of the study cohort, which consisted entirely of healthy adults.

stated_limitations.text: Analysis was offline, post-hoc.
stated_limitations.quote: the current analysis was conducted post-hoc, which limits its immediate utility at the point of care.

stated_limitations.text: Large per-octant errors, especially contralateral.
stated_limitations.quote: average percent errors reached as high as 15.45% (Frontal) and 50.21% (Offset) in contralateral octants.

stated_limitations.text: Not precise enough for individual superior or contralateral octants.
stated_limitations.quote: it lacks the consistency required for precise measurement of specific superior or contralateral octants.

stated_limitations.text: Monocular depth ambiguity along the optical axis is unresolved.
stated_limitations.quote: struggles to resolve depth ambiguity in the absence of binocular or multi-view parity.

failure_modes: Posterior octants: depth ambiguity produced elevated anterior-posterior errors for the frontal camera.
Offset camera: ML errors in contralateral octants; under 40% agreement in the superior-anterior contralateral octant.
Cross-body reaches where the torso or reaching arm occludes the hand and wrist force the model to infer distal joints.
Movements parallel to the optical axis cause foreshortening and low signal-to-noise in 2D keypoints.
Systematic keypoint localisation biases shift peak reach distance.
future_work: Validate in clinical populations (stroke, brachial plexus palsy).
Real-time feedback and mobile platforms for point-of-care and home use.
Address spatial and algorithmic limitations in posterior and contralateral workspace.
restrictive_assumptions: Static camera with known calibrated intrinsics.
Healthy adults, nine participants, VR-headset-displayed targets.
Offline GPU optimisation of a MuJoCo biomechanical model per trial.
Post-hoc alignment of MMC coordinates to the marker-based system.

benchmark_gaps.observation: Up to 15.45% (frontal) and 50.21% (offset) in contralateral octants.
Offset camera under 40% agreement in the superior-anterior contralateral octant.

open_problems_listed: Validation in patients with atypical kinematics (tremor, compensatory trunk motion).
Real-time point-of-care processing.
Monocular depth ambiguity and self-occlusion in posterior and contralateral workspace.

papers.title: Muscles in Time: Learning to Understand Human Motion by Simulating Muscle Activations

stated_limitations.text: Object-related motions such as lifting and throwing assume negligible object mass because mass is unknown.
stated_limitations.quote: Since we miss information about object mass, we assume interaction with very small, lightweight objects of negligible weight in these cases.

stated_limitations.text: Ethnicity and some body-weight types are under-represented.

stated_limitations.text: Simulation is computationally heavy and fails on some segments, so released data contains gaps; longer sequences are more prone to gaps.

Activation analysis is unstable at sequence start and end (first and last 0.14 s cut).
Predicted activations slightly underestimate activation peaks (qualitative results).

Validate MinT-based models and analyses against real-world experiments.

Restricted to AMASS subsets EyesJapan, BMLrub, KIT, BMLmovi, TotalCapture

papers.title: InterCap: Joint Markerless 3D Tracking of Humans and Objects in Interaction from Multi-view RGB-D Images

stated_limitations.quote: for small objects, like a bottle or a cup, it struggles significantly due to occlusion.

stated_limitations.text: Residual jitter remains, from detector sensitivity to occlusion and illumination and from small inter-camera delays of Azure Kinects; it is worse for hands.

2D keypoint detection (OpenPose) fails when objects occlude the body or hands interact with them.

Spurious contact detected on the back of the hand.

Advanced motion priors to reduce jitter
Interactions with smaller objects and dexterous manipulation

Subject interacts with a single object

Offline whole-sequence optimization
Single body shape per sequence
Pseudo ground truth only; no independent mocap ground truth for evaluation
